styles.visual_cues: Use a column grid, baseline alignment, repeated spacing, asymmetric composition, and generous negative space. Set left-aligned sans-serif type with clear size hierarchy; use black and white with restrained accent colors and grid-aligned photography. Animate along layout axes and settle elements on shared alignment points without disrupting reading order.
styles.note: A supplemental design reference; not claimed as a directly named style in the source collection.

tech.implementation: Build typography with CSS Grid and loaded fonts. Align SVG geometry to the baseline grid; animate position, scale, and cropping.
tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
framework_selection.scope: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

tech.library_selection: Choose libraries by role and scene requirements; the available options are not a required bundle. Prefer existing suitable dependencies. Use one owner for each animated property. Preserve HyperFrames as the primary video framework and Remotion as the conditional fallback. For video, drive all state from seekable composition time; live hover, scroll, and pointer behavior belongs only to interactive delivery. Select visual and motion technologies from the style, action, assets, and required fidelity before choosing the composition and export pipeline. Pipeline availability must not determine or simplify the visual style or motion technique. Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

motion_guidance.application: Apply shared movement quality to International Typographic Style (Swiss Style) without weakening its visual_cues, materials, typography or existing motion_references.
motion_guidance.cadence_guidance: Use smooth, coherent authored movement where the action benefits from it. Preserve deliberate sharp cuts, impacts, constant-speed sections and reading holds; not every transition needs easing.
motion_guidance.implementation: Prefer existing timeline and renderer dependencies. Evaluate key states at requested composition time, maintain a single property owner, and cache or deterministically replay stateful motion. Do not introduce a library solely to add generic smoothing.

style_renderer.selection_basis: Use visual_cues and tech.implementation for styles, or the selected style and this pattern implementation for motion recipes. Select by visual fidelity and medium, not pipeline availability.

motion_engine.selection_basis: Use the authored action, style cadence, trajectory, material behavior, and simulation requirements. Select one owner for each animated property.

styles.executable_prompt_template:
Replace all double-brace placeholders with task inputs before execution. Use documented defaults only for omitted optional inputs and state the assumptions.
Create a International Typographic Style (Swiss Style) video about {{subject}} for {{audience_and_objective}}. Use {{assets_and_exact_copy}}. Deliver a video of {{duration_seconds}} seconds, with aspect ratio {{aspect_ratio}}, resolution {{resolution}}, and frame rate {{frame_rate}}. Follow {{audio_or_rhythm_requirements}} and save deliverables to {{output_directory}}.
Use {{render_pipeline}} for composition and export only. If omitted, resolve it to tech.framework_selection.default. 1. Inspect the project, available tools, assets, exact wording, and input formats. Reuse suitable existing components. Treat visual_cues as art-direction constraints and choose only the tech.recommended_stack entries needed for the selected framework and asset-generation method. Example dimensions, palette sizes, beats, and scenes apply only when the task adopts them.
2. Write a short storyboard with explicit time ranges. Give each section one main idea, a clear focal point, and enough reading or observation time. Plan staging around this style's visual rules: Use a column grid, baseline alignment, repeated spacing, asymmetric composition, and generous negative space. Set left-aligned sans-serif type with clear size hierarchy; use black and white with restrained accent colors and grid-aligned photography. Animate along layout axes and settle elements on shared alignment points without disrupting reading order. Add secondary styles only when their materials, composition, and movement remain compatible.
3. Implement the style-specific technique: Build typography with CSS Grid and loaded fonts. Align SVG geometry to the baseline grid; animate position, scale, and cropping. Keep Canvas, DOM, and WebGL in the browser and file processing in Node.js or Python. Drive visual updates from shared, seekable video time; load fonts and assets, seed randomness, and cache stateful simulation. Centralize colors, fonts, dimensions, camera settings, and timing. Build representative frames and key actions before expanding the sequence.
4. Follow only the tech.render_pipeline route for {{render_pipeline}}. Distinguish drawing or pose-exposure rate from delivery frame rate. Use task-provided or authorized audio, and synchronize picture and sound against the same time data. Match composition and velocity at loop boundaries.
5. Render and inspect actual opening, key-action, transition, and closing frames, then watch the decoded video. Check the style-specific constraints in visual_cues, readable text, correct glyphs, stable materials and outlines, missing assets, crop margins, timing, dimensions, and audio synchronization. Fix issues and rerender until the relevant checks pass; compilation alone is insufficient.
6. Deliver the video, editable source or project, a key-frame contact sheet, chosen parameters, and reproducible render instructions. State any missing assets or unverified limitations. Distinguish photographed production from simulated appearance.
Framework contract: select the packages, runtime, timeline registration, validation commands, and renderer that actually belong to {{render_pipeline}}. Do not mix another framework's hooks, composition lifecycle, or renderer. Specialist modeling, photography, drawing, and scientific computation can produce inputs for the selected video framework without being replaced by it.
Palette contract: read palette before implementation. Use its suggested tokens only when task, brand, or reference colors are absent. Keep supplied exact colors, source artwork, existing semantic assignments, and style color-family and color-count constraints unchanged. Use chroma-js to validate and normalize equivalent color values, select readable existing foreground/background pairs, and interpolate only when palette.gradient is enabled. Do not recolor assets or add hues to improve contrast; change text placement, an existing backing color, or typography instead. Follow palette.agent_instruction and inspect actual composited frames.
Shared movement quality: follow shared_motion_guidance and tech.motion_guidance. Design coherent trajectories, acceleration, transitions and settling with readable holds. Use time-based interpolation and authored easing when appropriate; preserve deliberate cuts, impacts, stepped exposure, whole-pixel placement and line-boil cadence. Do not automatically add springs, bounce, floating or extra in-between poses. Derive state from composition time; bake or deterministically replay any stateful smoothing, physics or camera damping. Verify direct, backward and out-of-order seeks plus the decoded sequence and loop seams. Keep the existing palette and style-specific motion direction intact.
Production ownership: follow production_policy. Choose the style_renderer and motion_engine from the style and motion requirements first, and state the selected tools and their responsibilities. Build the visuals and movement with those tools according to tech.implementation and visual_cues. Use {{render_pipeline}} only for scene assembly, seekable composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and export. Keep specialist rendering and motion logic in their own layers; do not substitute generic framework text, DOM transitions, or framework animation helpers merely because the pipeline is available. Native DOM or SVG is appropriate when it actually satisfies the style. Integrate deterministic time-driven layers or baked assets, and verify representative visuals and motion before assembling the full video.
Audio direction: follow audio_direction. Based on {{subject}}, {{audience_and_objective}}, the storyboard, visual_cues, and motion direction, suggest suitable background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or silence. Honor {{audio_or_rhythm_requirements}} first. State the proposed choices and why they fit this topic and style; suggest mood, texture, energy, tempo where useful, voice language and delivery where useful, and scene-level audio changes. Do not impose a fixed soundtrack rule or include every layer. Source or create authorized assets, then use {{render_pipeline}} for assembly, synchronization, mixing, and export. Verify speech intelligibility, audio balance, absence of clipping, and picture synchronization in the final video.

motion_references.selection_policy: Optional candidates are screened for natural style compatibility. Before selection, inspect the actual scene illustration, assets, geometry and narrative beat. Keep only references whose defining action is supported by that scene. Choosing no reference is valid. Do not infer motion from a similar label; do not replace the existing style motion direction.

candidates.usage_guidance: Consider a fixed hero stage whose internal composition separates, expands, and shifts from centered to peripheral copy without a cut. Adapt the example objects to the topic. Pin the stage rather than freezing every internal subject.

Consider a progress-controlled handoff between outgoing and incoming chapters with synchronized copy and readable endpoints. Choose one compatible transition treatment and make both forward and backward state evaluation coherent.

Consider a horizontal card track that moves with swipe or drag and settles at a defined snap selection. Preserve readable cards, accessible navigation, and one track-position owner; author the track directly for video.

Consider meaningful narrative steps with synchronized copy and visual states, plus optional within-step progress or sticky graphics. Use only scene-level motions that serve the story, and schedule the same states by time for video.

A printed full stop can provide one axis-aligned shared-element crop. Optional only when actual scene assets support the defining action; preserve the style palette and medium and choose no reference when unsuitable.

motion_references.agent_instruction: Read the actual illustration and complete pattern description, motion_sequence and video_adaptation. Identify which scene elements implement that action. Reject unsupported geometry, absent subjects, unintended depth, broken contact points or unrelated interactions. Select none when no candidate fits; use restrained style-native motion instead. Preserve authored transforms, fixed backgrounds and reading layers.

audio_direction.prompt: Based on the topic, audience, objective, narrative, and the visual and motion characteristics of International Typographic Style (Swiss Style), suggest an appropriate audio direction. Consider background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or intentional silence. Explain which choices support this particular video; do not assign a fixed genre, tempo, instrument, voice, or mandatory audio layer to the style.
suggestion_dimensions: Whether background music is useful, and its suggested mood, texture, energy, tempo range, and progression.
Whether voiceover helps explain the topic, and its suggested language, tone, pace, and placement.
Whether sung vocals support the topic or distract from narration and essential text.
Whether sound effects, ambience, or silence clarify key actions, transitions, and reading holds.
How audio changes across scenes, supports motion cadence, and leaves space for speech and comprehension.
audio_direction.selection_guidance: Treat these as task-specific suggestions, not requirements to include every audio layer. Honor explicit user audio choices and supplied assets. When inputs are absent, propose a coherent direction and state assumptions; do not silently default to instrumental music or invent available audio assets.
audio_direction.integration_guidance: Select or create authorized audio assets separately from visual construction and motion design. Use render_pipeline to assemble, synchronize, mix, and export audio with picture. Keep speech intelligible, avoid clipping and competing vocals, and inspect the delivered audio and picture together.

suggested_combinations.selection_guidance: Use Swiss Style alone for posters, identity and typographic statements where grid and type carry everything. Choose a hybrid only when data must be explained or headlines must perform, and keep the black, white and single red accent untouched.

supporting_styles.role: Diagram and chart layer drawn inside the column grid

suggestions.rationale: Swiss grids and baseline alignment give data storytelling a rigorous, readable frame, and both share HTML/CSS-SVG renderers. The supporting style supplies variable, unit and causal sequencing discipline only.
suggestions.best_for: Annual reports, research summaries and explainer segments with a few verified figures.
suggestions.video_application: Charts build along grid axes in reading order, with red reserved for the one series or value under discussion and holds after each conclusion.
suggestions.html_application: Responsive CSS Grid page with SVG charts that reflow by column count, keyboard-focusable data points with text equivalents, and prefers-reduced-motion disabling axis slides.
consistency_rules: Charts use only #000000, #FFFFFF and #D32F2F; extra categories use line weight or pattern, not new hues.
All labels flush-left sans-serif on the shared baseline grid.
Motion travels only horizontally or vertically and settles on grid lines.
avoid: Multi-hue categorical palettes imported from the data style
Decorative chart animation without a stated value

supporting_styles.role: Headline and statement motion

suggestions.rationale: Kinetic typography lets the Swiss type hierarchy narrate directly, while the grid constrains where words may travel. Both use HTML/CSS with measured fonts.
suggestions.best_for: Title sequences, manifesto videos and brand statements built entirely from type.
suggestions.video_application: Words slide, crop and scale along column edges into a settled asymmetric layout; red marks one keyword per scene.
suggestions.html_application: Hero headlines animate into place on load or scroll with real DOM text, remain selectable, and render as the final static layout under reduced motion.
consistency_rules: One sans-serif family with weight and size steps only.
No springs or overshoot; linear-to-ease-out settling on alignment points.
Reading order never changes mid-animation.
avoid: Red used on more than one element per frame

tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

sources.style_evidence: Forceful diagonal crimson band, radial wedges, and a restricted red/black/off-white palette with bold type set on the slash, as in seconds 6–8.
sources.palette_lesson: The author's example palette is a grainy near-black ground, warm off-white type and one saturated crimson accent. Red builds up in stages: first a separator dot, then low-value radial rays, then a full-width flat band, and finally a stamp badge. What defines the style is not the black or the specific red. It is three things: a single dominant dark or neutral ground, one high-chroma signal color kept for punctuation and the hero band, and type with the strongest value contrast. The background never competes, because the sunburst rays sit close to the ground's value. Type that sits on the accent band stays the paper/off-white tone, so the band reads as a backing plate rather than as the canvas. For new subjects, change the ground and the accent while keeping these roles: for example, a deep indigo/ink-navy ground with a signal-orange band, a cold slate/graphite ground with an acid-yellow band, a deep forest or bottle-green ground with a vermilion band, or an inverted light warm-gray paper ground with black type and a cobalt band. Keep one accent hue, keep the rays within roughly 10–15% of the ground's value, and check the contrast of off-white type on the band.

Specialist modeling, photography, drawing, and scientific computation can produce inputs for the selected video framework without being replaced by it.
Palette contract: read palette before implementation. Use its suggested tokens only when task, brand, or reference colors are absent. Keep supplied exact colors, source artwork, existing semantic assignments, and style color-family and color-count constraints unchanged. Use chroma-js to validate and normalize equivalent color values, select readable existing foreground/background pairs, and interpolate only when palette.gradient is enabled. Shared movement quality: follow shared_motion_guidance and tech.motion_guidance. Design coherent trajectories, acceleration, transitions and settling with readable holds. Use time-based interpolation and authored easing when appropriate; preserve deliberate cuts, impacts, stepped exposure, whole-pixel placement and line-boil cadence. Do not automatically add springs, bounce, floating or extra in-between poses. Derive state from composition time; bake or deterministically replay any stateful smoothing, physics or camera damping. Verify direct, backward and out-of-order seeks plus the decoded sequence and loop seams. Keep the existing palette and style-specific motion direction intact.
Production ownership: follow production_policy. Choose the style_renderer and motion_engine from the style and motion requirements first, and state the selected tools and their responsibilities. Build the visuals and movement with those tools according to tech.implementation and visual_cues. Use {{render_pipeline}} only for scene assembly, seekable composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and export. Keep specialist rendering and motion logic in their own layers; do not substitute generic framework text, DOM transitions, or framework animation helpers merely because the pipeline is available. Native DOM or SVG is appropriate when it actually satisfies the style. Integrate deterministic time-driven layers or baked assets, and verify representative visuals and motion before assembling the full video.

Based on {{subject}}, {{audience_and_objective}}, the storyboard, visual_cues, and motion direction, suggest suitable background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or silence. 1. Inspect the project, available tools, assets, exact wording, and input formats. Reuse suitable existing components. Treat visual_cues as art-direction constraints and choose only the tech.recommended_stack entries needed for the selected framework and asset-generation method. Example dimensions, palette sizes, beats, and scenes apply only when the task adopts them.
2. Write a short storyboard with explicit time ranges. Give each section one main idea, a clear focal point, and enough reading or observation time. Plan staging around this style's visual rules: Combine dots, zigzags, stripes, circles, and irregular geometry with bold contrasting colors. Keep the headline readable and use patterns to establish rhythm. Alternate shapes, elastic offsets, and pattern handoffs while limiting simultaneous movement and avoiding rapid full-frame flashing. Add secondary styles only when their materials, composition, and movement remain compatible.
3. Implement the style-specific technique: Build SVG patterns and reusable shape groups. Stagger selected movements and elastic accents instead of animating every pattern at once. Keep Canvas, DOM, and WebGL in the browser and file processing in Node.js or Python. Drive visual updates from shared, seekable video time; load fonts and assets, seed randomness, and cache stateful simulation. Centralize colors, fonts, dimensions, camera settings, and timing. Build representative frames and key actions before expanding the sequence.
4. Follow only the tech.render_pipeline route for {{render_pipeline}}. Distinguish drawing or pose-exposure rate from delivery frame rate. Use task-provided or authorized audio, and synchronize picture and sound against the same time data. Match composition and velocity at loop boundaries.
5. Render and inspect actual opening, key-action, transition, and closing frames, then watch the decoded video. Check the style-specific constraints in visual_cues, readable text, correct glyphs, stable materials and outlines, missing assets, crop margins, timing, dimensions, and audio synchronization. Fix issues and rerender until the relevant checks pass; compilation alone is insufficient.
6. Deliver the video, editable source or project, a key-frame contact sheet, chosen parameters, and reproducible render instructions. State any missing assets or unverified limitations. Distinguish photographed production from simulated appearance.
Framework contract: select the packages, runtime, timeline registration, validation commands, and renderer that actually belong to {{render_pipeline}}. Do not mix another framework's hooks, composition lifecycle, or renderer. Specialist modeling, photography, drawing, and scientific computation can produce inputs for the selected video framework without being replaced by it.
Palette contract: read palette before implementation. Use its suggested tokens only when task, brand, or reference colors are absent. Keep supplied exact colors, source artwork, existing semantic assignments, and style color-family and color-count constraints unchanged. Use chroma-js to validate and normalize equivalent color values, select readable existing foreground/background pairs, and interpolate only when palette.gradient is enabled. Do not recolor assets or add hues to improve contrast; change text placement, an existing backing color, or typography instead. Follow palette.agent_instruction and inspect actual composited frames.
Optional mo.js effects: consult the @mojs/core entry in tech.recommended_stack when shape, burst, swirl or HTML effects support the scene. Follow its style_application, integration_guidance, determinism_guidance and color_guidance. Preserve the resolved palette and reading holds. Build effects once, pause independent playback, and drive progress from shared composition time; verify direct, repeated, backward and out-of-order seeks. Keep one owner per animated property and preserve the selected video framework lifecycle. Do not use live click triggers or regeneration during video export. Use the existing GSAP/SVG route if an effect cannot satisfy deterministic seeking.
Shared movement quality: follow shared_motion_guidance and tech.motion_guidance. Design coherent trajectories, acceleration, transitions and settling with readable holds. Use time-based interpolation and authored easing when appropriate; preserve deliberate cuts, impacts, stepped exposure, whole-pixel placement and line-boil cadence. Do not automatically add springs, bounce, floating or extra in-between poses. Derive state from composition time; bake or deterministically replay any stateful smoothing, physics or camera damping. Verify direct, backward and out-of-order seeks plus the decoded sequence and loop seams. Keep the existing palette and style-specific motion direction intact.
Production ownership: follow production_policy. Choose the style_renderer and motion_engine from the style and motion requirements first, and state the selected tools and their responsibilities. Build the visuals and movement with those tools according to tech.implementation and visual_cues. Use {{render_pipeline}} only for scene assembly, seekable composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and export. Keep specialist rendering and motion logic in their own layers; do not substitute generic framework text, DOM transitions, or framework animation helpers merely because the pipeline is available. Native DOM or SVG is appropriate when it actually satisfies the style. Integrate deterministic time-driven layers or baked assets, and verify representative visuals and motion before assembling the full video.
Audio direction: follow audio_direction. Based on {{subject}}, {{audience_and_objective}}, the storyboard, visual_cues, and motion direction, suggest suitable background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or silence. Honor {{audio_or_rhythm_requirements}} first. State the proposed choices and why they fit this topic and style; suggest mood, texture, energy, tempo where useful, voice language and delivery where useful, and scene-level audio changes. Do not impose a fixed soundtrack rule or include every layer. Source or create authorized assets, then use {{render_pipeline}} for assembly, synchronization, mixing, and export. sources.style_evidence: Seconds 4–6: scattered zigzags, squiggles, outline rings, triangles, x-crosses and dots in bold contrasting colors as a rhythmic confetti layer.
sources.palette_lesson: The background changes on purpose with each life stage, and that is the main lesson. The opening is near-black navy for an abstract, pre-life pulse. Childhood uses naturalistic sky-teal, pale green and green with a warm yellow sun. Adolescence uses a saturated indigo-to-magenta gradient with a striped warm sun and neon cyan, yellow and orange confetti. Adulthood uses desaturated stepped greys with only small red and brown accents. These specific hues are this author's choices for this story, not rules of the style. What defines the style: each scene has a coherent flat palette of about 3–6 families; a thin white line/HUD layer stays readable on every background; a small warm accent (red heart, red tie, red ball) carries over between scenes; and saturation and value shifts are used as storytelling, not decoration. For new subjects, choose the field from the emotion of each chapter. Options include deep teal night ocean, dusty terracotta desert at dusk, cold blue-white winter morning, lime-and-mint spring, warm amber interior lamplight, slate-blue rain, and black-and-violet club space. Then check that the white line and HUD keep enough contrast; on very light fields, switch the line to dark ink.

sources.style_evidence: The backgrounds rotate through bold flat fields with stripes, dot grids and concentric rings, using contrasting candy colors (yellow/pink/cyan, mint, violet, indigo). Pattern handoffs happen at each cut.
sources.palette_lesson: These colors are the creator's choices for this short, not a fixed recipe. Each scene uses one saturated, nearly flat background family (golden-yellow stripes, deep indigo, slate blue with a screenshot collage, mint, periwinkle, a yellow/pink/cyan wipe) and changes family at every hard cut to mark a new idea. The parts that stay constant are what define the style: a pastel mascot with a black contour, caption type in white or yellow fill with a near-black stroke, a white outer keyline and a hard offset shadow, plus small multicolor confetti. The heavy dark stroke plus white halo is what keeps captions legible on any field, light or dark. For new subjects, choose the background from the topic and mood. Options include: deep teal or ink navy for tech or night topics, coral or tomato red for urgency, a soft lilac or sky-blue dot grid for calm explainers, charcoal with a neon-lime ring pulse for gaming, warm terracotta or olive for food or lifestyle, or a desaturated photo or screenshot wall as evidence. Keep one dominant field per scene with a quieter same-hue pattern (dots, stripes or rings at low contrast), and reserve the most saturated accent (yellow or hot pink here) for the key word. Recheck contrast between the mascot's pastel fill and the field: pale lilac on mint or butter yellow relies entirely on the black contour.

tech.implementation: Prepare color separations, comic contours, and repeated panels. Generate stable halftones in Canvas while keeping SVG or HTML text crisp.
tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
framework_selection.scope: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

Use one owner for each animated property. Preserve HyperFrames as the primary video framework and Remotion as the conditional fallback. For video, drive all state from seekable composition time; live hover, scroll, and pointer behavior belongs only to interactive delivery. Select visual and motion technologies from the style, action, assets, and required fidelity before choosing the composition and export pipeline. Pipeline availability must not determine or simplify the visual style or motion technique. Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. sources.palette_lesson:
The magenta/violet title ground and the yellow/blue-dot info ground are this author's example choices, not the style. The style's constraints are:
- a two-tone diagonal-stripe field combined with a corner-weighted halftone screen in a contrasting ink
- hard dark outlines and offset shadows
- a rotating set of 4–5 saturated flat card fills plus one cream/paper neutral card
- type colored to contrast with its own card fill
- lime/yellow tape or ticker accents
The ground hue pair changes per scene, which shows the system is scene-dependent. For new subjects, choose the ground pair from the subject's mood and keep the card set readable against it. Recheck that no card fill matches the ground (for example, avoid a yellow card on a yellow ground). Dark outlines and shadows must stay visible on darker grounds; switch to light outlines if needed.

sources.style_evidence: The 3s scene uses a saturated flat field, burst lines, halftone and ink splats behind a heavy black letter.

Pair it with a dark ink and a light ground chosen for the scene, such as cool gray concrete, newsprint gray, slate, or a cream tone only where it fits. Keep high contrast between letter and ground in every scene, and recheck it on textured or fluid backgrounds.

sources.palette_lesson: The warm peach, apricot and gold sky, the amber sea and the later rose-to-mauve dusk grade come from this author's chosen golden-hour subject. They are not a style rule. The lesson the style needs is the lighting structure: one strong motivated key light (here the low sun behind the subject), atmospheric haze that tints the whole background, and a darker silhouetted midground (pier, posts, lamp) for contrast. Small saturated accents tie into that key light, like the orange beak and legs and the life ring. The grade shifts between shots (warm gold in the wide shot, cooler lavender in the close-up), so the palette can move with the camera while the light direction stays the same. No letterbox or UI is present; the frames are the full composition.

sources.style_evidence: The title is ransom-note lettering: each letter is on its own paper chip in a mismatched typeface and color, set in an irregular, deliberately imperfect layout, with chips pasted on one by one (s1–s4).
sources.palette_lesson: The warm tan cork, brown wood frame and dark slate-navy room are this author's scene choices for a 'nerdy desk at night' story. They are not rules of the medium. What makes the style is how roles are split. The ground is one muted, textured surface. Saturated color comes from the letter chips, which mix roughly six families (cream, black, red, yellow, green, pink/sky blue) so that each letter contrasts with the ground. A single emissive accent (green CRT phosphor) carries the night scene, and the warm skin and red-tie figure stand out against the cool wall. For a new subject, choose the ground for the setting and keep the chips high-contrast against it. If the ground is dark, use more pale and saturated chips. If it is pale, use more black and saturated chips. Recheck legibility when chips overlap the pinned notes.

sources.style_evidence: Ransom-note cutout headline letters on mixed black, white and pink tiles, torn paper edges, a deliberately irregular pasted layout, and a limited palette of pink, black and white with one blue accent (s1-s4).
sources.palette_lesson: The grid stays in every frame and the accent roles stay fixed: one hot accent (magenta) is used as backing paper, halftone and stamp ink; black and white carry type and characters; cobalt blue and mustard yellow appear only rarely as third accents (one tile, one scrap, the blob's offset rim, the smiley). Scenes alternate between loud and quiet. Headline beats flood the frame with pink, and dialogue beats drop back to the plain grid so the bubbles can be read. The specific colours (sage graph paper, hot pink) belong to this author's example. They are not style constants. What defines the style is a light ruled/grid substrate, black-and-white cutout and pixel figures, one saturated print-ink accent, and white sticker borders that separate figures from any background.

styles.visual_cues: Organize headlines, short body copy, images, and annotations with the reading logic of a magazine or book. Use a consistent grid and purposeful serif-sans-serif combinations. Reveal information in reading order and transition through cropping, grouped movement, and layout changes rather than sliding an entire page.
styles.note: The source directly names or describes this visual direction.

tech.implementation: Measure actual fonts and build a shared headline, body-text, and image grid. Transition through masks, grouped movement, and layout reflow.
tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
framework_selection.scope: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

tech.library_selection: Choose libraries by role and scene requirements; the available options are not a required bundle. Prefer existing suitable dependencies. Use one owner for each animated property. Preserve HyperFrames as the primary video framework and Remotion as the conditional fallback. For video, drive all state from seekable composition time; live hover, scroll, and pointer behavior belongs only to interactive delivery. Select visual and motion technologies from the style, action, assets, and required fidelity before choosing the composition and export pipeline. Pipeline availability must not determine or simplify the visual style or motion technique. Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

motion_guidance.application: Apply shared movement quality to Editorial Design without weakening its visual_cues, materials, typography or existing motion_references.
motion_guidance.cadence_guidance: Use smooth, coherent authored movement where the action benefits from it. Preserve deliberate sharp cuts, impacts, constant-speed sections and reading holds; not every transition needs easing.
motion_guidance.implementation: Prefer existing timeline and renderer dependencies. Evaluate key states at requested composition time, maintain a single property owner, and cache or deterministically replay stateful motion. Do not introduce a library solely to add generic smoothing.

style_renderer.selection_basis: Use visual_cues and tech.implementation for styles, or the selected style and this pattern implementation for motion recipes. Select by visual fidelity and medium, not pipeline availability.

motion_engine.selection_basis: Use the authored action, style cadence, trajectory, material behavior, and simulation requirements. Select one owner for each animated property.

styles.executable_prompt_template:
Replace all double-brace placeholders with task inputs before execution. Use documented defaults only for omitted optional inputs and state the assumptions.
Create a Editorial Design video about {{subject}} for {{audience_and_objective}}. Use {{assets_and_exact_copy}}. Deliver a video of {{duration_seconds}} seconds, with aspect ratio {{aspect_ratio}}, resolution {{resolution}}, and frame rate {{frame_rate}}. Follow {{audio_or_rhythm_requirements}} and save deliverables to {{output_directory}}.
Use {{render_pipeline}} for composition and export only. If omitted, resolve it to tech.framework_selection.default. Check the primary framework first; use tech.framework_selection.fallback only when the documented fallback_condition is met, and record the verified reason. An existing React project alone is not sufficient reason to switch.
1. Inspect the project, available tools, assets, exact wording, and input formats. Reuse suitable existing components. Treat visual_cues as art-direction constraints and choose only the tech.recommended_stack entries needed for the selected framework and asset-generation method. Example dimensions, palette sizes, beats, and scenes apply only when the task adopts them.
2. Write a short storyboard with explicit time ranges. Give each section one main idea, a clear focal point, and enough reading or observation time. Plan staging around this style's visual rules: Organize headlines, short body copy, images, and annotations with the reading logic of a magazine or book. Use a consistent grid and purposeful serif-sans-serif combinations. Reveal information in reading order and transition through cropping, grouped movement, and layout changes rather than sliding an entire page. Add secondary styles only when their materials, composition, and movement remain compatible.
3. Implement the style-specific technique: Measure actual fonts and build a shared headline, body-text, and image grid. Transition through masks, grouped movement, and layout reflow. Keep Canvas, DOM, and WebGL in the browser and file processing in Node.js or Python. Drive visual updates from shared, seekable video time; load fonts and assets, seed randomness, and cache stateful simulation. Centralize colors, fonts, dimensions, camera settings, and timing. Build representative frames and key actions before expanding the sequence.
4. Follow only the tech.render_pipeline route for {{render_pipeline}}. Distinguish drawing or pose-exposure rate from delivery frame rate. Use task-provided or authorized audio, and synchronize picture and sound against the same time data. Match composition and velocity at loop boundaries.
5. Render and inspect actual opening, key-action, transition, and closing frames, then watch the decoded video. Check the style-specific constraints in visual_cues, readable text, correct glyphs, stable materials and outlines, missing assets, crop margins, timing, dimensions, and audio synchronization. Fix issues and rerender until the relevant checks pass; compilation alone is insufficient.
6. Deliver the video, editable source or project, a key-frame contact sheet, chosen parameters, and reproducible render instructions. State any missing assets or unverified limitations. Distinguish photographed production from simulated appearance.
Framework contract: select the packages, runtime, timeline registration, validation commands, and renderer that actually belong to {{render_pipeline}}. Do not mix another framework's hooks, composition lifecycle, or renderer. Specialist modeling, photography, drawing, and scientific computation can produce inputs for the selected video framework without being replaced by it.
Palette contract: read palette before implementation. Use its suggested tokens only when task, brand, or reference colors are absent. Keep supplied exact colors, source artwork, existing semantic assignments, and style color-family and color-count constraints unchanged. Use chroma-js to validate and normalize equivalent color values, select readable existing foreground/background pairs, and interpolate only when palette.gradient is enabled. Do not recolor assets or add hues to improve contrast; change text placement, an existing backing color, or typography instead. Follow palette.agent_instruction and inspect actual composited frames.
Optional PhotoSwipe gallery: use the PhotoSwipe entry in tech only when interactive web delivery requires an image lightbox. Follow its style_application, import_guidance, integration_guidance and selection_guidance. Supply accurate image dimensions, responsive sources, fallback links and usable navigation; preserve image colors and the resolved palette. For video, follow video_guidance and author swipe, zoom and thumbnail transitions on the shared composition timeline instead of running a live lightbox.
Optional crop preparation: consult Cropper.js in tech.recommended_stack when raster assets need interactive crop authoring. Follow its style_application, api_version_guidance, integration_guidance and color_guidance. Preserve original assets, approved colors, essential subject context and motion overscan; record the source, selection, transforms, coordinate system and output size. Await export and inspect actual framing and image quality. For video, follow video_guidance and use a saved asset or reproducible crop recipe on the shared composition timeline. Cropper.js does not supply subject extraction, background removal or missing parallax artwork.
Shared movement quality: follow shared_motion_guidance and tech.motion_guidance. Design coherent trajectories, acceleration, transitions and settling with readable holds. Use time-based interpolation and authored easing when appropriate; preserve deliberate cuts, impacts, stepped exposure, whole-pixel placement and line-boil cadence. Do not automatically add springs, bounce, floating or extra in-between poses. Derive state from composition time; bake or deterministically replay any stateful smoothing, physics or camera damping. Verify direct, backward and out-of-order seeks plus the decoded sequence and loop seams. Keep the existing palette and style-specific motion direction intact.
Production ownership: follow production_policy. Choose the style_renderer and motion_engine from the style and motion requirements first, and state the selected tools and their responsibilities. Build the visuals and movement with those tools according to tech.implementation and visual_cues. Use {{render_pipeline}} only for scene assembly, seekable composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and export. Keep specialist rendering and motion logic in their own layers; do not substitute generic framework text, DOM transitions, or framework animation helpers merely because the pipeline is available. Native DOM or SVG is appropriate when it actually satisfies the style. Integrate deterministic time-driven layers or baked assets, and verify representative visuals and motion before assembling the full video.
Audio direction: follow audio_direction. Based on {{subject}}, {{audience_and_objective}}, the storyboard, visual_cues, and motion direction, suggest suitable background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or silence. Honor {{audio_or_rhythm_requirements}} first. State the proposed choices and why they fit this topic and style; suggest mood, texture, energy, tempo where useful, voice language and delivery where useful, and scene-level audio changes. Do not impose a fixed soundtrack rule or include every layer. Source or create authorized assets, then use {{render_pipeline}} for assembly, synchronization, mixing, and export. Verify speech intelligibility, audio balance, absence of clipping, and picture synchronization in the final video.

sources.style_evidence: A book/museum-plate layout: a large serif headline, a short body paragraph, small-caps section labels, a grid of charts, orthographic plates and a stats table inside a ruled border.
sources.palette_lesson: The aged-parchment field, sepia wash and brown ink are this author's choice for a period military subject. They are not a rule of the style. What actually defines it: one quiet, low-chroma page tone acting as the canvas; a single dark ink colour for all type, hairline rules, charts and orthographic plates; a realistically lit hero object whose own materials (here iron and timber) carry the only rich colour; a translucent wash stain (here sepia) that grounds the object instead of a hard drop shadow; and UI states shown by inverting ink fill (filled versus outlined pills, a muted inactive pill), not by bright accent hues. Contrast between the dark ink and the light page must stay high for small serif text. For new subjects, pick the page tone from the subject's context. Examples: a cool blue-grey drafting paper with navy ink for a naval or aviation object; a pale celadon or jade-grey ground with deep green-black ink for a botanical or ceramic object; a warm graphite-grey board with off-white ink, as a dark inverted plate, for an engine or watch movement; a soft terracotta or clay-pink stock with deep oxblood ink for an archaeological artifact; a chalky stone white with slate ink for an architectural element. The grounding wash should take a darker, desaturated tone of the page hue, and object materials should stay true to the subject.

sources.style_evidence: Newspaper-style reading logic: a refined transitional serif for headlines, paired with small wide-tracked monospace source labels and timestamps, in left-aligned editorial hierarchy.
sources.palette_lesson: The visible palette is a near-black flat canvas (the extraction's dominant composite reads ~#080808, which includes the foreground), white serif text, cool gray card text and borders, and one mid sky-blue accent. The accent's roles are strictly semantic: the italic punchline phrase, source-label bullets, and structural rail and header markers. The near-black field and that particular blue are this author's choices for a sober news/tech brand mood. They are not a constraint of the style. What defines the style is: one dominant field, one high-contrast text color for statements, one reserved accent for the punchline and for structure, and card panels only slightly separated from the field by hairline borders. Depth is handled with blur and dimming rather than extra colors. For other subjects the field can change while those roles stay the same. Examples: deep ink-navy with warm-white type and an amber accent for finance; off-white newsprint gray with charcoal serif and a vermilion accent for a print-journalism feel; dark forest green with bone-white type and a citrus accent for climate stories; slate-plum with pale lilac cards and a coral accent for culture coverage; a light cool-gray field with near-black type and a cobalt accent for a daytime product look. When the cards are dimmed or blurred, recheck their contrast against the field so the background texture stays clearly behind the focal text.

audio_direction.prompt: Based on the topic, audience, objective, narrative, and the visual and motion characteristics of Editorial Design, suggest an appropriate audio direction. Consider background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or intentional silence. Explain which choices support this particular video; do not assign a fixed genre, tempo, instrument, voice, or mandatory audio layer to the style.
suggestion_dimensions: Whether background music is useful, and its suggested mood, texture, energy, tempo range, and progression.
Whether voiceover helps explain the topic, and its suggested language, tone, pace, and placement.
Whether sung vocals support the topic or distract from narration and essential text.
Whether sound effects, ambience, or silence clarify key actions, transitions, and reading holds.
How audio changes across scenes, supports motion cadence, and leaves space for speech and comprehension.
audio_direction.selection_guidance: Treat these as task-specific suggestions, not requirements to include every audio layer. Honor explicit user audio choices and supplied assets. When inputs are absent, propose a coherent direction and state assumptions; do not silently default to instrumental music or invent available audio assets.
audio_direction.integration_guidance: Select or create authorized audio assets separately from visual construction and motion design. Use render_pipeline to assemble, synchronize, mix, and export audio with picture. Keep speech intelligible, avoid clipping and competing vocals, and inspect the delivered audio and picture together.

sources.style_evidence: Refined serif display type, restrained palette, generous negative space, a darkened full-bleed hero photo used as mood, and a single warm accent. No excessive gold or sparkle.
sources.palette_lesson: The author's example colors are subject-driven: a brown-maroon overlay on loom footage, then a warm off-white lined field with rust/terracotta accents. These echo dyed textiles and handmade craft. They are not rules of the style. What defines the style: (1) Two scene modes, a dark photographic hero darkened for type contrast, then a flat light information page. (2) One warm accent color reserved for the italic keyword, eyebrow, rule and stat numeral. (3) Neutral light and dark text tones. (4) Saturated color allowed only inside the photographs. Keep that hierarchy and pick the actual hues per subject: one overlay tint, one canvas, one accent. Check accent contrast on both the dark and light scenes. The faint horizontal lines on the light field are a subject motif (weave/ruling) and should change with the subject.

sources.style_evidence: Refined high-contrast serif display type with a roman/italic pairing, concise copy, a sparse thin accent rule, a restrained warm glow and precise centered settling.
sources.palette_lesson: The author's example colors are a warm near-black charcoal field, a rust-brown radial bloom, ivory type and a coral/terracotta accent. That is one brand-adjacent scene choice, not a fixed requirement. What defines the style is structural: one dark or quiet field with a single soft, low-contrast light source; one high-contrast neutral color for type; and one accent hue used only for thin functional marks (caret, divider rule, small eyebrow label). For new subjects, keep the three-role split and change the hues. Examples: a deep ink-navy field with a cool steel glow, bone-white type and amber accents for a night or tech topic; an oxblood field with blush type and gold-ochre rules for culture or wine; a forest-green field with a moss bloom, pale sage type and copper accents for nature; or a light mode with fog-gray paper, graphite type and a cobalt accent for a daytime or editorial piece. Keep the accent area tiny and check type contrast over the brightest part of the glow.

tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

sources.palette_lesson: The measured dominant composite colour is a warm tan, but that comes from this author's chosen setting: a cosy, warmly lit office drawn on warm paper. What actually defines the style: a textured, low-contrast surface field; dark brown-black hand-inked contours; soft, slightly desaturated flat fills; and a small recurring accent set reused across props and characters for cohesion. Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
framework_selection.scope: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

tech.library_selection: Choose libraries by role and scene requirements; the available options are not a required bundle. Prefer existing suitable dependencies. Use one owner for each animated property. Preserve HyperFrames as the primary video framework and Remotion as the conditional fallback. For video, drive all state from seekable composition time; live hover, scroll, and pointer behavior belongs only to interactive delivery. Select visual and motion technologies from the style, action, assets, and required fidelity before choosing the composition and export pipeline. Pipeline availability must not determine or simplify the visual style or motion technique. Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. Framework contract: select the packages, runtime, timeline registration, validation commands, and renderer that actually belong to {{render_pipeline}}. Do not mix another framework's hooks, composition lifecycle, or renderer. Specialist modeling, photography, drawing, and scientific computation can produce inputs for the selected video framework without being replaced by it.
Palette contract: read palette before implementation. Use its suggested tokens only when task, brand, or reference colors are absent. Keep supplied exact colors, source artwork, existing semantic assignments, and style color-family and color-count constraints unchanged. Use chroma-js to validate and normalize equivalent color values, select readable existing foreground/background pairs, and interpolate only when palette.gradient is enabled. Do not recolor assets or add hues to improve contrast; change text placement, an existing backing color, or typography instead. Follow palette.agent_instruction and inspect actual composited frames.
Optional sketch rendering: when the brief calls for sketch-like marks, consult the Rough.js entry in tech.recommended_stack. Use package roughjs to generate seeded Canvas/SVG geometry, preserve the resolved palette, and follow its style_application and integration_guidance. Cache shapes; let the selected timeline animate transforms, masks, reveals or authored pose variants. Rough.js does not supply handwriting, authentic drawing media, a character rig or frame-by-frame poses. Keep precise text, measured geometry and approved source assets intact.
Shared movement quality: follow shared_motion_guidance and tech.motion_guidance. Design coherent trajectories, acceleration, transitions and settling with readable holds. Use time-based interpolation and authored easing when appropriate; preserve deliberate cuts, impacts, stepped exposure, whole-pixel placement and line-boil cadence. Do not automatically add springs, bounce, floating or extra in-between poses. Derive state from composition time; bake or deterministically replay any stateful smoothing, physics or camera damping. Verify direct, backward and out-of-order seeks plus the decoded sequence and loop seams. Keep the existing palette and style-specific motion direction intact.
Production ownership: follow production_policy. Choose the style_renderer and motion_engine from the style and motion requirements first, and state the selected tools and their responsibilities. Build the visuals and movement with those tools according to tech.implementation and visual_cues. Use {{render_pipeline}} only for scene assembly, seekable composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and export. Keep specialist rendering and motion logic in their own layers; do not substitute generic framework text, DOM transitions, or framework animation helpers merely because the pipeline is available. Native DOM or SVG is appropriate when it actually satisfies the style. Integrate deterministic time-driven layers or baked assets, and verify representative visuals and motion before assembling the full video.
Audio direction: follow audio_direction. Based on {{subject}}, {{audience_and_objective}}, the storyboard, visual_cues, and motion direction, suggest suitable background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or silence. Honor {{audio_or_rhythm_requirements}} first. State the proposed choices and why they fit this topic and style; suggest mood, texture, energy, tempo where useful, voice language and delivery where useful, and scene-level audio changes. Do not impose a fixed soundtrack rule or include every layer. Source or create authorized assets, then use {{render_pipeline}} for assembly, synchronization, mixing, and export. Verify speech intelligibility, audio balance, absence of clipping, and picture synchronization in the final video.

sources.style_evidence: Every frame is built from graphite marks on pale paper: smudged soft bands, firm strokes, tonal letter shading and hatching. Marks appear in drawing order, and texture stays coherent throughout.
sources.palette_lesson: The defining constraint is a two-pigment drafting system. Neutral graphite (soft grey to near-black) handles structure, shadows, smudges and reference lines. One cool blue-violet pencil or ink colour is kept for hatched fills, construction-curve families and measurement annotations. The substrate stays as bare paper with a faint grid, and it shows through the hatching instead of being covered. The warm off-white graph paper is this author's example, not a rule. New projects can change the substrate as long as there is enough contrast for both the graphite and the accent colour, then re-tune the accent hue so it still separates from the graphite. Captions and counters stay tiny and low-contrast.

sources.style_evidence: Hairline graphite-like contours for the mountain and ground, sparse one-sided hatch shading on the mountain, and volume built from marks on pale paper. Lines reveal in drawing order.
sources.palette_lesson: The red is an accent role, not a background: one warm red pigment used three ways (dense cross-hatch fill, a solid stamp, a hairline underline) against dark graphite/ink line and type. The pale warm off-white paper is this author's choice for a Japanese summer field sketchbook. The medium constraints are visible paper between strokes, line-built tone, no gradients, and one accent hue. The red sun suits a heat topic; for other subjects, swap the accent to suit the subject (e.g. cobalt for water, moss green for forest) and keep it to one pigment. The opening grey at 1s is a fade-up of the same paper, not a separate canvas colour.

suggestion_dimensions: Whether background music is useful, and its suggested mood, texture, energy, tempo range, and progression.
Whether voiceover helps explain the topic, and its suggested language, tone, pace, and placement.
Whether sung vocals support the topic or distract from narration and essential text.
Whether sound effects, ambience, or silence clarify key actions, transitions, and reading holds.

audio_direction.selection_guidance: Treat these as task-specific suggestions, not requirements to include every audio layer. Honor explicit user audio choices and supplied assets. suggestions.video_application: Contours draw first, then hatching, then light graphite arrows and short notes in drawing order, each with a reading pause.
suggestions.html_application: A process gallery where toggles reveal SVG note layers over the sketch; notes have text equivalents and a full-reveal option for reduced motion.
consistency_rules: Everything uses #383838 on #F5F2EA; no accent colors.
Note strokes are lighter than the subject contours.
The drawing order is contour, hatching, notes.

supporting_styles.role: Layout and typography: editorial grid framing sketches and captions

suggestions.rationale: An editorial grid gives pencil studies a sketchbook-journal structure with measured captions.
suggestions.best_for: Artist profiles, design essays, visual journals.
suggestions.video_application: A sketch occupies the image column and draws in while the serif headline and caption set in reading order; transitions crop to the next sketch.
suggestions.html_application: A responsive article template with sketch figures and captions, where figures draw once on view and the layout collapses to one column.
consistency_rules: Type is set in #383838, matching the graphite.
Sketches stay inside grid image frames.
Paper texture appears only within figures; the page stays flat.

sources.style_evidence: A simple-contour blob mascot with dash eyes and a minimal prop. Its reaction pose changes, a silent ellipsis bubble appears, and the background stays quiet and light.
sources.palette_lesson: The mint-gray to near-white gradient with mint and teal bokeh dots is this author's choice of mood: calm and clinical-gentle, which suits a healthcare and patient-communication topic. It is not a requirement of the style. What defines the style is the set of roles: (1) a low-contrast, quiet, tinted field; (2) opaque white pills and bubbles as the reading surface, so text contrast stays independent of the background; (3) one dark ink color for all type and line art; (4) one accent hue family reused in the decorative dots and the character details. To adapt it, keep the white-card plus dark-ink reading layer and choose a new field and accent pair for each subject. Examples: dusty lavender to white with lilac dots for sleep or wellness; pale peach to warm white with coral dots for food or family; soft sky-blue to white with aqua dots for travel or weather; muted sage with olive dots for gardening; a deep slate-navy field with white cards and soft amber dots for an evening or night topic. Recheck that the dots never sit at high contrast behind card edges. Sampled exact source hex values are not claimed. The 'dominant color' in the evidence file is a composite measurement, not a design token.

sources.style_evidence: Casual black-ink sun, clouds, grass ticks, steam squiggles, music notes and scattered paper doodles on a quiet background; expressive reaction poses.
sources.palette_lesson: The style constraint is that the substrate is visible paper (here a faint square grid with soft vignette) carrying a muted, low-saturation field, while foreground pigment is saturated: flat pixel-block colors (red, blue, skin tones, green) plus marker accents (red, pink-magenta, orange, blue, yellow) and black ink outlines. The specific warm light-grey graph paper, red hoodie, and green 'accept' button are this author's example choices for a tech/coding gag, not requirements. Keep the background quieter and lower-chroma than the pixel subject, reserve one handwriting ink (red here) for annotations, and use one strong semantic color for the key UI action (green = accept). Composited dominant measures are only light greige approximations, not design tokens.

tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

Select visual and motion technologies from the style, action, assets, and required fidelity before choosing the composition and export pipeline.
