styles.executable_prompt_template:
Replace all double-brace placeholders with task inputs before execution. Use documented defaults only for omitted optional inputs and state the assumptions.
Create a Abstract Motion Graphics video about {{subject}} for {{audience_and_objective}}. Use {{assets_and_exact_copy}}. Deliver a video of {{duration_seconds}} seconds, with aspect ratio {{aspect_ratio}}, resolution {{resolution}}, and frame rate {{frame_rate}}. Follow {{audio_or_rhythm_requirements}} and save deliverables to {{output_directory}}.
Use {{render_pipeline}} for composition and export only. If omitted, resolve it to tech.framework_selection.default. Check the primary framework first; use tech.framework_selection.fallback only when the documented fallback_condition is met, and record the verified reason. An existing React project alone is not sufficient reason to switch.
1. Inspect the project, available tools, assets, exact wording, and input formats. Reuse suitable existing components. Treat visual_cues as art-direction constraints and choose only the tech.recommended_stack entries needed for the selected framework and asset-generation method. Example dimensions, palette sizes, beats, and scenes apply only when the task adopts them.
2. Write a short storyboard with explicit time ranges. Give each section one main idea, a clear focal point, and enough reading or observation time. Plan staging around this style's visual rules: Build a continuous visual system from a few shapes and limited colors with deliberate proportions and centers of gravity. Use repetition, division, merging, rotation, and varied timing; let each state lead into the next. Avoid unrelated particles or light effects that weaken the structural motif. Add secondary styles only when their materials, composition, and movement remain compatible.
3. Implement the style-specific technique: Use reusable shape groups and shared coordinates for repetition and assembly. Use an existing path-interpolation library for complex morphing. Keep Canvas, DOM, and WebGL in the browser and file processing in Node.js or Python. Drive visual updates from shared, seekable video time; load fonts and assets, seed randomness, and cache stateful simulation. Centralize colors, fonts, dimensions, camera settings, and timing. Build representative frames and key actions before expanding the sequence.
4. Follow only the tech.render_pipeline route for {{render_pipeline}}. Distinguish drawing or pose-exposure rate from delivery frame rate. Use task-provided or authorized audio, and synchronize picture and sound against the same time data. Match composition and velocity at loop boundaries.
5. Render and inspect actual opening, key-action, transition, and closing frames, then watch the decoded video. Check the style-specific constraints in visual_cues, readable text, correct glyphs, stable materials and outlines, missing assets, crop margins, timing, dimensions, and audio synchronization. Fix issues and rerender until the relevant checks pass; compilation alone is insufficient.
6. Deliver the video, editable source or project, a key-frame contact sheet, chosen parameters, and reproducible render instructions. State any missing assets or unverified limitations. Distinguish photographed production from simulated appearance.
Framework contract: select the packages, runtime, timeline registration, validation commands, and renderer that actually belong to {{render_pipeline}}. Do not mix another framework's hooks, composition lifecycle, or renderer. Specialist modeling, photography, drawing, and scientific computation can produce inputs for the selected video framework without being replaced by it.
Palette contract: read palette before implementation. Use its suggested tokens only when task, brand, or reference colors are absent. Keep supplied exact colors, source artwork, existing semantic assignments, and style color-family and color-count constraints unchanged. Use chroma-js to validate and normalize equivalent color values, select readable existing foreground/background pairs, and interpolate only when palette.gradient is enabled. Do not recolor assets or add hues to improve contrast; change text placement, an existing backing color, or typography instead. Follow palette.agent_instruction and inspect actual composited frames.
Optional mo.js effects: consult the @mojs/core entry in tech.recommended_stack when shape, burst, swirl or HTML effects support the scene. Follow its style_application, integration_guidance, determinism_guidance and color_guidance. Preserve the resolved palette and reading holds. Build effects once, pause independent playback, and drive progress from shared composition time; verify direct, repeated, backward and out-of-order seeks. Keep one owner per animated property and preserve the selected video framework lifecycle. Do not use live click triggers or regeneration during video export. Use the existing GSAP/SVG route if an effect cannot satisfy deterministic seeking.
Optional triangular geometry: consult Delaunator in tech.recommended_stack when a 2D triangle mesh supports the scene. Follow its style_application, input_guidance, integration_guidance, animation_guidance and color_guidance. Choose a boundary strategy and stable connectivity or deliberate retriangulation; preserve approved palette roles and source data. Render the resulting geometry separately with SVG, Canvas, PixiJS or suitable Three.js geometry. Derive point states from shared composition time and verify direct, repeated, backward and out-of-order seeks, face quality and color continuity. Do not claim arbitrary 3D meshing, boundary-constrained triangulation, scientific interpolation or semantic relationships from Delaunator alone.
Shared movement quality: follow shared_motion_guidance and tech.motion_guidance. Design coherent trajectories, acceleration, transitions and settling with readable holds. Use time-based interpolation and authored easing when appropriate; preserve deliberate cuts, impacts, stepped exposure, whole-pixel placement and line-boil cadence. Do not automatically add springs, bounce, floating or extra in-between poses. Derive state from composition time; bake or deterministically replay any stateful smoothing, physics or camera damping. Verify direct, backward and out-of-order seeks plus the decoded sequence and loop seams. Keep the existing palette and style-specific motion direction intact.
p5.js option: If useful, select the p5.js entry in tech.recommended_stack for the visual layer. Build procedural patterns, particles, waves and noise-driven motion with authored pacing and controlled complexity. Follow its integration_guidance, constraints and verification, and use the selected framework composition time for redraws. Keep all approved palette colors and existing style cadence unchanged.
Anime.js option: Optionally select Anime.js from tech.recommended_stack when its documented animation features help the scene. Coordinate abstract shapes and numeric scene parameters with authored timing; renderer-specific drawing remains separate. Follow its integration_guidance, constraints and verification. Retain the selected framework render_pipeline and the HyperFrames GSAP master timeline contract; use Anime.js only through a verified time adapter with separate property ownership. Preserve palette tokens, exact copy, shared_motion_guidance and style cadence.
Paper.js option: Optionally select Paper.js from tech.recommended_stack when vector path geometry or Canvas rendering is useful. Animate parameterized curves and geometric compositions from fixed key states and shared composition time. Follow its suggested_methods, integration_guidance, constraints and verification. Evaluate geometry from fixed rest states at composition time, explicitly update the view, and preserve palette tokens, original contour character, style cadence and the selected framework render_pipeline.
Production ownership: follow production_policy. Choose the style_renderer and motion_engine from the style and motion requirements first, and state the selected tools and their responsibilities. Build the visuals and movement with those tools according to tech.implementation and visual_cues. Use {{render_pipeline}} only for scene assembly, seekable composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and export. Keep specialist rendering and motion logic in their own layers; do not substitute generic framework text, DOM transitions, or framework animation helpers merely because the pipeline is available. Native DOM or SVG is appropriate when it actually satisfies the style. Integrate deterministic time-driven layers or baked assets, and verify representative visuals and motion before assembling the full video.
Audio direction: follow audio_direction. Based on {{subject}}, {{audience_and_objective}}, the storyboard, visual_cues, and motion direction, suggest suitable background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or silence. Honor {{audio_or_rhythm_requirements}} first. State the proposed choices and why they fit this topic and style; suggest mood, texture, energy, tempo where useful, voice language and delivery where useful, and scene-level audio changes. Do not impose a fixed soundtrack rule or include every layer. Source or create authorized assets, then use {{render_pipeline}} for assembly, synchronization, mixing, and export. Verify speech intelligibility, audio balance, absence of clipping, and picture synchronization in the final video.

candidates.usage_guidance: Consider a fixed hero stage whose internal composition separates, expands, and shifts from centered to peripheral copy without a cut. Adapt the example objects to the topic. Pin the stage rather than freezing every internal subject.

Consider a progress-controlled handoff between outgoing and incoming chapters with synchronized copy and readable endpoints. Choose one compatible transition treatment and make both forward and backward state evaluation coherent.

Consider a cohesive orb deformed through bounded vertex displacement or compact metaballs. Keep the form connected and time-evaluated. Energy styling, blue, and glow are optional; this visual treatment does not establish physical fluid behavior.

Consider meaningful narrative steps with synchronized copy and visual states, plus optional within-step progress or sticky graphics. Use only scene-level motions that serve the story, and schedule the same states by time for video.

A punctuation circle can become the next geometric state while retaining center and continuity. Optional only when actual scene assets support the defining action; preserve the style palette and medium and choose no reference when unsuitable.

A single central mark with a limited set of rings and rays fits repeated geometric transformation; particles must belong to the motif. Optional only when actual scene assets support the defining action; preserve the style palette and medium and choose no reference when unsuitable.

sources.style_evidence: The whole piece is a continuous motion-graphics reel built from a few shapes (ball, square, morphing blob, point cloud) and a limited, rotating set of flat color fields, with state-to-state handoffs.
sources.palette_lesson: This author swaps whole backgrounds per chapter: near-black for physics and for the 3D chapter, saturated red-orange for transitions and type, off-white, acid chartreuse, then cobalt blue. A small shared accent set (red-orange, lime/chartreuse, cobalt, white, black) recurs across chapters, and each accent shows up as a background in one chapter and as an accent in others. These exact hues are this author's examples. What carries over is the method: flat, highly saturated digital fields with a mild radial vignette, one dominant field per section, 1–3 accents drawn from the shared set, and HUD ink that flips between dark and light (or drops to a tonal low-contrast version during transitions) to stay readable. For a new subject, build a 4–6 color set from that subject's own color world. Keep one dark neutral and one light neutral for chapters that need quiet staging, and recheck HUD and caption contrast on every field.

sources.style_evidence: A closed system of a few flat shapes (radial hairlines, squares, wedge) in four limited colours. A grid scale/rotation wave (s6) hands off to a tile border framing the title (s7).
sources.palette_lesson: The colours that define the style are a small set of flat spot colours: one near-black, one warm light neutral, and three saturated accents (orange-red, acid lime, electric violet). Each scene is a hard cut to a full-bleed field in one of these colours. The background rotates among them (dark → orange → dark → cream → violet), so no single canvas colour is the identity; the identity is the rotation of field colours. In each scene one colour carries the type (black on light or orange fields, cream on dark or violet fields) and one accent marks the key word or glyph. The specific orange/lime/violet trio and the warm cream are this author's brand-like example choices. For a new subject, keep the structure: two neutrals of opposite value plus three saturated, clearly separated hues, with full-field cuts between them. Swap the hues to suit the subject, e.g. a deep teal field with coral and pale-yellow accents for an ocean-tech piece, cobalt and hot pink with mint for a music brand, forest green and tangerine with sky blue for sport, or graphite with cool white and a single signal red for a fintech reel. Keep contrast checks per field: the accent used as text colour must change when the field takes that accent's hue.

tech.implementation:
Reconstruct the actual product's components as DOM (cards, numbers, chart states as SVG) using supplied brand tokens, fonts and copy. Neutral #F7F9FA/#263440 is used only for new presentation chrome. A GSAP timeline drives causal state changes: a button press, then a card expands as a shared element (FLIP measured once at build), then numbers count with tabular figures, then the chart path transitions. The camera is a wrapper transform with precise framing. Card labels carry data-reveal-after on their card container. X-ray recipe: exterior and interior supplied layers share one registered transform, and a feathered CSS mask-image radial position animated by GSAP replaces pointer input. No invented internals. 3s preview: tap 0–0.5s → card expansion 0.5–1.4s → metric/chart update 1.4–2.4s → hold. If no real product assets are supplied, report the gap instead of inventing a UI.
Optional recipe registered_xray: Register exterior/interior media with one coordinate system and shared transform. Reveal matching internal structure through a feathered mask without jumping scale or orientation; retain readable product labels. For export animate the mask with deterministic authored time instead of live pointer state. Keep the primary product/interface central; never manufacture unsupported internal features.

tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.

Select visual and motion technologies from the style, action, assets, and required fidelity before choosing the composition and export pipeline. Pipeline availability must not determine or simplify the visual style or motion technique. Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. sources.style_evidence: A single phone is framed against a dark, quiet vignette with concise copy, restrained warm light and generous space above the device.
sources.palette_lesson: The scene choices in this example are a near-black warm brown/olive vignette, warm off-white headline type, a single gold/amber emphasis color, and a phone screen that changes from stark white (the problem) to a warm paper tone (the solution). The gold, the brown-black field and the paper tone are this author's mood choices for a 'late-night reading' feel. They are not rules of the style. What defines the style is structural: a low-key, quiet field so the bright device screen is the luminance peak; one accent hue kept for emphasis words and the brand eyebrow; and a meaningful change in screen tone between states. For new subjects, rebuild the field and accent around the product's context and check that the headline reads against the vignette glow.

sources.style_evidence: Clean product-launch pacing: a problem-to-solution scene change, a minimal centered lockup, generous negative space and soft gradient canvases.
sources.palette_lesson: The navy and near-white canvases and the lime accent are this author's brand example, not something the style requires. What carries over is the structure: (1) a low-key canvas for the problem and a high-key canvas for the solution, with the scene flip marking the story turn; (2) one saturated accent color used only on keywords, then reused in the solution scene so the two halves connect; (3) secondary copy that is dimmed or gray, so contrast does the job of a reading cursor; (4) two soft, blurred blooms in opposite corners that keep the same positions across both scenes. For new subjects, pick the canvas pair and the accent from the subject. Examples: charcoal to warm off-white with coral for food; deep teal to pale mint with amber for health; aubergine to soft lilac-gray with electric cyan for fintech; forest green to pale sage with orange for outdoor; graphite to cool silver with magenta for audio or tech. Check accent contrast on both canvases. In the source, the lime is strong on navy but weak on near-white, which is why the date line needs its gray label.

tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Use one owner for each animated property. Preserve HyperFrames as the primary video framework and Remotion as the conditional fallback. For video, drive all state from seekable composition time; live hover, scroll, and pointer behavior belongs only to interactive delivery. Select visual and motion technologies from the style, action, assets, and required fidelity before choosing the composition and export pipeline. suggested_combinations.selection_guidance: Use Scientific Visualization alone when charts and labeled mechanisms suffice. Choose a hybrid when a mechanism needs drawn diagrams or the story spans orders of magnitude, keeping semantic color assignments unchanged.

suggestions.rationale: Line art gives mechanisms a clean drawn structure that Manim or D3 can reveal in causal order.
suggestions.best_for: Science explainers, research summaries and process mechanisms.
suggestions.video_application: Objects outline first, then arrows draw causal relationships in teal/ochre/violet semantic colors, with pauses after each step.
suggestions.html_application: D3/SVG stepper where each step reveals a mechanism stage; keyboard navigation, alt text summaries and data tables.
consistency_rules: Each accent keeps one semantic meaning throughout
Units and labels appear with their objects
Line widths encode hierarchy only
avoid: Decorative lines that imply causation not in the data

supporting_styles.role: Scene transitions: continuous zoom between scale levels

suggestions.rationale: Infinite zoom makes scale relationships tangible when each level is embedded in the previous one.
suggestions.best_for: Scale-of-the-universe or organism-to-molecule stories.
suggestions.video_application: Zoom into a labelled region until it becomes the next scene, with a persistent scale bar updating units.
suggestions.html_application: Scroll or button-driven zoom levels with a visible scale indicator; each level is also reachable as a labelled step.
consistency_rules: A scale bar with correct units persists through zooms
Color semantics identical across levels
Hold at each level for reading
avoid: Implying continuity where scales are not actually nested

styles.visual_cues: Plan connected worlds or scales so the next scene already exists within a visible object, lens, or portal. Follow a continuous zoom path and align transitions as the portal fills the frame. Match focus, scale, and velocity; a loop must connect both composition and motion.
styles.note: The source directly names or describes this visual direction. A camera and transition technique rather than an art movement.

tech.implementation: Define portals, transform chains, and handoff scales for each level. Drive camera matrices from time and render sections separately if needed to control memory use.
tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
framework_selection.scope: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

tech.library_selection: Choose libraries by role and scene requirements; the available options are not a required bundle. Prefer existing suitable dependencies. Use one owner for each animated property. Preserve HyperFrames as the primary video framework and Remotion as the conditional fallback. For video, drive all state from seekable composition time; live hover, scroll, and pointer behavior belongs only to interactive delivery. Select visual and motion technologies from the style, action, assets, and required fidelity before choosing the composition and export pipeline. Pipeline availability must not determine or simplify the visual style or motion technique. Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

motion_guidance.application: Apply shared movement quality to Infinite Zoom without weakening its visual_cues, materials, typography or existing motion_references.
motion_guidance.cadence_guidance: Use smooth, coherent authored movement where the action benefits from it. Preserve deliberate sharp cuts, impacts, constant-speed sections and reading holds; not every transition needs easing.
motion_guidance.implementation: Prefer existing timeline and renderer dependencies. Evaluate key states at requested composition time, maintain a single property owner, and cache or deterministically replay stateful motion. Do not introduce a library solely to add generic smoothing.

style_renderer.selection_basis: Use visual_cues and tech.implementation for styles, or the selected style and this pattern implementation for motion recipes. Select by visual fidelity and medium, not pipeline availability.

motion_engine.selection_basis: Use the authored action, style cadence, trajectory, material behavior, and simulation requirements. Select one owner for each animated property.

1. Inspect the project, available tools, assets, exact wording, and input formats. Reuse suitable existing components. Plan staging around this style's visual rules: Plan connected worlds or scales so the next scene already exists within a visible object, lens, or portal. Framework contract: select the packages, runtime, timeline registration, validation commands, and renderer that actually belong to {{render_pipeline}}. Do not mix another framework's hooks, composition lifecycle, or renderer. Specialist modeling, photography, drawing, and scientific computation can produce inputs for the selected video framework without being replaced by it.
Palette contract: read palette before implementation. Use its suggested tokens only when task, brand, or reference colors are absent. Keep supplied exact colors, source artwork, existing semantic assignments, and style color-family and color-count constraints unchanged. Use chroma-js to validate and normalize equivalent color values, select readable existing foreground/background pairs, and interpolate only when palette.gradient is enabled. Do not recolor assets or add hues to improve contrast; change text placement, an existing backing color, or typography instead. Follow palette.agent_instruction and inspect actual composited frames.
Shared movement quality: follow shared_motion_guidance and tech.motion_guidance. Design coherent trajectories, acceleration, transitions and settling with readable holds. Use time-based interpolation and authored easing when appropriate; preserve deliberate cuts, impacts, stepped exposure, whole-pixel placement and line-boil cadence. Do not automatically add springs, bounce, floating or extra in-between poses. Derive state from composition time; bake or deterministically replay any stateful smoothing, physics or camera damping. Verify direct, backward and out-of-order seeks plus the decoded sequence and loop seams. Keep the existing palette and style-specific motion direction intact.
Production ownership: follow production_policy. Choose the style_renderer and motion_engine from the style and motion requirements first, and state the selected tools and their responsibilities. Build the visuals and movement with those tools according to tech.implementation and visual_cues. Use {{render_pipeline}} only for scene assembly, seekable composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and export. Keep specialist rendering and motion logic in their own layers; do not substitute generic framework text, DOM transitions, or framework animation helpers merely because the pipeline is available. Native DOM or SVG is appropriate when it actually satisfies the style. Integrate deterministic time-driven layers or baked assets, and verify representative visuals and motion before assembling the full video.
Audio direction: follow audio_direction. Based on {{subject}}, {{audience_and_objective}}, the storyboard, visual_cues, and motion direction, suggest suitable background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or silence. Honor {{audio_or_rhythm_requirements}} first. State the proposed choices and why they fit this topic and style; suggest mood, texture, energy, tempo where useful, voice language and delivery where useful, and scene-level audio changes. Do not impose a fixed soundtrack rule or include every layer. Source or create authorized assets, then use {{render_pipeline}} for assembly, synchronization, mixing, and export. Verify speech intelligibility, audio balance, absence of clipping, and picture synchronization in the final video.

motion_references.selection_policy: Optional candidates are screened for natural style compatibility. Before selection, inspect the actual scene illustration, assets, geometry and narrative beat. Keep only references whose defining action is supported by that scene. Choosing no reference is valid. Do not infer motion from a similar label; do not replace the existing style motion direction.

candidates.usage_guidance: Consider a vortex passage with camera advance, expanding surrounding bands, full-frame central coverage, and a destination reveal. Use only when the topic benefits from a meaningful chapter passage; a decorative spiral is insufficient.

Consider a gateway-centered environment with slow approach, rising mist, and bounded depth-layer parallax. Use only when the scene and topic support an atmospheric opening; this ID does not describe a cursor-following light trail.

Consider a progress-controlled handoff between outgoing and incoming chapters with synchronized copy and readable endpoints. Choose one compatible transition treatment and make both forward and backward state evaluation coherent.

Consider meaningful narrative steps with synchronized copy and visual states, plus optional within-step progress or sticky graphics. Use only scene-level motions that serve the story, and schedule the same states by time for video.
Use real depth geometry or a clearly identified 2.5D approximation. Do not translate a camera through a flat illustration and call it a dolly.

The punctuation mark is a visible portal whose next scene exists within it; match focus scale and velocity. Optional only when actual scene assets support the defining action; preserve the style palette and medium and choose no reference when unsuitable.

A drawn mark can become the portal: a lasso around the region that holds the next scene straightens into the frame the zoom travels through. Optional only when the marked region really contains the destination; keep one persistent frame stroke and reveal labels after it locks.

motion_references.agent_instruction: Read the actual illustration and complete pattern description, motion_sequence and video_adaptation. Identify which scene elements implement that action. Reject unsupported geometry, absent subjects, unintended depth, broken contact points or unrelated interactions. Select none when no candidate fits; use restrained style-native motion instead. Preserve authored transforms, fixed backgrounds and reading layers.

source_frame_review.sampling_limitation: One frame at each available second 01–08. No continuous motion, sub-second timing, audio or later scenes verified. Color families are visual observations; whole-frame measured dominant colors are not semantic background tokens.
source_frame_review.guidance: Choose scene-dependent backgrounds and readable coordinated colors. Separate material colors, source demonstration choices and surrounding UI/letterboxing. Existing swatches are examples, not permanent canvas restrictions. Keep explicit user-approved colors and medium-defining constraints. Only sampled seconds, not continuous motion or audio, were visually reviewed.

sources.style_evidence: A continuous camera push from the whole PC into its cooler, with a log-scale field-of-view ruler (1 m to 1 nm) whose readout drops each second (about 95 → 22.5 cm). The next scale level already exists inside the current object.
sources.palette_lesson: The colours are lighting, not paint. The canvas is an unlit near-black void (the dominant composite reads around #080808), the objects are neutral achromatic greys that brighten as key light and proximity increase, and one warm amber family is used for two roles: emissive functional trim (airflow rings, heatpipes, light bars) and UI data (scale readout, title rule, subline). The amber-on-black pairing is this author's example. The style constraint itself is one saturated semantic accent over a neutral, value-driven material stage, with UI kept flat and high-contrast. For other subjects, choose the stage and accent from the subject. Keep a single accent that means one thing, keep it off large surface fills, and recheck label contrast as exposure rises (by 8 s the fins approach clipping).

sources.style_evidence: One continuous push-in runs from desk, to phone, to PCB, to SoC, to die blocks, to cell array. Each next scale already sits visible inside the previous frame (chip on board, odd cell in grid).
sources.palette_lesson: The palette comes from the subject at each scale, not from a fixed canvas. The warm brown wood desk is only this author's staging choice for a human-scale establishing shot. Past that, color is set by material identity: green solder mask, cream SMD parts, chrome and copper. At die level, color turns semantic: muted, low-saturation purple, sage, slate blue, olive, ochre and pastel blocks, separated by near-black gutters, with pale grey for repetitive arrays. The fixed rules are low-saturation functional coding, a dark structural ground between regions, and one deliberately different element as the next target. For new subjects, choose the outer environment from the story and let each deeper scale bring in its own palette. Recheck contrast between region colors and the dark gaps.

Consider background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or intentional silence. Whether sound effects, ambience, or silence clarify key actions, transitions, and reading holds.

sources.style_evidence: All eight seconds read as one unbroken camera path: a smooth pull-back and rise from the deck-level boat to an altitude view of open water. Lighting and the wake stay continuous with no cuts, and the structure comes from scale change.
sources.palette_lesson: The colors here belong to this author's lighting setup, not to the style. The sunset gives a warm gold horizon, a slate sky and deep blue-teal water, with a white-hot sun-glitter path. Saturated local color is kept to small props (yellow and blue boxes, a red-orange hull stripe, a red flag) so they read against the cool sea. The dominant composite color moves from mid grey-violet in the close shots to near-black teal in the altitude shots. That shift is driven by framing and light, not by a fixed background swatch. What defines the style is a lit 3D environment where the sky and water are the background, a single key light that sets the warm/cool split, and a few local accents on simple geometry. Choose the key light and environment for each new subject instead of reusing this sunset.

sources.style_evidence: Across 1–8 s there are no cuts. A single camera path dollies, tilts low over the die and keeps lighting continuous.
sources.palette_lesson: The palette comes from the subject at each scale, not from a fixed canvas. The warm brown wood desk is only this author's staging choice for a human-scale establishing shot. Past that, color is set by material identity: green solder mask, cream SMD parts, chrome and copper. At die level, color turns semantic: muted, low-saturation purple, sage, slate blue, olive, ochre and pastel blocks, separated by near-black gutters, with pale grey for repetitive arrays. The fixed rules are low-saturation functional coding, a dark structural ground between regions, and one deliberately different element as the next target. For new subjects, choose the outer environment from the story and let each deeper scale bring in its own palette. Recheck contrast between region colors and the dark gaps.

Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. sources.style_evidence: At 6s a white form is mid-morph between rounded square and triangle, with contour echoes and a target-shape caption.
sources.palette_lesson: This author swaps whole backgrounds per chapter: near-black for physics and for the 3D chapter, saturated red-orange for transitions and type, off-white, acid chartreuse, then cobalt blue. A small shared accent set (red-orange, lime/chartreuse, cobalt, white, black) recurs across chapters, and each accent shows up as a background in one chapter and as an accent in others. These exact hues are this author's examples. What carries over is the method: flat, highly saturated digital fields with a mild radial vignette, one dominant field per section, 1–3 accents drawn from the shared set, and HUD ink that flips between dark and light (or drops to a tonal low-contrast version during transitions) to stay readable. For a new subject, build a 4–6 color set from that subject's own color world. Keep one dark neutral and one light neutral for chapters that need quiet staging, and recheck HUD and caption contrast on every field.

sources.style_evidence: One continuous object changes form: circle (1s) → card (2–3s) → pill slider (4–5s) → toggle (6s) → segmented control (7s) → chart card (8s). It stays centred and continuous across these changes rather than cutting.
sources.palette_lesson: The near-white neutral grey stage and the orange-magenta-violet artwork gradient are this author's example choices, not fixed rules. What defines the style is the structure. (1) A quiet, low-texture stage separate from the object. (2) A strictly two-value object language, black and white, whose polarity can flip between components: a black card with white marks, then a white card with black marks. (3) At most one saturated accent, kept inside a content element such as artwork or a data highlight, never across the background. (4) Soft, wide, low-contrast shadows that lift the object off the stage. For new subjects, keep the high-contrast object pair and the single contained accent, and choose the stage to suit the scene. When the stage is dark, invert the object polarity and recheck shadow and edge contrast, because soft dark shadows disappear on dark stages. In that case use a faint rim or a lighter surface tone instead.

sources.style_evidence: Flat artwork is separated into foreground columns, midground subjects and background fog, with defocused foreground layers (s5) and distant faded silhouettes (s3, s4). Depth comes from layers, not modeling.
sources.palette_lesson: This author does not use a fixed canvas color. Each environment sets its own dominant hue family: navy-black for the abyss, violet fog for the jellyfish, rust-orange murk for the vents, teal-green for the wreck, black-purple with green-violet particles for the bioluminescent zone. What stays constant is the hero's own palette (brass/bronze shell, cool blue eyes) and a single warm cream-gold lamp glow, which is the brightest warm value in every frame. The rule to transfer: keep the backgrounds dark and low in value, pick one environment hue family per scene, and keep the hero's light source as the stable luminance anchor so it reads against any hue. Even in the warm rust scene, the lamp stays the highest-value spot. Source colors were not sampled; these are color-family descriptions only.

sources.style_evidence: Decor layers move outward and upward at different rates while the can tumbles down independently, giving a scroll-driven depth separation.
sources.palette_lesson: The sage-green field and cream reading panel are this author's brand and flavour choices for one product. They are not style requirements. What defines the style: one flat, low-detail canvas colour per section. Flat decor uses three or four saturated, warm-cool contrasting fills (here coral, yellow, deep green and sky blue), with white kept for doodles and sparkles. Sections change through a large calm neutral that holds dark, thin type. The canvas should be desaturated relative to the accents so the saturated decor and the specular 3D hero both pop. Pick the canvas hue from the subject (e.g. its flavour, ingredient or mood), then pick accents that contrast with it.

tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
framework_selection.scope: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

tech.library_selection: Choose libraries by role and scene requirements; the available options are not a required bundle. Prefer existing suitable dependencies. Use one owner for each animated property. Preserve HyperFrames as the primary video framework and Remotion as the conditional fallback. For video, drive all state from seekable composition time; live hover, scroll, and pointer behavior belongs only to interactive delivery. Select visual and motion technologies from the style, action, assets, and required fidelity before choosing the composition and export pipeline. Pipeline availability must not determine or simplify the visual style or motion technique. Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

1. Inspect the project, available tools, assets, exact wording, and input formats. Reuse suitable existing components. Treat visual_cues as art-direction constraints and choose only the tech.recommended_stack entries needed for the selected framework and asset-generation method. Example dimensions, palette sizes, beats, and scenes apply only when the task adopts them.
2. Write a short storyboard with explicit time ranges. Give each section one main idea, a clear focal point, and enough reading or observation time. Plan staging around this style's visual rules: Design a complete static poster with clear headline, imagery, supporting information, and negative space before adding motion. Use local loops, layout changes, or controlled boundary crossings while retaining useful still frames. Give important text reading opportunities and match loop endpoints. Add secondary styles only when their materials, composition, and movement remain compatible.
3. Implement the style-specific technique: Build the static poster first, then animate selected elements and layout transitions. Match start and end parameters and preserve readable text. Keep Canvas, DOM, and WebGL in the browser and file processing in Node.js or Python. Drive visual updates from shared, seekable video time; load fonts and assets, seed randomness, and cache stateful simulation. Centralize colors, fonts, dimensions, camera settings, and timing. Build representative frames and key actions before expanding the sequence.
4. Follow only the tech.render_pipeline route for {{render_pipeline}}. Distinguish drawing or pose-exposure rate from delivery frame rate. Use task-provided or authorized audio, and synchronize picture and sound against the same time data. Match composition and velocity at loop boundaries.
5. Render and inspect actual opening, key-action, transition, and closing frames, then watch the decoded video. Check the style-specific constraints in visual_cues, readable text, correct glyphs, stable materials and outlines, missing assets, crop margins, timing, dimensions, and audio synchronization. Fix issues and rerender until the relevant checks pass; compilation alone is insufficient.

Framework contract: select the packages, runtime, timeline registration, validation commands, and renderer that actually belong to {{render_pipeline}}. Do not mix another framework's hooks, composition lifecycle, or renderer. Specialist modeling, photography, drawing, and scientific computation can produce inputs for the selected video framework without being replaced by it.
Palette contract: read palette before implementation. Use its suggested tokens only when task, brand, or reference colors are absent. Keep supplied exact colors, source artwork, existing semantic assignments, and style color-family and color-count constraints unchanged. Use chroma-js to validate and normalize equivalent color values, select readable existing foreground/background pairs, and interpolate only when palette.gradient is enabled. Do not recolor assets or add hues to improve contrast; change text placement, an existing backing color, or typography instead. Follow palette.agent_instruction and inspect actual composited frames.
Optional PhotoSwipe gallery: use the PhotoSwipe entry in tech only when interactive web delivery requires an image lightbox. Follow its style_application, import_guidance, integration_guidance and selection_guidance. Supply accurate image dimensions, responsive sources, fallback links and usable navigation; preserve image colors and the resolved palette. For video, follow video_guidance and author swipe, zoom and thumbnail transitions on the shared composition timeline instead of running a live lightbox.
Optional crop preparation: consult Cropper.js in tech.recommended_stack when raster assets need interactive crop authoring. Follow its style_application, api_version_guidance, integration_guidance and color_guidance. Preserve original assets, approved colors, essential subject context and motion overscan; record the source, selection, transforms, coordinate system and output size. Await export and inspect actual framing and image quality. For video, follow video_guidance and use a saved asset or reproducible crop recipe on the shared composition timeline. Cropper.js does not supply subject extraction, background removal or missing parallax artwork.
Optional mo.js effects: consult the @mojs/core entry in tech.recommended_stack when shape, burst, swirl or HTML effects support the scene. Follow its style_application, integration_guidance, determinism_guidance and color_guidance. Preserve the resolved palette and reading holds. Build effects once, pause independent playback, and drive progress from shared composition time; verify direct, repeated, backward and out-of-order seeks. Keep one owner per animated property and preserve the selected video framework lifecycle. Do not use live click triggers or regeneration during video export. Use the existing GSAP/SVG route if an effect cannot satisfy deterministic seeking.
Shared movement quality: follow shared_motion_guidance and tech.motion_guidance. Design coherent trajectories, acceleration, transitions and settling with readable holds. Use time-based interpolation and authored easing when appropriate; preserve deliberate cuts, impacts, stepped exposure, whole-pixel placement and line-boil cadence. Do not automatically add springs, bounce, floating or extra in-between poses. Derive state from composition time; bake or deterministically replay any stateful smoothing, physics or camera damping. Verify direct, backward and out-of-order seeks plus the decoded sequence and loop seams. Keep the existing palette and style-specific motion direction intact.
Anime.js option: Optionally select Anime.js from tech.recommended_stack when its documented animation features help the scene. Coordinate typography and graphic layers in a short composition with readable holds and an explicitly designed loop boundary. Follow its integration_guidance, constraints and verification. Retain the selected framework render_pipeline and the HyperFrames GSAP master timeline contract; use Anime.js only through a verified time adapter with separate property ownership. Preserve palette tokens, exact copy, shared_motion_guidance and style cadence.
Production ownership: follow production_policy. Choose the style_renderer and motion_engine from the style and motion requirements first, and state the selected tools and their responsibilities. Build the visuals and movement with those tools according to tech.implementation and visual_cues. Use {{render_pipeline}} only for scene assembly, seekable composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and export. Keep specialist rendering and motion logic in their own layers; do not substitute generic framework text, DOM transitions, or framework animation helpers merely because the pipeline is available. Native DOM or SVG is appropriate when it actually satisfies the style. Integrate deterministic time-driven layers or baked assets, and verify representative visuals and motion before assembling the full video.
Audio direction: follow audio_direction. Based on {{subject}}, {{audience_and_objective}}, the storyboard, visual_cues, and motion direction, suggest suitable background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or silence. Honor {{audio_or_rhythm_requirements}} first. State the proposed choices and why they fit this topic and style; suggest mood, texture, energy, tempo where useful, voice language and delivery where useful, and scene-level audio changes. Do not impose a fixed soundtrack rule or include every layer. Source or create authorized assets, then use {{render_pipeline}} for assembly, synchronization, mixing, and export. Verify speech intelligibility, audio balance, absence of clipping, and picture synchronization in the final video.

sources.style_evidence: Vertical event-poster layout. Title card, two day lineups, then a closing title card, with motion limited to type builds and ribbon intensity changes.
sources.palette_lesson: The lavender-to-pink gradient, the blue-violet and coral ribbons and the violet year numerals are this author's colors for one festival brand. They are not a style rule. What carries over is a structure. A single soft two-stop gradient field serves as the canvas. Two or three saturated gradient ribbons share the canvas's color family, plus one warm complementary ribbon. The type is one very dark, near-black hue taken from the gradient family so it stays readable on every part of the gradient. One accent hue is reused on a key word or number. A white label pill gives the small header text its own contrast. When dense text appears, ribbon opacity drops so the type stays legible, and it comes back up on the title cards. For new subjects, choose the gradient from the subject's mood and keep the dark-type contrast check for the lightest and darkest ends of the gradient.

sources.style_evidence: Seconds 7–8 settle into a complete static poster lockup: headline, subtitle strip, kicker, date label and stamp badge in balanced negative space.
sources.palette_lesson: The author's example palette is a grainy near-black ground, warm off-white type and one saturated crimson accent. Red builds up in stages: first a separator dot, then low-value radial rays, then a full-width flat band, and finally a stamp badge. What defines the style is not the black or the specific red. It is three things: a single dominant dark or neutral ground, one high-chroma signal color kept for punctuation and the hero band, and type with the strongest value contrast. The background never competes, because the sunburst rays sit close to the ground's value. Type that sits on the accent band stays the paper/off-white tone, so the band reads as a backing plate rather than as the canvas. For new subjects, change the ground and the accent while keeping these roles: for example, a deep indigo/ink-navy ground with a signal-orange band, a cold slate/graphite ground with an acid-yellow band, a deep forest or bottle-green ground with a vermilion band, or an inverted light warm-gray paper ground with black type and a cobalt band. Keep one accent hue, keep the rays within roughly 10–15% of the ground's value, and check the contrast of off-white type on the band.

audio_direction.prompt: Based on the topic, audience, objective, narrative, and the visual and motion characteristics of Motion Poster, suggest an appropriate audio direction. Consider background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or intentional silence. Explain which choices support this particular video; do not assign a fixed genre, tempo, instrument, voice, or mandatory audio layer to the style.
suggestion_dimensions: Whether background music is useful, and its suggested mood, texture, energy, tempo range, and progression.
Whether voiceover helps explain the topic, and its suggested language, tone, pace, and placement.
Whether sung vocals support the topic or distract from narration and essential text.
Whether sound effects, ambience, or silence clarify key actions, transitions, and reading holds.
How audio changes across scenes, supports motion cadence, and leaves space for speech and comprehension.
audio_direction.selection_guidance: Treat these as task-specific suggestions, not requirements to include every audio layer. Honor explicit user audio choices and supplied assets. When inputs are absent, propose a coherent direction and state assumptions; do not silently default to instrumental music or invent available audio assets.
audio_direction.integration_guidance: Select or create authorized audio assets separately from visual construction and motion design. Use render_pipeline to assemble, synchronize, mix, and export audio with picture. Keep speech intelligible, avoid clipping and competing vocals, and inspect the delivered audio and picture together.

sources.style_evidence: Strictly frontal, axially symmetric theatrical framing: paired curtains, paired lamps, a centred cup and pelmet medallion, and a controlled pastel-plus-jewel palette.
sources.palette_lesson: The pinks, the lavender mountains, the pink castle, the violet curtains, the gold trim and the crimson train are this author's choices for one cozy, whimsical rail scene. They are not rules of the style. What actually defines the style: a saturated, opaque, fixed interior frame that contrasts with the lighter, lower-contrast moving exterior; jewel-tone drapes against a calmer wall; small metallic accents; and depth shown by saturation and value falling off with distance. One unified grain or paper texture covers both layers. Exterior hues should follow the subject, time of day and weather. When a passing object fills the window, recheck contrast against the frame, because the dominant colour can flip completely, as it does from violet to crimson at second 8. The supplied colour figures are downscaled composite dominants, not design tokens.

sources.style_evidence: Seconds 1–7 use strict axial symmetry and frontal one-point framing: a tunnel vanishing point, a central aisle and a centered screen. Theatrical repeated architecture and a slow push-in along the axis.
sources.palette_lesson: The near-black, cool slate and blue-gray world is this author's choice for an oppressive, broadcast-dystopia mood. It is not a fixed rule of the style. What defines the craft: (1) a narrow, low-saturation environment value range; (2) one dominant light source per shot (tunnel core, projection screen, ceiling strips) that sets the silhouettes; (3) exactly one saturated hue reserved for the protagonist or turning point, with matching local light spill. The orange-red accent is meaningful because nothing else in the frame is warm. For new subjects, change the environment's color family and keep the single complementary accent: deep teal-green sea cave with a coral accent; dusty violet desert dusk with a lime or acid-yellow accent; warm sepia factory haze with a cobalt accent; cold snow-white overcast field with dark figures and a crimson accent; murky olive jungle with a magenta accent. Recheck that the silhouettes still separate from the glow field, and that captions on bright surfaces keep their contrast.

tech.implementation:
Silent 3s preview of the collision instrument: background #F3EBDD with an SVG ball (#293B44) dropping onto three tuned bars (#628C98, #BA7B61). An explicitly authored demonstration cue table (JSON: contact time, contact point, note, duration, labeled 'demo, not analyzed') becomes GSAP labels. Each contact visibly causes a response: bar compression, then a ripple ring, then the bar brightens for the note duration. Impacts read before the rebound, density varies, and there is a pause before the final hit. Full video: Python librosa beat_track/onset_detect and NumPy band RMS run offline, beats are manually verified, and the shared JSON drives both the GSAP visuals and HyperFrames audio placement. Account for sample attack. Never use live Web Audio analysis during export. The mechanical-sculpture recipe uses the same cue table, with bass, transient and treble mapped to separate bounded part owners, and parts return to rest in breaks.
Optional recipe collision_instrument: Each visible contact causes a corresponding note. Save collision time, contact point, note onset and duration in one offline cue table. Account for audio sample attack and ensure impacts read before rebound. Silent previews must visibly show the contact-to-response chain; full videos use the verified cues for audio.
Optional recipe audio_reactive_sculpture: Map measured low/mid/high frequency bands and amplitude envelopes to named mechanical parts. Bass extension, transient opening and upper-band brightness have distinct owners and bounded ranges. Save analysis offline and evaluate it from shared composition time; do not use live audio analysis during export. Breakdowns/silence return parts to rest without fighting the main timeline. Silent previews can use an explicitly authored demonstration cue table, not imply a real analyzed track.
tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
framework_selection.scope: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

tech.library_selection: The style is a timing discipline layered over another visual style, so the renderer is light and the shared offline cue table is central. SVG is enough for a clear contact-to-response chain. A 3D renderer would only be chosen if the underlying brief demands depth. Web Audio is limited to authoring inspection. mo.js bursts were rejected to avoid a second clock. FFmpeg is redundant with HyperFrames audio.

sources.style_evidence: Every visible development is a ball striking a labelled instrument key. Each impact plays a note, and the struck bar lights up as the event lands, so motion is driven by musical events.
sources.palette_lesson: The near-black navy canvas is this author's choice for a night-time scene. It is not a requirement of the style. The rules that actually define it are luminance-based: (1) the ground is quiet and low-contrast so emissive events are the brightest thing in frame; (2) the resting hardware (bars, catchers, launchers) is drawn in dim, desaturated versions of each instrument's hue; (3) each instrument or voice gets one stable hue family, here cool cyan-teal, warm amber-gold and dusky violet, with a small red-pink tick reserved for percussion; (4) the struck element jumps to a near-white core with a tint of its hue, then fades back. Moving to a light background flips the logic: hardware becomes mid-tone ink, and impacts read as saturated pulses or shadows rather than glow. Check that the small labels stay legible against whatever ground is chosen.

tech.implementation:
Background #F4EDDF and floor line #32444A. Two contrasting bodies, a #66978E ball and a #C78461 jelly block, each in nested <g> elements: an outer group for translation and an inner group for squash with transform-origin at the contact point. Key poses: anticipation (sy 0.85) → fall with stretch along velocity (sy 1.25) → impact (sx 1.3, sy 1/1.3, so area is preserved) → rebound → short hold → settle. Timing differs per object, and only one object deforms at a time. GSAP keyframes on the paused timeline; volume is checked by asserting sx·sy≈1 at sampled seeks. 3s preview: ball cycle 0–1.6s, block hop 1.4–2.6s, hold. Optional MorphSVGPlugin for contact-flattened silhouettes between compatible paths. Soft-body/glass recipe for full video: Three.js with MeshPhysicalMaterial on a deformed mesh, with XPBD fixed-step states baked and seeked from cache, labeled an approximation.
Optional recipe soft_body_glass: Use contact-aware deformation and apparent volume conservation with damped settling, not global scale pulsing. Combine Liquid Glass 069 when clear transmission is requested. XPBD is already in the technology pool: initialize once, cache/bake fixed-step states and support direct/backward seeking. Keep optical contours aligned with the deformed surface. Label analytic shape-key previews as soft-body approximations, not measured physical simulation.
tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. sources.style_evidence: At 1s the ball is flattened at ground contact, with impact sparks, a dotted bounce arc and a contact ellipse.
sources.palette_lesson: This author swaps whole backgrounds per chapter: near-black for physics and for the 3D chapter, saturated red-orange for transitions and type, off-white, acid chartreuse, then cobalt blue. A small shared accent set (red-orange, lime/chartreuse, cobalt, white, black) recurs across chapters, and each accent shows up as a background in one chapter and as an accent in others. These exact hues are this author's examples. What carries over is the method: flat, highly saturated digital fields with a mild radial vignette, one dominant field per section, 1–3 accents drawn from the shared set, and HUD ink that flips between dark and light (or drops to a tonal low-contrast version during transitions) to stay readable. For a new subject, build a 4–6 color set from that subject's own color world. Keep one dark neutral and one light neutral for chapters that need quiet staging, and recheck HUD and caption contrast on every field.

sources.style_evidence: Volume-preserving squash on the red figure at 7s and recovery at 8s. Vertical stretch on the blue figure at 2s and 5–7s. Bounces go from the trampoline into the air.
sources.palette_lesson: The creator chose a pastel pink-lilac room with white dots and a pink tile floor as their example environment. It isn't a medium constraint. What defines the look is the contrast: a few highly saturated, glossy, translucent jelly bodies (red, blue) set against a desaturated, high-value matte set, so each body's color glow pools on the floor and reads clearly. Props carry secondary saturated accents (yellow duck, purple ball), and the UI uses a full rainbow of glossy swatches. To reuse the style, keep the environment one or two values lighter and much less saturated than the jelly actors, give each actor a distinct hue with a matching floor glow, and keep the set pattern low-contrast so silhouettes stay readable. The source's dominant composite color sample is pink-lilac, but that comes from the downscaled whole frame and isn't a design token.

sources.style_evidence: Every letter switches medium: halftone print, comic burst, faux-3D extrusion, torn paper, liquid glass over smoke, minimal ink line. A shared black/off-white/orange system and a single centered letter tie them together.
sources.palette_lesson: Across scenes the constant is a restricted system: a near-black ink, a pale paper/off-white, and one hot red-orange accent. The roles invert from scene to scene. Black ground with a pale letter → orange ground with a black letter → paper ground with a black letter and orange offsets → a muted rust/charcoal fluid where the orange family is desaturated. The specific red-orange and warm paper are this author's example choices. The craft rule is the 2–3 role system plus the ground/figure inversion from letter to letter. For a new subject, pick one saturated accent family that suits the theme. Examples: cobalt, acid green, magenta, teal or deep ultramarine. Pair it with a dark ink and a light ground chosen for the scene, such as cool gray concrete, newsprint gray, slate, or a cream tone only where it fits. Keep high contrast between letter and ground in every scene, and recheck it on textured or fluid backgrounds.

sources.style_evidence: Painted terrain is deliberately combined with crisp cel/3D-like game sprites, vector reticles, outlined UI captions and a museum-label card. Each medium has a distinct role.
sources.palette_lesson: Here the colours come from the subject: a beach at low tide gives turquoise/cyan sea, white foam and warm sand-ochre ground, with small saturated sprite accents (red/white umbrellas, purple pearls, green props) and cream plus golden-yellow caption type. Those hues are this author's choice for a beach, not rules of the style. The style constraints are different: (1) opaque paint covers the whole frame with no blank canvas showing; (2) each terrain zone gets a limited family of 2–3 close values built from overlapping knife slabs; (3) the brightest impasto (here the white foam) carries the relief highlights; (4) game sprites use small, saturated, high-chroma accents so they read against broad painted masses; (5) UI type is cream or white with dark outlines so it stays legible over any paint. For a new subject, take the terrain families from that environment and re-check caption contrast against the busiest area.

tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
framework_selection.scope: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

tech.library_selection: Choose libraries by role and scene requirements; the available options are not a required bundle. Prefer existing suitable dependencies. Use one owner for each animated property. Preserve HyperFrames as the primary video framework and Remotion as the conditional fallback. For video, drive all state from seekable composition time; live hover, scroll, and pointer behavior belongs only to interactive delivery. Select visual and motion technologies from the style, action, assets, and required fidelity before choosing the composition and export pipeline. Pipeline availability must not determine or simplify the visual style or motion technique. Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.
