sources.palette_lesson:
The dark navy canvas is this author's choice for a nighttime, dashboard-style simulation. It is not part of what defines isometric diorama style. The style constraints are these:
- Neutral matte masses (grey concrete, brown soil cross-sections) give low-saturation structure.
- Exactly one emissive 'system' hue (here cyan/teal) is reserved for flow, transport and movement.
- A warm secondary light (yellow windows) shows that spaces are lived in.
- A small set of semantic UI colours (green on time, red late, amber priority) is used only in the 2D overlay.

For new subjects, keep these roles and resolve the canvas from the scene's lighting and mood:
- Daytime city logistics: a pale cool grey or soft sky-blue field, with darker charcoal UI panels.
- Agriculture or water systems: a muted sage or slate-green canvas with blue flow lines.
- Factory or energy: a deep graphite with an orange emissive system hue in place of cyan.
- Medical or lab: an off-white with cool blue-grey masses and a magenta flow accent.
- Ocean or harbour: a deep teal-blue with sand-coloured section faces.

Whatever the canvas, check that the flow hue stands out against both the canvas and the building masses, and that the UI panels stay readable over the scene.

sources.style_evidence: Shallow 3D blocks with visible top and side faces, a common light direction, soft contact shadows, and labels kept in a 2D overlay at 8s. The view is close to isometric, with little perspective shrinkage.
sources.palette_lesson: The near-white page and dark browser frame are screen-recording context (website UI), not a style background. The composition's real palette is inside the map: muted lawn green, soft grey roads, slate-blue water, and buildings in desaturated pastels (cream, blush pink, lilac, blue-grey) with charcoal factory roofs and brick chimneys. One warm orange/amber accent family marks the active state and tags. These colors are this author's choice for a sunny daytime suburban town, and the app even offers Morning/Dusk/Night modes. What defines the style is the medium: flat matte shading with no textures, a restrained desaturated base with one saturated accent hue for interaction or emphasis, soft ambient shadows, and readable 2D labels on top. For new subjects, take the ground plane and lighting from the scene rather than reusing green lawn and white UI.

palette.composition_guidance: Use one dominant background and a clear foreground hierarchy. Keep accents subordinate except where the style calls for bold geometric fields. Preserve exact anchors; improve balance through area, spacing and placement rather than hue substitution. Gradient samples and material lighting are not extra base-color licenses.

Use chroma-js for validation, equivalent normalization and contrast assessment; evaluate gradients only when enabled and appropriate. Select readable token pairs from contrast_checks, otherwise move text onto an existing contrasting backing. Record the resolved tokens and inspect actual composited frames before rendering.

audio_direction.prompt: Based on the topic, audience, objective, narrative, and the visual and motion characteristics of Isometric Motion Graphics, suggest an appropriate audio direction. Consider background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or intentional silence. Explain which choices support this particular video; do not assign a fixed genre, tempo, instrument, voice, or mandatory audio layer to the style.
suggestion_dimensions: Whether background music is useful, and its suggested mood, texture, energy, tempo range, and progression.
Whether voiceover helps explain the topic, and its suggested language, tone, pace, and placement.
Whether sung vocals support the topic or distract from narration and essential text.
Whether sound effects, ambience, or silence clarify key actions, transitions, and reading holds.
How audio changes across scenes, supports motion cadence, and leaves space for speech and comprehension.
audio_direction.selection_guidance: Treat these as task-specific suggestions, not requirements to include every audio layer. Honor explicit user audio choices and supplied assets. When inputs are absent, propose a coherent direction and state assumptions; do not silently default to instrumental music or invent available audio assets.
audio_direction.integration_guidance: Select or create authorized audio assets separately from visual construction and motion design. Use render_pipeline to assemble, synchronize, mix, and export audio with picture. Keep speech intelligible, avoid clipping and competing vocals, and inspect the delivered audio and picture together.

suggested_combinations.selection_guidance: Choose isometric alone for a clear assembled system or space; add a hybrid when the scene must also show flows between parts or demonstrate an actual product interface.

supporting_styles.role: Diagram drawing: connectors and flow paths drawn along the isometric axes between assembled objects.

suggestions.rationale: Line-art connectors explain relationships the blocks alone cannot, and constraining them to the iso grid keeps the projection intact.
suggestions.best_for: Infrastructure, logistics and data pipeline explainers.
suggestions.video_application: Assemble blocks with the orthographic Three.js camera, then reveal axis-aligned paths in #2C424F with #63968D pulses showing flow direction after each object lands.
suggestions.html_application: Hover or focus on a node to draw its connections and show a 2D label panel; keyboard-navigable node list mirrors the diagram.
consistency_rules: Paths follow the three iso axes only, with consistent caps and joins.
Objects reveal before the connections between them.
Labels stay in screen-space 2D, not skewed onto faces.

Tangled crossing paths without a reading order.

suggestions.best_for: SaaS feature tours and platform overviews linking several tools.
suggestions.video_application: Map UI screens as textures on iso device tops, then cut or push in to a flat front view for the interaction itself before returning to the iso overview.
suggestions.html_application: An iso overview whose tiles open accessible flat UI demo panels on click or Enter; responsive layouts drop to stacked flat cards on narrow screens.
consistency_rules: UI uses the primary tokens #F3EFE6, #2C424F, #63968D, #C58662 only.
UI micro-motion stays in its flat view; iso objects move only along axes.

avoid: Distorting real UI text by skewing it into the iso plane at small sizes.

styles.visual_cues: Build the subject from contours, connectors, arrows, and paths with consistent widths, caps, and joins. Reveal objects before relationships, then draw connections, follow paths, or reorganize outlines. Maintain continuous endpoints and readable completed structures; avoid arbitrary tangled lines or endlessly repeated drawing.

tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
framework_selection.scope: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

tech.library_selection: Choose libraries by role and scene requirements; the available options are not a required bundle. Prefer existing suitable dependencies. Use one owner for each animated property. Preserve HyperFrames as the primary video framework and Remotion as the conditional fallback. For video, drive all state from seekable composition time; live hover, scroll, and pointer behavior belongs only to interactive delivery. Select visual and motion technologies from the style, action, assets, and required fidelity before choosing the composition and export pipeline. Pipeline availability must not determine or simplify the visual style or motion technique. Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

motion_guidance.cadence_guidance: Use smooth, coherent authored movement where the action benefits from it. Preserve deliberate sharp cuts, impacts, constant-speed sections and reading holds; not every transition needs easing.
motion_guidance.implementation: Prefer existing timeline and renderer dependencies. Evaluate key states at requested composition time, maintain a single property owner, and cache or deterministically replay stateful motion. Do not introduce a library solely to add generic smoothing.

style_renderer.selection_basis: Use visual_cues and tech.implementation for styles, or the selected style and this pattern implementation for motion recipes. Select by visual fidelity and medium, not pipeline availability.

motion_engine.selection_basis: Use the authored action, style cadence, trajectory, material behavior, and simulation requirements. Select one owner for each animated property.

styles.executable_prompt_template:
Replace all double-brace placeholders with task inputs before execution. Use documented defaults only for omitted optional inputs and state the assumptions.
Create a Animated Line Art video about {{subject}} for {{audience_and_objective}}. Use {{assets_and_exact_copy}}. Deliver a video of {{duration_seconds}} seconds, with aspect ratio {{aspect_ratio}}, resolution {{resolution}}, and frame rate {{frame_rate}}. Follow {{audio_or_rhythm_requirements}} and save deliverables to {{output_directory}}.
Use {{render_pipeline}} for composition and export only. If omitted, resolve it to tech.framework_selection.default. Check the primary framework first; use tech.framework_selection.fallback only when the documented fallback_condition is met, and record the verified reason. An existing React project alone is not sufficient reason to switch.
1. Inspect the project, available tools, assets, exact wording, and input formats. Reuse suitable existing components. Treat visual_cues as art-direction constraints and choose only the tech.recommended_stack entries needed for the selected framework and asset-generation method. Example dimensions, palette sizes, beats, and scenes apply only when the task adopts them.
2. Write a short storyboard with explicit time ranges. Give each section one main idea, a clear focal point, and enough reading or observation time. Plan staging around this style's visual rules: Build the subject from contours, connectors, arrows, and paths with consistent widths, caps, and joins. Reveal objects before relationships, then draw connections, follow paths, or reorganize outlines. Maintain continuous endpoints and readable completed structures; avoid arbitrary tangled lines or endlessly repeated drawing. Add secondary styles only when their materials, composition, and movement remain compatible.
3. Implement the style-specific technique: Use stroke-dasharray, stroke-dashoffset, or DrawSVGPlugin to reveal path length. Sequence paths, nodes, and arrows according to the explanation. Keep Canvas, DOM, and WebGL in the browser and file processing in Node.js or Python. Drive visual updates from shared, seekable video time; load fonts and assets, seed randomness, and cache stateful simulation. Centralize colors, fonts, dimensions, camera settings, and timing. Build representative frames and key actions before expanding the sequence.
4. Follow only the tech.render_pipeline route for {{render_pipeline}}. Distinguish drawing or pose-exposure rate from delivery frame rate. Use task-provided or authorized audio, and synchronize picture and sound against the same time data. Match composition and velocity at loop boundaries.
5. Render and inspect actual opening, key-action, transition, and closing frames, then watch the decoded video. Check the style-specific constraints in visual_cues, readable text, correct glyphs, stable materials and outlines, missing assets, crop margins, timing, dimensions, and audio synchronization. Fix issues and rerender until the relevant checks pass; compilation alone is insufficient.
6. Deliver the video, editable source or project, a key-frame contact sheet, chosen parameters, and reproducible render instructions. State any missing assets or unverified limitations. Distinguish photographed production from simulated appearance.
Framework contract: select the packages, runtime, timeline registration, validation commands, and renderer that actually belong to {{render_pipeline}}. Do not mix another framework's hooks, composition lifecycle, or renderer. Specialist modeling, photography, drawing, and scientific computation can produce inputs for the selected video framework without being replaced by it.
Palette contract: read palette before implementation. Use its suggested tokens only when task, brand, or reference colors are absent. Keep supplied exact colors, source artwork, existing semantic assignments, and style color-family and color-count constraints unchanged. Use chroma-js to validate and normalize equivalent color values, select readable existing foreground/background pairs, and interpolate only when palette.gradient is enabled. Do not recolor assets or add hues to improve contrast; change text placement, an existing backing color, or typography instead. Follow palette.agent_instruction and inspect actual composited frames.
Optional sketch rendering: when the brief calls for sketch-like marks, consult the Rough.js entry in tech.recommended_stack. Use package roughjs to generate seeded Canvas/SVG geometry, preserve the resolved palette, and follow its style_application and integration_guidance. Cache shapes; let the selected timeline animate transforms, masks, reveals or authored pose variants. Rough.js does not supply handwriting, authentic drawing media, a character rig or frame-by-frame poses. Keep precise text, measured geometry and approved source assets intact.
Shared movement quality: follow shared_motion_guidance and tech.motion_guidance. Design coherent trajectories, acceleration, transitions and settling with readable holds. Use time-based interpolation and authored easing when appropriate; preserve deliberate cuts, impacts, stepped exposure, whole-pixel placement and line-boil cadence. Do not automatically add springs, bounce, floating or extra in-between poses. Derive state from composition time; bake or deterministically replay any stateful smoothing, physics or camera damping. Verify direct, backward and out-of-order seeks plus the decoded sequence and loop seams. Keep the existing palette and style-specific motion direction intact.
Optional rendering techniques: Read tech.rendering_technique_refs and resolve them against rendering_techniques. Select only techniques needed by the storyboard; follow their implementation, constraints, recommended_stack and verification. These are optional compatible treatments, not instructions to change this style or its palette. Preserve shared_motion_guidance, authored cadence, and the selected framework render_pipeline.
p5.js option: If useful, select the p5.js entry in tech.recommended_stack for the visual layer. Draw evolving curves and contours using explicit path progress; reconstruct trails from time or cached samples rather than accumulated draw calls. Follow its integration_guidance, constraints and verification, and use the selected framework composition time for redraws. Keep all approved palette colors and existing style cadence unchanged.
Cytoscape.js option: For scenes containing meaningful node-edge relationships, optionally select Cytoscape.js from tech.recommended_stack. Use cached graph positions and connections to generate SVG paths for line reveals; stage node and edge appearances in explanatory order without replacing the line-art style. Follow its graph validation, layout, algorithm and rendering guidance. Cache layouts and analysis, drive highlights and movement from composition time, and preserve exact graph meaning, palette tokens, style cadence and the selected framework render_pipeline. Use a custom visual renderer where required by the style.
Anime.js option: Optionally select Anime.js from tech.recommended_stack when its documented animation features help the scene. Use svg.createDrawable for line reveals and svg.createMotionPath for moving accents; keep stroke treatment and explanatory ordering. Follow its integration_guidance, constraints and verification. Retain the selected framework render_pipeline and the HyperFrames GSAP master timeline contract; use Anime.js only through a verified time adapter with separate property ownership. Preserve palette tokens, exact copy, shared_motion_guidance and style cadence.
Paper.js option: Optionally select Paper.js from tech.recommended_stack when vector path geometry or Canvas rendering is useful. Prepare authored line paths, sample points and tangents for line reveals and accents, and preserve the intended stroke treatment. Follow its suggested_methods, integration_guidance, constraints and verification. Evaluate geometry from fixed rest states at composition time, explicitly update the view, and preserve palette tokens, original contour character, style cadence and the selected framework render_pipeline.
Production ownership: follow production_policy. Choose the style_renderer and motion_engine from the style and motion requirements first, and state the selected tools and their responsibilities. Build the visuals and movement with those tools according to tech.implementation and visual_cues. Use {{render_pipeline}} only for scene assembly, seekable composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and export. Keep specialist rendering and motion logic in their own layers; do not substitute generic framework text, DOM transitions, or framework animation helpers merely because the pipeline is available. Native DOM or SVG is appropriate when it actually satisfies the style. Integrate deterministic time-driven layers or baked assets, and verify representative visuals and motion before assembling the full video.
Audio direction: follow audio_direction. Based on {{subject}}, {{audience_and_objective}}, the storyboard, visual_cues, and motion direction, suggest suitable background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or silence. Honor {{audio_or_rhythm_requirements}} first. State the proposed choices and why they fit this topic and style; suggest mood, texture, energy, tempo where useful, voice language and delivery where useful, and scene-level audio changes. Do not impose a fixed soundtrack rule or include every layer. Source or create authorized assets, then use {{render_pipeline}} for assembly, synchronization, mixing, and export. Verify speech intelligibility, audio balance, absence of clipping, and picture synchronization in the final video.

motion_references.selection_policy: Optional candidates are screened for natural style compatibility. Before selection, inspect the actual scene illustration, assets, geometry and narrative beat. Keep only references whose defining action is supported by that scene. Choosing no reference is valid. Do not infer motion from a similar label; do not replace the existing style motion direction.

candidates.usage_guidance: Consider a progress-controlled handoff between outgoing and incoming chapters with synchronized copy and readable endpoints. Choose one compatible transition treatment and make both forward and backward state evaluation coherent.

Consider meaningful narrative steps with synchronized copy and visual states, plus optional within-step progress or sticky graphics. Use only scene-level motions that serve the story, and schedule the same states by time for video.

An outlined punctuation shape can enlarge into a connected path or scene while retaining controlled stroke widths. Optional only when actual scene assets support the defining action; preserve the style palette and medium and choose no reference when unsuitable.

Reveal a designed radial line mark then expand a few coherent rays; keep endpoints deliberate and completed structure readable. Optional only when actual scene assets support the defining action; preserve the style palette and medium and choose no reference when unsuitable.

motion_references.agent_instruction: Read the actual illustration and complete pattern description, motion_sequence and video_adaptation. Identify which scene elements implement that action. Reject unsupported geometry, absent subjects, unintended depth, broken contact points or unrelated interactions. Select none when no candidate fits; use restrained style-native motion instead. Preserve authored transforms, fixed backgrounds and reading layers.

source_frame_review.sampling_limitation: One frame at each available second 01–08. No continuous motion, sub-second timing, audio or later scenes verified. Color families are visual observations; whole-frame measured dominant colors are not semantic background tokens.
source_frame_review.guidance: Choose scene-dependent backgrounds and readable coordinated colors. Separate material colors, source demonstration choices and surrounding UI/letterboxing. Existing swatches are examples, not permanent canvas restrictions. Keep explicit user-approved colors and medium-defining constraints. Only sampled seconds, not continuous motion or audio, were visually reviewed.

sources.style_evidence: Every object is built from consistent monoline contours: the robot, the thought bubble, the icon and the frames. Outlines draw on along their paths (the rectangle at 7–8s, the robot assembled in stages). Containers complete before their contents appear.
sources.palette_lesson: These frames use a monochrome palette: black strokes and type on a flat near-white field, gray for secondary labels and code comments, and no hue accents. Hierarchy comes from stroke weight, bold vs regular monospace and gray value. The near-white canvas is this author's example, not a rule. What defines the style is a single flat, untextured field with one high-contrast line color and at most one value step for secondary text. For new subjects the field can follow the scene, provided the line color is inverted or adjusted to keep strong contrast. Options: a deep charcoal or ink-navy field with off-white lines for a night or technical topic; pale cool gray-blue for infrastructure or data; soft sage or mint-gray for health or nature; slate with pale lines for security; a muted terracotta or dusty rose field with dark lines for a warmer consumer story. If an accent is used, give it one semantic job (cursor, active state, a single highlight), keep it scarce, and recheck caption and code contrast against the new field.

sources.style_evidence: Each chapter's icon is built from consistent thin white contours and connectors: a node-link network, an outlined house, a line chart that draws left-to-right and finishes with an endpoint dot. Objects appear first, then change state.
sources.palette_lesson: The fixed part of this style is the system, not the hues: a dark low-luminance stage, one saturated glow color per chapter (here blue, then red, then green) applied to both the year numerals and the ambient radial glow, white for all line icons and body text, and one warm yellow 'spark' accent reused across chapters for the key node or fill. The gradient underline on the title is a multicolor brand-like signature specific to this author's subject and should not be reused as a default. For new projects, choose the chapter hues from the subject's meaning and check that white text stays readable against each glow. The background just needs to be dark enough for emissive strokes to read. It can be deep navy, charcoal, aubergine, dark teal or warm near-black.

supporting_styles.role: Typography and grid: Swiss-style sans hierarchy and modular grid placing the drawn diagrams and labels.

suggestions.rationale: A strict grid and clear type hierarchy make the line reveals feel precise and editorial without competing with the strokes.
suggestions.best_for: Technical explainers, annual-report motion and process diagrams.
suggestions.video_application: Lay diagrams on a modular grid with flush-left labels in #27434A, then draw paths with DrawSVGPlugin in reading order, using #AA6945 for the active path only.
suggestions.html_application: A responsive SVG diagram that reflows its grid on small screens and draws each step on scroll, with an ordered text list as accessible equivalent.
consistency_rules: Keep the three-token palette; no Swiss red unless it is the primary accent #AA6945.
Stroke widths tie to grid units.
Labels set after their path completes.
avoid: Heavy color fields that overpower thin strokes.
Labels animating along with the path drawing.

supporting_styles.role: Annotation typography: handwritten notes and emphasis marks layered on finished line drawings.

suggestions.rationale: Handwritten notes add a teaching voice on top of the clean line structure, and they appear only once the structure is readable.
suggestions.best_for: Educational lessons, workshop recaps and concept walkthroughs.
suggestions.video_application: Complete each contour drawing, then add a handwritten note and circle in #AA6945 that points at the concept being narrated.
suggestions.html_application: Toggleable annotation layer, so learners can show or hide notes; notes are also available as text for screen readers.
consistency_rules: Annotation strokes are visibly looser than the primary contours but share caps.
Use the primary accent for notes and the foreground for structure.
Add at most one note per narrated idea.
avoid: Mixing hand-wobbly strokes into the structural lines.
Covering endpoints or connectors with notes.

1. Inspect the project, available tools, assets, exact wording, and input formats. Reuse suitable existing components. Treat visual_cues as art-direction constraints and choose only the tech.recommended_stack entries needed for the selected framework and asset-generation method. Example dimensions, palette sizes, beats, and scenes apply only when the task adopts them.
2. Write a short storyboard with explicit time ranges. Give each section one main idea, a clear focal point, and enough reading or observation time. Plan staging around this style's visual rules: Choose photorealistic, cartoon, or stylized rendering before building genuine 3D geometry. Use coherent bevels, roughness, reflections, contact shadows, and a clear key light. Choose perspective or orthographic framing deliberately. Animate weighted rotation, assembly, and camera movement without intersections, floating objects, inconsistent scale, or blown-out highlights. Add secondary styles only when their materials, composition, and movement remain compatible.
3. Implement the style-specific technique: Generate models, materials, lights, and cameras with bpy. Use instancing or Geometry Nodes for large object counts; bake rigid-body and other simulations before rendering frame sequences. Keep Canvas, DOM, and WebGL in the browser and file processing in Node.js or Python. Drive visual updates from shared, seekable video time; load fonts and assets, seed randomness, and cache stateful simulation. Centralize colors, fonts, dimensions, camera settings, and timing. Build representative frames and key actions before expanding the sequence.
4. Follow only the tech.render_pipeline route for {{render_pipeline}}. Distinguish drawing or pose-exposure rate from delivery frame rate. Use task-provided or authorized audio, and synchronize picture and sound against the same time data. Match composition and velocity at loop boundaries.
5. Render and inspect actual opening, key-action, transition, and closing frames, then watch the decoded video. Check the style-specific constraints in visual_cues, readable text, correct glyphs, stable materials and outlines, missing assets, crop margins, timing, dimensions, and audio synchronization. Fix issues and rerender until the relevant checks pass; compilation alone is insufficient.
6. Deliver the video, editable source or project, a key-frame contact sheet, chosen parameters, and reproducible render instructions. State any missing assets or unverified limitations. Distinguish photographed production from simulated appearance.
Framework contract: select the packages, runtime, timeline registration, validation commands, and renderer that actually belong to {{render_pipeline}}. Do not mix another framework's hooks, composition lifecycle, or renderer. Specialist modeling, photography, drawing, and scientific computation can produce inputs for the selected video framework without being replaced by it.
Palette contract: read palette before implementation. Use its suggested tokens only when task, brand, or reference colors are absent. Keep supplied exact colors, source artwork, existing semantic assignments, and style color-family and color-count constraints unchanged. Use chroma-js to validate and normalize equivalent color values, select readable existing foreground/background pairs, and interpolate only when palette.gradient is enabled. Do not recolor assets or add hues to improve contrast; change text placement, an existing backing color, or typography instead. Follow palette.agent_instruction and inspect actual composited frames.
Optional XPBD simulation: consult the XPBD entry in tech.recommended_stack only when its style_application matches the scene. Choose an explicitly verified solver implementation and required constraints; XPBD is an algorithm with no universal package or API. Define masses, rest geometry, compliance, damping, collision handling and fixed stepping. Bake or deterministically replay simulation so repeated, backward and out-of-order composition-time requests return the same state. Render evaluated geometry with Three.js or the selected renderer while keeping solver-owned positions separate from timeline-authored controls. Preserve palette, materials, poses and readable holds. Validate representative deformation and contacts; do not claim fluid, plastic clay or origami behavior without the required specialized model.
Shared movement quality: follow shared_motion_guidance and tech.motion_guidance. Design coherent trajectories, acceleration, transitions and settling with readable holds. Use time-based interpolation and authored easing when appropriate; preserve deliberate cuts, impacts, stepped exposure, whole-pixel placement and line-boil cadence. Do not automatically add springs, bounce, floating or extra in-between poses. Derive state from composition time; bake or deterministically replay any stateful smoothing, physics or camera damping. Verify direct, backward and out-of-order seeks plus the decoded sequence and loop seams. Keep the existing palette and style-specific motion direction intact.
Optional rendering techniques: Read tech.rendering_technique_refs and resolve them against rendering_techniques. Select only techniques needed by the storyboard; follow their implementation, constraints, recommended_stack and verification. These are optional compatible treatments, not instructions to change this style or its palette. Preserve shared_motion_guidance, authored cadence, and the selected framework render_pipeline.
Production ownership: follow production_policy. Choose the style_renderer and motion_engine from the style and motion requirements first, and state the selected tools and their responsibilities. Build the visuals and movement with those tools according to tech.implementation and visual_cues. Use {{render_pipeline}} only for scene assembly, seekable composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and export. Keep specialist rendering and motion logic in their own layers; do not substitute generic framework text, DOM transitions, or framework animation helpers merely because the pipeline is available. Native DOM or SVG is appropriate when it actually satisfies the style. Integrate deterministic time-driven layers or baked assets, and verify representative visuals and motion before assembling the full video.
Audio direction: follow audio_direction. Based on {{subject}}, {{audience_and_objective}}, the storyboard, visual_cues, and motion direction, suggest suitable background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or silence. Honor {{audio_or_rhythm_requirements}} first. State the proposed choices and why they fit this topic and style; suggest mood, texture, energy, tempo where useful, voice language and delivery where useful, and scene-level audio changes. Do not impose a fixed soundtrack rule or include every layer. Source or create authorized assets, then use {{render_pipeline}} for assembly, synchronization, mixing, and export. Verify speech intelligibility, audio balance, absence of clipping, and picture synchronization in the final video.

motion_references.selection_policy: Optional candidates are screened for natural style compatibility. Before selection, inspect the actual scene illustration, assets, geometry and narrative beat. Keep only references whose defining action is supported by that scene. Choosing no reference is valid. Do not infer motion from a similar label; do not replace the existing style motion direction.

candidates.usage_guidance: Consider a hovering orb that drops on activation, compresses at contact, and triggers outward surface growth. Select only when that transformation serves the topic and assets support it; do not use this ID for ambient floating or parallax.

Consider a guided camera journey along a double helix through wide, close-rung, and opposite-side wide views, with copy changes at each stage. Require meaningful subject matter and suitable geometry or prepared views; particle travel alone is a different effect.

Consider a full camera circuit around a stationary subject with angle-specific annotations and a closing front view. Require complete geometry or sufficient captured turntable views. Omit when strict isometric projection or a single flat image cannot support it; character travel around a center is a different pattern.

Consider a progress-controlled handoff between outgoing and incoming chapters with synchronized copy and readable endpoints. Choose one compatible transition treatment and make both forward and backward state evaluation coherent.

Consider a cohesive orb deformed through bounded vertex displacement or compact metaballs. Keep the form connected and time-evaluated. Energy styling, blue, and glow are optional; this visual treatment does not establish physical fluid behavior.

Consider meaningful narrative steps with synchronized copy and visual states, plus optional within-step progress or sticky graphics. Use only scene-level motions that serve the story, and schedule the same states by time for video.
Only when the scene contains separable components and the reveal explains their relationships. Do not explode arbitrary decorative shapes.
Use real depth geometry or a clearly identified 2.5D approximation. Do not translate a camera through a flat illustration and call it a dolly.
Requires real 3D depth or an explicitly labeled parallax alternative. Orbit the camera, not the subject; avoid uncontrolled full rotations.

Use a genuine 3D punctuation target and deliberate camera framing rather than a flat image-scale substitute. Optional only when actual scene assets support the defining action; preserve the style palette and medium and choose no reference when unsuitable.

Build a genuine 3D mark and controlled radial geometry with consistent light; avoid floating intersections and blown highlights. Optional only when actual scene assets support the defining action; preserve the style palette and medium and choose no reference when unsuitable.

Orbit a complete modeled hero (logo object, product or abstract sculpture) on a ground with contact shadow under a fixed key light. Choose perspective or non-isometric orthographic deliberately and keep it constant. Check bevels, roughness and highlights at every angle so nothing blows out, and avoid floating geometry. Bake any simulations before the orbit.

motion_references.agent_instruction: Read the actual illustration and complete pattern description, motion_sequence and video_adaptation. Identify which scene elements implement that action. Reject unsupported geometry, absent subjects, unintended depth, broken contact points or unrelated interactions. Select none when no candidate fits; use restrained style-native motion instead. Preserve authored transforms, fixed backgrounds and reading layers.

source_frame_review.sampling_limitation: One frame at each available second 01–08. No continuous motion, sub-second timing, audio or later scenes verified. Color families are visual observations; whole-frame measured dominant colors are not semantic background tokens.
source_frame_review.guidance: Choose scene-dependent backgrounds and readable coordinated colors. Separate material colors, source demonstration choices and surrounding UI/letterboxing. Existing swatches are examples, not permanent canvas restrictions. Keep explicit user-approved colors and medium-defining constraints. Only sampled seconds, not continuous motion or audio, were visually reviewed.

sources.style_evidence: Real 3D geometry (tower lattice, cables, deck, pier ring) shown through measured camera dolly, orbit and pull-back, with atmospheric fog for depth and no visible intersections.
sources.palette_lesson: Palette structure: one saturated, subject-owned hue (the bridge's red-orange paint) set against a desaturated atmospheric field (fog gray with a faint warm haze) and a darker, low-contrast ground plane (slate water). A separate cooler surround color (dark teal) belongs to the UI or page chrome. These colors come from the subject, location and weather. They are this author's example, not a style rule. What carries over is the luminance and saturation hierarchy: the hero object holds the only strong chroma, the atmosphere fades distant geometry toward the background value, and the chrome color contrasts with the scene without competing with it.

sources.style_evidence: Satin metal with cut-face bevels, translucent glass and a coherent key light. The camera moves from a close push-in to a three-quarter orbit to a side elevation, all in one weighted continuous camera move.
sources.palette_lesson: The near-black, slightly cool stage is this author's choice for an optics subject. It suits the subject because emissive ray lines need a dark field to read as light. It is not a requirement of the cutaway/exploded style. What defines the style is how colors are used, not the hues: an opaque, low-chroma shell material; lighter cut faces so the section reads; translucent glass; one or two small warm material accents (the gold mounts); semantic, legend-backed colors for flows (here red/green/blue rays plus a white converged core); and one saturated highlight for the selected part (the blue sensor). In a new scene, choose the stage from the subject and the lighting. Flow colors must stay readable against it, and the same color should mean the same thing across every camera move and state.

audio_direction.prompt: Based on the topic, audience, objective, narrative, and the visual and motion characteristics of 3D Motion Graphics, suggest an appropriate audio direction. Consider background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or intentional silence. Explain which choices support this particular video; do not assign a fixed genre, tempo, instrument, voice, or mandatory audio layer to the style.
suggestion_dimensions: Whether background music is useful, and its suggested mood, texture, energy, tempo range, and progression.
Whether voiceover helps explain the topic, and its suggested language, tone, pace, and placement.
Whether sung vocals support the topic or distract from narration and essential text.
Whether sound effects, ambience, or silence clarify key actions, transitions, and reading holds.
How audio changes across scenes, supports motion cadence, and leaves space for speech and comprehension.
audio_direction.selection_guidance: Treat these as task-specific suggestions, not requirements to include every audio layer. Honor explicit user audio choices and supplied assets. When inputs are absent, propose a coherent direction and state assumptions; do not silently default to instrumental music or invent available audio assets.
audio_direction.integration_guidance: Select or create authorized audio assets separately from visual construction and motion design. Use render_pipeline to assemble, synchronize, mix, and export audio with picture. Keep speech intelligible, avoid clipping and competing vocals, and inspect the delivered audio and picture together.

suggested_combinations.selection_guidance: Use 3D Motion Graphics alone for hero renders where the object is the message; choose a hybrid when the render needs strong titling or precise feature callouts layered in 2D.

supporting_styles.role: Typography: 2D kinetic titles composited over or between Blender-rendered shots.

suggestions.rationale: The 3D render carries material and weight, while composited kinetic type carries the message and stays crisp.
suggestions.best_for: Product launch films and brand stings.
suggestions.video_application: Render frame sequences with Cycles, then composite title animations in #303C40 on #EDE9E1 timed to camera beats, so type motion follows the weighted 3D easing.
suggestions.html_application: Scroll-scrubbed prerendered image sequence with DOM headings layered on top; preload frames and offer a static poster frame under reduced motion.
consistency_rules: Titles share the camera's easing curve and direction.
Type uses only primary tokens; no metallic text materials.
Text never intersects rendered geometry.
avoid: Rendering text inside 3D, where it can blow out or alias.
Fast type cuts fighting slow weighted camera moves.

supporting_styles.role: Diagram drawing: 2D leader lines and outline callouts that point to features on the rendered object.

suggestions.rationale: Drawn callouts explain components precisely, and keeping them 2D avoids extra 3D assets.
suggestions.best_for: Hardware feature breakdowns and exploded-view explanations.
suggestions.video_application: Export object anchor positions from bpy per frame, then draw SVG leader lines in #303C40 with #B9866C endpoints after each assembly step settles.
suggestions.html_application: Hotspots over a prerendered frame that draw a callout on hover or focus and show feature text in an accessible panel.
consistency_rules: Callouts attach to exported 3D anchors, not hand-placed guesses.
One stroke width and cap style for all leader lines.
Callouts draw only when the object is at rest.
avoid: Lines drifting off anchors while the camera moves.
Too many simultaneous callouts covering the model.

styles.visual_cues: Make scientific objects and symbols into consistent stickers with white borders, rounded silhouettes, and light shadows. Assign stable colors or symbols to concepts. tech.implementation: Put SVG charts, transparent stickers, and real text in a shared scene coordinate system. Pan and scale scene containers instead of requiring an enormous bitmap canvas; reveal relationships in explanatory order.
tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.

visual_guidance: Near-black grain stage; stickers keep consistent white borders and semantic fills, and black outlines become white or are dropped for contrast.

Avoid the source's generative smear morphs; use authored shape changes or cuts.

sources.style_evidence: Every object is a flat sticker-like card with a heavy black outline and hard offset shadow. Concepts have stable semantic colors (pink machine, cyan channel, gray-striped dead state, green check, yellow message), and short labels plus connectors walk through question, mechanism and conclusion.
sources.palette_lesson: The defining constraint is a flat, high-chroma sticker system: black outlines and hard black offset shadows, white card interiors, and a handful of saturated fills that each carry a fixed semantic role (in this example: pink = machine/alive, cyan = channel/receiver, gray diagonal hatching = dead, green check = delivered, yellow = message or highlight, dashed outline = absent). The pale near-white dotted field and the lime-green dotted field are the author's chapter colors for this video, not part of the style. The background works as a flat chapter-coded stage with a subtle same-hue dot grid, and it changes on a hard cut when the narrative question changes. For new subjects, choose a chapter color that suits the topic and keep enough value contrast that white cards and black strokes stand out. Avoid giving an accent its own fill as the background (for example a pink field when pink means the actor). Recheck that yellow highlight strips and pastel cards stay distinct on whatever field you choose.

sources.style_evidence: Concept icons (the chart sheet and the clapperboard) are rendered as tilted stickers with white borders and soft shadows to stand for ideas in an explainer-style statement.
sources.palette_lesson: The colours that define the style are the medium's own: a lightly textured paper canvas with fiber speckle and a soft vignette, matte opaque paper pieces in a limited set (about four to six families), a near-black rounded heavy display ink for text, and small muted geometric confetti. The author's specific colour choices (warm greige paper for the statement scene, mint/sage sky with yellow-green to forest-green hills, a mustard sun, navy and coral confetti, a lime highlighter) are one example tied to a growth and enablement subject. They are not fixed tokens. Note that the canvas tint already changes with the scene in this source, from warm off-white to cool mint, which shows the background is meant to follow the scene. In new projects, keep the paper grain, the matte cut-paper layers and the dark ink type, and choose the paper tint from the subject. Keep strong contrast between the dark type and the light paper, keep accents sparse, and do not let the highlighter or confetti compete with the headline.

tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
framework_selection.scope: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

styles.visual_cues: Place frosted panels over slow aurora bands, diffuse color fields, or mesh gradients using two to four main colors and stable brightness. Use fine borders, highlights, and soft shadows; local refraction or dispersion is optional. Keep foreground text sharp and panel movement precise. Avoid banding, shimmering edges, excessive blur, or backgrounds that compete with reading.
styles.note: A user-requested direction developed into practical prompt guidance. A descriptive combination of aurora or mesh gradients with frosted panels; not a synonym for Liquid Glass.

tech.implementation: Use a full-screen WebGL shader for aurora or diffuse color fields and CSS backdrop-filter for frosted panels. Keep text in a separate DOM layer. Add screen-space or SVG displacement only when refraction is required; background blur alone is not refraction. Seed noise and inspect filters in rendered frames.
tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
framework_selection.scope: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

tech.library_selection: Choose libraries by role and scene requirements; the available options are not a required bundle. Prefer existing suitable dependencies. Use one owner for each animated property. Preserve HyperFrames as the primary video framework and Remotion as the conditional fallback. For video, drive all state from seekable composition time; live hover, scroll, and pointer behavior belongs only to interactive delivery. Select visual and motion technologies from the style, action, assets, and required fidelity before choosing the composition and export pipeline. Pipeline availability must not determine or simplify the visual style or motion technique. Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

Framework contract: select the packages, runtime, timeline registration, validation commands, and renderer that actually belong to {{render_pipeline}}. Do not mix another framework's hooks, composition lifecycle, or renderer. Specialist modeling, photography, drawing, and scientific computation can produce inputs for the selected video framework without being replaced by it.
Palette contract: read palette before implementation. Use its suggested tokens only when task, brand, or reference colors are absent. Keep supplied exact colors, source artwork, existing semantic assignments, and style color-family and color-count constraints unchanged. Use chroma-js to validate and normalize equivalent color values, select readable existing foreground/background pairs, and interpolate only when palette.gradient is enabled. Do not recolor assets or add hues to improve contrast; change text placement, an existing backing color, or typography instead. Follow palette.agent_instruction and inspect actual composited frames.
Shared movement quality: follow shared_motion_guidance and tech.motion_guidance. Design coherent trajectories, acceleration, transitions and settling with readable holds. Use time-based interpolation and authored easing when appropriate; preserve deliberate cuts, impacts, stepped exposure, whole-pixel placement and line-boil cadence. Do not automatically add springs, bounce, floating or extra in-between poses. Derive state from composition time; bake or deterministically replay any stateful smoothing, physics or camera damping. Verify direct, backward and out-of-order seeks plus the decoded sequence and loop seams. Keep the existing palette and style-specific motion direction intact.
Production ownership: follow production_policy. Choose the style_renderer and motion_engine from the style and motion requirements first, and state the selected tools and their responsibilities. Build the visuals and movement with those tools according to tech.implementation and visual_cues. Use {{render_pipeline}} only for scene assembly, seekable composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and export. Keep specialist rendering and motion logic in their own layers; do not substitute generic framework text, DOM transitions, or framework animation helpers merely because the pipeline is available. Native DOM or SVG is appropriate when it actually satisfies the style. Integrate deterministic time-driven layers or baked assets, and verify representative visuals and motion before assembling the full video.
Audio direction: follow audio_direction. Based on {{subject}}, {{audience_and_objective}}, the storyboard, visual_cues, and motion direction, suggest suitable background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or silence. Honor {{audio_or_rhythm_requirements}} first. State the proposed choices and why they fit this topic and style; suggest mood, texture, energy, tempo where useful, voice language and delivery where useful, and scene-level audio changes. Do not impose a fixed soundtrack rule or include every layer. Source or create authorized assets, then use {{render_pipeline}} for assembly, synchronization, mixing, and export. Verify speech intelligibility, audio balance, absence of clipping, and picture synchronization in the final video.

motion_references.selection_policy: Optional candidates are screened for natural style compatibility. Before selection, inspect the actual scene illustration, assets, geometry and narrative beat. Keep only references whose defining action is supported by that scene. Choosing no reference is valid. Do not infer motion from a similar label; do not replace the existing style motion direction.

candidates.usage_guidance: Consider anchored cards progressively covered by incoming cards, with optional scale or dimming for recession and a defined stack release. Keep active content readable and simulate sticky or pinned behavior with time-driven layers in video.

Consider pointer-driven perspective tilt with optional separated depth layers and a neutral return. A voice or waveform is content layered onto the motion; choose playback separately and do not infer spatial audio from card depth.

Consider a progress-controlled handoff between outgoing and incoming chapters with synchronized copy and readable endpoints. Choose one compatible transition treatment and make both forward and backward state evaluation coherent.

Consider a horizontal card track that moves with swipe or drag and settles at a defined snap selection. Preserve readable cards, accessible navigation, and one track-position owner; author the track directly for video.

Consider a cohesive orb deformed through bounded vertex displacement or compact metaballs. Keep the form connected and time-evaluated. Energy styling, blue, and glow are optional; this visual treatment does not establish physical fluid behavior.

Consider meaningful narrative steps with synchronized copy and visual states, plus optional within-step progress or sticky graphics. Use only scene-level motions that serve the story, and schedule the same states by time for video.

Use sharp phrase units over slow aurora fields, keeping emphasis readable and background subordinate. Optional only when actual scene assets support the defining action; preserve the style palette and medium and choose no reference when unsuitable.

A precise circular punctuation mask can reveal a frosted panel while retaining optical boundaries and text contrast. Optional only when actual scene assets support the defining action; preserve the style palette and medium and choose no reference when unsuitable.

motion_references.agent_instruction: Read the actual illustration and complete pattern description, motion_sequence and video_adaptation. Identify which scene elements implement that action. Reject unsupported geometry, absent subjects, unintended depth, broken contact points or unrelated interactions. Select none when no candidate fits; use restrained style-native motion instead. Preserve authored transforms, fixed backgrounds and reading layers.

sources.style_evidence: Short emphasis captions use layered fill, a heavy dark stroke, a white outer halo and a hard drop shadow. Confetti stars burst on reaction beats. The layout is 9:16, with the mascot kept clear of the text and readable holds after pop-ins.
sources.palette_lesson: These colors are the creator's choices for this short, not a fixed recipe. Each scene uses one saturated, nearly flat background family (golden-yellow stripes, deep indigo, slate blue with a screenshot collage, mint, periwinkle, a yellow/pink/cyan wipe) and changes family at every hard cut to mark a new idea. The parts that stay constant are what define the style: a pastel mascot with a black contour, caption type in white or yellow fill with a near-black stroke, a white outer keyline and a hard offset shadow, plus small multicolor confetti. The heavy dark stroke plus white halo is what keeps captions legible on any field, light or dark. For new subjects, choose the background from the topic and mood. Options include: deep teal or ink navy for tech or night topics, coral or tomato red for urgency, a soft lilac or sky-blue dot grid for calm explainers, charcoal with a neon-lime ring pulse for gaming, warm terracotta or olive for food or lifestyle, or a desaturated photo or screenshot wall as evidence. Keep one dominant field per scene with a quieter same-hue pattern (dots, stripes or rings at low contrast), and reserve the most saturated accent (yellow or hot pink here) for the key word. Recheck contrast between the mascot's pastel fill and the field: pale lilac on mint or butter yellow relies entirely on the black contour.

sources.style_evidence: 9:16 short-form layout with bold white rounded captions, a consistent navy outline and shadow, a pink emphasis word, emoji, reaction stickers (cloud, hearts, sparkles) and an x1→x2 counter. Captions sit in the upper third, clear of the characters.
sources.palette_lesson: The colours here belong to this author's example: a saturated cyan/cobalt sky, golden-yellow sand and turquoise surf for a cheerful beach. The measured dominant colour is just the sand area of the composite, not a style token. What actually defines the style is a set of layer contrasts. (1) A fairly saturated, textured, painted environment carries the setting and mood. (2) Characters use low-saturation pastel fills (peach, cream, blush) inside a single dark navy/ink outline, so they read against any busy backdrop. (3) Captions are white with a dark outline and shadow, which keeps them legible over both light and saturated areas. (4) One warm emotional accent (pink/red hearts, a pink highlight word) is reserved for affection and payoff. (5) Neutral grey props (rain cloud, mailbox) mark sadness or utility. For new subjects, pick the environment from the story and keep the pastel-character, dark-outline and white-outlined-caption roles. Check that the characters' pastel fills still separate from the backdrop (for example, avoid a peach character on peach sand without a contact shadow).

tech.implementation:
Fixed 1920x1080 composition with a full-bleed #1B3ED2 rect as the opaque scene field (never cream). Everything is drawn in a single SVG with viewBox in drafting units (1 unit = 1 mm at a fixed scale).

Layers:
- Minor and major white grid lines (stroke-opacity 0.25 / 0.5).
- Object outlines at 2.5px.
- Hidden edges as stroke-dasharray '8 6' at 1.5px.
- Section hatching as a 45° <pattern> of 1px lines, clipped to closed regions.
- Dimension lines with extension lines.

All geometry comes from one measured spec object, so label text is computed from the real dimensions. Labels are HTML/CSS (or SVG text) in a monospaced/technical face, with each label annotated data-reveal-after="dim-N".

Motion: one paused GSAP timeline registered as window.__timelines[id].
1. Grid fades in.
2. Outlines draw with DrawSVGPlugin ('0% 0%' → '0% 100%').
3. Hidden edges draw. Dashing is a mask over a fully drawn dashed path, so it never conflicts with the drawSVG dasharray.
4. The hatch clip rect wipes in.
5. Dimension shafts draw from both ends toward their arrows.

Arrowheads are separate <path data-arrowhead-for="dim-N"> elements, set to autoAlpha 0 and switched on with gsap.set at the exact time the shaft's drawSVG reaches 100%. Each label appears only after its dimension line and both heads are complete.

Preview (3 s): one part view, about 4 dimensions, hatching and labels.
Full video: chains views through labels on the same timeline.

Verify forward, backward and direct seeks at the head-switch times. Use chroma_js to confirm the white-on-blue contrast of 7.88.

styles.visual_cues: Black field with cyan contours, narrow white cores and horizontal scan-line fills. Light is communicated through line density, without blur halos or generic neon particles.
styles.note: Added from the 2026-10-12 repository sync. Read the source and palette background evidence; reference posters do not verify every scene in a video.

tech.implementation:
A Canvas 2D renderer at a devicePixelRatio-fixed backing size. Each frame clears to opaque #07080A. Subjects are authored as Path2D outlines (head/object contours) cached once.

Render per frame from progress values:
1. Scanline fill: clip to the Path2D, then fillRect horizontal 1px lines of #45F0DD every N px, pixel-aligned to integer rows. Line spacing varies with an authored 'light' value per region, so denser lines read as brighter and sparser as darker. Light is communicated only by line density.
2. Contour: stroke the path twice, cyan #45F0DD at 3px, then a white #FFFFFF core at 1px.
3. Optional faint cyan grid behind.

No shadowBlur, no bloom, no particles.

GSAP owns a plain state object, tweened on the paused registered timeline: contour reveal (setLineDash-based length progress from path lengths precomputed via an offscreen SVG getTotalLength), scanline wipe y-extent, and density shifts. A single render(state) is called from the timeline's onUpdate and also after any seek, so direct seeks are exact. Any interior labels use data-reveal-after on their container frame.

Full video: reuses the renderer with more paths.

Reviewed technology choice: A Canvas 2D renderer at a devicePixelRatio-fixed backing size. Each frame clears to opaque #07080A. Subjects are authored as Path2D outlines (head/object contours) cached once.

Render per frame from progress values:
1. Scanline fill: clip to the Path2D, then fillRect horizontal 1px lines of #45F0DD every N px, pixel-aligned to integer rows. Line spacing varies with an authored 'light' value per region, so denser lines read as brighter and sparser as darker. Light is communicated only by line density.
2. Contour: stroke the path twice, cyan #45F0DD at 3px, then a white #FFFFFF core at 1px.
3. Optional faint cyan grid behind.

No shadowBlur, no bloom, no particles.

GSAP owns a plain state object, tweened on the paused registered timeline: contour reveal (setLineDash-based length progress from path lengths precomputed via an offscreen SVG getTotalLength), scanline wipe y-extent, and density shifts. A single render(state) is called from the timeline's onUpdate and also after any seek, so direct seeks are exact. Any interior labels use data-reveal-after on their container frame.

Preview (3 s): one subject outline draws, scanlines sweep in top-to-bottom, then density modulates.
Full video: reuses the renderer with more paths. Pixel-aligned scanlines clipped to shapes are cheapest and crispest in Canvas 2D, with exact control over line density.

Alternatives considered:
- SVG pattern fills would work but scale or anti-alias scanlines unevenly under transforms.
- WebGL/GLSL is overkill for flat line art.
- UnrealBloom and Points are excluded because the style forbids blur halos and neon particles.

Tradeoff: Canvas text is less accessible, so keep captions as DOM overlays if needed.

tech.implementation:
Three.js WebGLRenderer with an orthographic fullscreen quad and a ShaderMaterial, cleared to opaque #080808.

Canvas 2D rasterizes the authored sharp silhouette (head profile) once into a mask CanvasTexture, plus a blurred distance-like copy for interior falloff. The fragment shader computes heat as:
- the interior falloff (core warmer than edges),
- plus authored Gaussian hotspots (uniform arrays: position, radius, intensity),
- minus cooling at narrow extremities (nose, ears) from a thinness term,
- plus slow seeded value-noise shimmer evaluated from uTime.

Heat is mapped through a 4-stop ramp texture (1D DataTexture) precomputed with chroma.scale(['#080808','#C82E20','#F07C30','#FFF1D5']).mode('lab'). The ramp applies only inside the silhouette mask, and edges stay sharp via the hard mask alpha.

GSAP tweens a uniform-state object (hotspot intensities, warm-up progress, uTime) on the paused registered timeline. onUpdate writes the uniforms and calls renderer.render, so seeks are exact.

No temperature scale, degrees or legend is shown: this is illustrative heat, not measured data.

Preview (3 s): the silhouette warms from black through red to cream hotspots.
Full video: alternating paper/red scenes are separate clips; the thermal clip keeps black.
tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.

tech.library_selection:

- Inspection rails: parallel lines with notch marks.

Motion: a single GSAP driver value `drive` (degrees of the input crank) on the paused registered timeline. In onUpdate, every linked part is derived kinematically from it:
- wheel B rotation = -drive * (rA/rB),
- belt tooth stroke-dashoffset = drive * rA * π/180,
- the rail carriage translates by belt travel,
- the wheel digit settles with a detent ease when it crosses a step.

Because no part has its own independent tween, the movement explains a real operation (e.g. a carry: one full units revolution advances the tens wheel one step). Engraved contours first draw in with DrawSVGPlugin.

Any pointer arrows use a separate data-arrowhead-for head, shown only when the shaft completes. Wheel labels use data-reveal-after on their wheel group.

styles.visual_cues: Reflective fractal solids emerge from dark fog, evolve into a landscape and return to sculptural lettering. Preserve coherent reflections, spatial scale and depth.
styles.note: Added from the 2026-10-12 repository sync. Read the source and palette background evidence; reference posters do not verify every scene in a video.

tech.implementation:
Three.js fullscreen-quad ShaderMaterial that raymarches an SDF scene: a Mandelbox/Mandelbulb-style fractal solid with a bounded iteration count (e.g. 8 fractal iterations, max 96 march steps, max distance clamp).

Shading:
- normals by central differences,
- one reflection bounce by re-marching along reflect(rd, n) with a reduced step budget,
- soft AO approximated by a few SDF samples,
- exponential distance fog toward #080A0C.

The scene is rendered into a WebGLRenderTarget at about 0.5–0.66 scale and upsampled to the canvas with linear filtering, to bound GPU time per frame. Tone mapping and sRGB output are done once in the final blit.

GSAP tweens uniforms on the paused registered timeline: uEmerge (fog density and fractal power morph), camera position/target along an authored path, and uLandscape (blends the SDF via smooth-min toward a domain-repeated terrain fold). Each update renders synchronously from the uniforms; there is no frame accumulation, so out-of-order seeks match.

Preview (3 s): reflective fractal solids emerge from dark fog with a slow dolly.
Full video: continues into the landscape and later the sunset. Sculptural lettering is planned as an SDF built from a precomputed glyph distance texture, extruded via max(d2D, |z|-h). It is not in the preview, and that limitation is reported.

styles.visual_cues: Powdery chalk marks on black paper with broken textured edges and layered opaque/pale strokes. Preserve a dark paper field; this differs from charcoal drawn on light paper.
styles.note: Added from the 2026-10-12 repository sync. Read the source and palette background evidence; reference posters do not verify every scene in a video.

tech.implementation:
Canvas 2D on an opaque #15141A field. A static black-paper tooth texture is generated once into an offscreen canvas from seeded noise2D (low-contrast speckle) and drawn first each frame.

Each chalk stroke is an authored path whose points are sampled at fixed arc-length steps once, cached with tangents. Rendering a stroke up to progress p stamps small irregular dabs of #F1EBDD along the cached samples:
- dab alpha is modulated by noise2D(x, y), which is spatial and seeded, so the same pixel always gets the same grain;
- 'paper tooth' gaps come from destination-out using the cached tooth texture threshold;
- edges break up via a noise-perturbed dab radius.

Layering: pale passes draw at about 0.35 alpha and opaque accent passes at about 0.9, with chalk pressure varied per stroke parameter.

Every frame is rebuilt from scratch: clear, paper, then each stroke up to its timeline progress. Nothing accumulates, so backward and direct seeks are exact.

GSAP tweens per-stroke progress values in order on the paused registered timeline. Arrows drawn in chalk render the head only after the shaft samples reach the endpoint. Text inside chalk-drawn boxes reveals after the box stroke completes.

Preview (3 s): a simple subject is sketched in pale strokes, then opaque highlights are added.
Full video: reuses the stroke library.
tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.

Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
