tech.library_selection:
Powdery broken edges need per-dab raster compositing, which Canvas 2D does deterministically and cheaply. Seeded spatial noise from @remotion/noise (pure functions, browser-safe) keeps the grain stable across seeks.

Alternatives considered:
- p5.js adds a redraw lifecycle for no gain.
- Rough.js produces sketch wobble, not chalk texture.
- SVG feTurbulence filters are slow and harder to control per stroke.

Tradeoff: dab counts must be bounded, roughly 30–60k per frame.

styles.note: Added from the 2026-10-12 repository sync. Read the source and palette background evidence; reference posters do not verify every scene in a video.

tech.implementation:
Fullscreen ShaderMaterial on a Three.js orthographic quad.

Canvas 2D rasterizes authored sand shapes (silhouettes) and scrape strokes into two cached mask textures, A and B, for each keyed drawing state.

The fragment shader computes sand density:
- mix(maskA, maskB, uMorph) blurred via a few mip samples, to get soft accumulation;
- minus scraped negative-space lines (an SDF of polylines passed as a texture, multiplied by uScrape progress);
- multiplied by high-frequency seeded hash grain (per-pixel grain fixed in screen space, so it does not swim).

Backlight transmission: color = mix(sandColor #3A291B, lightColor #F5E3B5, exp(-k * density)). Light therefore shines through thin sand and gaps rather than illuminating a white page, with a slight warm vignette of the table (still the #F5E3B5 family).

GSAP tweens uMorph, uScrape and the sand pour radius on the paused registered timeline, and every update re-renders from the uniforms.

Preview (3 s): a sand silhouette thins, a finger-scrape line cuts through, then the shape transitions to the next form.
Full video: chains more mask pairs. This is illustrative granular appearance, not a granular physics simulation.
tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
framework_selection.scope: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

tech.library_selection:
A transmitted-light density field with fine grain suits a fragment shader. Canvas 2D masks give authored control over shapes.

Alternatives considered:
- Three.js Points would read as particles, not continuous sand.
- Canvas-only per-pixel loops are slow at 1080p.
- Photographed stop-motion frames are unavailable.

Tradeoff: grain must be checked for temporal flicker and compression banding; keep it static in screen space.

sources.palette_lesson: The stills show one dark umber/brown-black medium on a warm pale ochre-ivory lit field, with a soft centre glow and edge vignette. The medium constraint is the structure: a single dark granular pigment against a luminous substrate, with value contrast doing all the work and no second colour. The warm amber-cream field is this author's example choice. It suits a historical, commemorative theme and is not a fixed requirement. For new subjects, keep the luminous field and the one dark grain colour, but tint the light source and density to fit the scene. Change only the light-source temperature and the field's brightness; keep it a lit field rather than a flat page colour. Always check that small italic text stays dark enough against the brightest central glow.

styles.visual_cues: Folded paper structures rise from hinged pages with visible tabs, paper thickness, contact shadows and consistent creases. Page mechanics drive the reveal.
styles.note: Added from the 2026-10-12 repository sync. Read the source and palette background evidence; reference posters do not verify every scene in a video.

tech.implementation:
A perspective Three.js scene with a separately colored environment. The book is two page boards: thin BoxGeometry with visible paper thickness, carrying a #F1E5CE paper CanvasTexture with seeded subtle grain and #342B25 printed linework drawn in Canvas 2D.

Pop-up pieces are thin boxes parented to hinge pivots placed on crease lines, with visible tabs glued to the pages. Each piece angle is derived analytically from the single page-opening angle θ:
- V-fold: piece angles solve the closed-loop hinge constraint, precomputed as a function table of θ;
- parallel fold: the panel stays parallel to the spine.

Creases therefore stay consistent and page mechanics drive the reveal.

The procedural curl technique adds slight bend to large flaps from immutable rest vertices × bend(θ), followed by computeVertexNormals.

Lighting: soft key plus fill, PCFSoftShadowMap contact shadows on the pages, and an explicit ACES tone map with output sRGB checked against the paper tokens.

GSAP owns θ and the camera dolly on the paused registered timeline. onUpdate evaluates all transforms from θ and renders, so seeks are exact. Labels printed on pop-up panels live in the panel textures, so they appear with their container.

Preview (3 s): the book opens from 20° to 180° as one V-fold structure rises with shadows.
Full video: adds pages, each with its own θ track.

Reviewed technology choice: A perspective Three.js scene with a separately colored environment. The book is two page boards: thin BoxGeometry with visible paper thickness, carrying a #F1E5CE paper CanvasTexture with seeded subtle grain and #342B25 printed linework drawn in Canvas 2D.

Pop-up pieces are thin boxes parented to hinge pivots placed on crease lines, with visible tabs glued to the pages. Each piece angle is derived analytically from the single page-opening angle θ:
- V-fold: piece angles solve the closed-loop hinge constraint, precomputed as a function table of θ;
- parallel fold: the panel stays parallel to the spine.

Creases therefore stay consistent and page mechanics drive the reveal.

The procedural curl technique adds slight bend to large flaps from immutable rest vertices × bend(θ), followed by computeVertexNormals.

Lighting: soft key plus fill, PCFSoftShadowMap contact shadows on the pages, and an explicit ACES tone map with output sRGB checked against the paper tokens.

GSAP owns θ and the camera dolly on the paused registered timeline. onUpdate evaluates all transforms from θ and renders, so seeks are exact. Labels printed on pop-up panels live in the panel textures, so they appear with their container.

Preview (3 s): the book opens from 20° to 180° as one V-fold structure rises with shadows.
Full video: adds pages, each with its own θ track. Depth, paper thickness and hinge mechanics are defining, so true 3D is required. Flat SVG cutouts would fake it.

Alternatives considered:
- XPBD was rejected: rigid-panel kinematics are exact, cheaper and deterministic.
- Blender is unavailable.
- Outline/crease edge passes would push toward a cel look.
- MeshToon would flatten the paper.

Tradeoff: hinge constraints must be authored per structure, and shadow-map resolution must be tuned to avoid acne on thin boards.

styles.visual_cues: Overlapping translucent fibers, torn edges and colored tissue layers create underwater depth. Preserve light transmission and overlap rather than opaque cardstock shapes.
styles.note: Added from the 2026-10-12 repository sync. Read the source and palette background evidence; reference posters do not verify every scene in a video.

tech.implementation:
Canvas 2D on an opaque #172D3A underwater field.

Each tissue piece is an authored polygon (fish, kelp, light shafts) whose torn edge is generated once: the outline is subdivided and perturbed by seeded noise2D, then cached as Path2D. A fiber texture per piece is generated once offscreen: seeded noise speckle plus short random-but-seeded fiber strokes, with stored seeds.

Per frame, pieces are composited back-to-front with globalAlpha around 0.45–0.6 and source-over, so overlaps visibly compound color and light transmission reads through the stack. The fiber texture is overlaid via 'multiply' clipped to the piece, and a slightly lighter, thinner torn rim stroke shows the paper edge. Tissue hue tokens are additional approved colors only if supplied; otherwise they are derived as foreground #F2EEE1 tints, checked with chroma_js. No arbitrary hues are invented.

GSAP tweens per-piece transforms on the paused registered timeline: gentle sway, a drift parallax with depth-scaled offsets, and layer laydown. Every frame is redrawn from scratch.

Preview (3 s): layers settle into an underwater scene with slow overlapping drift.
Full video: extends the layer manifest.

tech.implementation:
Three.js scene on an opaque #100D09 background. The vessel is LatheGeometry from an authored amphora/krater profile curve (about 64 radial segments), so the profile stays coherent.

Canvas 2D paints a wide, seamless wrap texture:
- terracotta #BA642F ground,
- ornamental registers (meander and tongue bands) as repeated authored paths,
- a continuous narrative frieze of dark painted figure silhouettes with #F3DFC0 incised detail lines.

The texture's U axis wraps exactly once around the vessel, so the narrative is continuous. No specific historical technique is claimed.

Material: MeshStandardMaterial with moderate roughness and a subtle roughness/normal variation for a burnished surface. Soft key and rim lighting. Tone mapping is checked so terracotta stays in its family.

GSAP owns the vessel rotation and a slow camera orbit on the paused registered timeline. A narrative 'reveal' is a texture-space mask uniform that progressively paints figures in register order.

Preview (3 s): the vessel rotates about 90° as the frieze figures resolve.

tech.implementation:
Three.js stone interior: box room with MeshStandardMaterial, cool dim gray stone, high roughness and procedural Canvas grain on a #101216 dark field.

Canvas 2D paints the stained-glass image once: jewel-colored panes separated by dark leading lines. The same CanvasTexture is used twice:
- as the emissive map of the window plane, and
- as SpotLight.map behind the window, projecting that image onto the floor and walls with castShadow.

The window frame and mullions occlude the light coherently via the shadow map. This is a projected-texture approximation, not physically accurate refraction or caustics, and is stated as such.

Post: EffectComposer with RenderPass, then UnrealBloomPass (strength 0 until the finale), then OutputPass for tone mapping and sRGB.

GSAP timeline on the paused registered clock:
1. Dim stone.
2. Blackout: light intensity to 0.
3. Light up: spotlight intensity and angle sweep, and the projected pattern moves across the floor.
4. Final white bloom: bloom strength and light intensity ramp up.

All values are pure functions of time.

1. Dim stone.
2. Blackout: light intensity to 0.
3. Light up: spotlight intensity and angle sweep, and the projected pattern moves across the floor.
4. Final white bloom: bloom strength and light intensity ramp up.

All values are pure functions of time.

Preview (3 s): dim → blackout → colored projection.
Full video: adds the white bloom finale and camera moves. Coherent occlusion of colored transmitted light in an architectural space needs a 3D light with a projected texture and shadows. Using one shared texture keeps the window and its projection identical.

Alternatives considered:
- MeshPhysicalMaterial transmission is unneeded and must not imply physical refraction.
- Cycles caustics are unavailable.
- 2D overlays would fake occlusion.

Bloom is limited to the source-specified finale. Tradeoff: shadow-map softness and resolution need tuning, and the projection is an explicit approximation.

tech.implementation: Stage #101820. A procedural lens mechanism in a deterministic hierarchy: housing (steel #8196A5 PBR metal), lens elements (MeshPhysicalMaterial tinted #61D4DC, transmission approximated), retaining rings and an aperture. A cutaway uses a clipping plane with localClippingEnabled plus stencil caps or explicit cut-face geometry so there are no hollow faces. An internal light path is a TubeGeometry with #628BF4 → focus #EF9F5C as discrete segments. GSAP owns part offsets along the optical axis and a calm camera arc. SVG overlay labels are reprojected each seek with Vector3.project from part anchors. Leader lines draw with DrawSVGPlugin, and anchor dots or arrowheads (data-arrowhead-for) appear only when the stroke arrives. Label text uses data-reveal-after its caption backing (#EFF4F7 on a dark local card). 3s preview: assembled 0–0.5s → axial separation and cutaway 0.5–1.5s → held labeled path 1.5–2.4s → precise reassembly by 3s. glTF parts only if authorized assets are supplied.

styles.visual_cues: Render emissive three-dimensional flame and translucent smoke as coherent volumes with readable depth, buoyant motion, cooling soot and light spill. Maintain a stable dark or contrasting stage, bounded exposure and consistent camera scale. Do not substitute a flat glow sprite, liquid blob or unrelated particle shower for the volume.
styles.note: Added from the completed 523-entry Skillry posted-text review on 2026-10-13. Background hex values are authored defaults, not verified source tokens. Preview limitations must disclose procedural approximations.

tech.implementation:
Raw WebGL2 fullscreen triangle at a bounded internal resolution (e.g. 640×360, upscaled), fragment-shader raymarch at ≤64 primary steps and ≤6 light steps through a 3D density/emission field. The field is seeded fBm noise advected analytically upward by uTime (buoyancy and curl offsets as closed-form functions of time, no feedback buffers). The temperature field maps through an explicitly approximate ramp: flame_core #FFF0BC → flame_amber #FFAD42 → flame_orange #F05A28, then cooling into smoke #747B86 that absorbs and scatters light (Beer–Lambert). An analytic stationary hearth/ground with coal #4B403A receives flicker light spill. Background #101218, exposure clamped. GSAP's paused timeline sets uTime, uIgnite and uCool; every seek redraws one frame. 3s preview: ignition 0–0.6s → tall readable flame 0.6–2.0s → cooling translucent smoke 2.0–3.0s. The caption states it is an illustrative procedural volume, not a combustion solver. Full physically simulated shots need Blender/Cycles gas simulation with baked frames; it is unavailable here and reported as missing. The explosion recipe uses staged deterministic shock radius and debris uniforms.
Optional recipe blast_aftermath: Stage ignition/compression, expanding force, displaced material and cooling aftermath. Keep causal propagation visible across several states; never replace it with one white flash. Use deterministic or baked volume/debris trajectories and coherent environmental response.

tech.implementation: Preview (3s, 1920x1080, HyperFrames): a #EEE3BB plaster/papyrus field with fixed seeded SVG feTurbulence grain. Two or three horizontal registers sit on #3B2D23 baselines with a registered border band. Original outlined SVG figures use the canonical pose (profile head and legs, frontal shoulders and eye) and symbolic scale. Each figure is grouped as contour, flat mineral fills (red #A84532, ochre #B9793C, blue #426C88, green #738261) and pivoted limb subgroups. Timeline: 0–0.8s, DrawSVG draws contours in reading order. 0.6–1.4s, each figure's fills clip-wipe in only after its own contour completes. 1.2–2.6s, a measured procession: x-only steps along the baseline with small pivot gestures, no perspective or shadow. Then hold. Captions sit in an HTML/CSS band below the registers, contrast-checked with chroma.js. Inscription columns stay empty frames unless verified text is supplied. All tweens are fromTo, verified with direct, backward and repeated seeks. Full video: reuse the figure library across registers. Optional approved layered or rigged figure assets, or Krita-drawn gesture frames (Krita runtime unverified), are stepped by composition time inside the same register system. Live-action gait reference is for timing only, redrawn to the canonical pose. Supplied hieroglyph inscriptions are revealed after their column frames.
tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

tech.library_selection: Flat bounded fills with fine contours belong to SVG. Canvas or WebGL would lose path editability and add nothing. GSAP plus DrawSVG gives a seekable contour-then-fill order, while Anime.js or Motion would duplicate it. Rough.js, 3D and scrambled text were rejected because they break the canonical convention or invent inscriptions. Asset-based routes (layered figures, drawn frames) are valid full-video options, but the procedural SVG route is the bounded, faithful default.

tech.implementation: Preview: warm paper #F0E6C9. (1) A seeded Canvas 2D paper-fibre texture generated once, fixed, and reused as a multiply mask over the plates so grain coordinates match. sources.style_evidence: Second 7 shows flat indigo patterned waves, a vermilion sun disc, a cartouche label and warm print paper. It is a simplified pastiche rather than fine key-block linework.
sources.palette_lesson: The video is a style-switching montage. Each scene's palette comes from that scene's medium, not from one shared author palette: casino green and yellow/black hazard; blueprint blue with white line; pink halftone on off-white for comic; a near-black viewport with magenta and an iridescent shader for 3D; sky blue and brick orange for 8-bit; neutral grey with terminal green; warm paper with indigo and vermilion for the print; and white receipt paper on charcoal. What carries over is the motif (the 運 glyph plus a d6), not a colour. The medium-defining constraints are blueprint blue + white line, a limited game palette with whole pixels, flat registered print colours on paper, a dot screen with ink lines, and a dark 3D viewport. The specific yellows, greens and the warm paper tone are this author's examples. For new subjects, choose a ground per medium and scene: deep navy or teal drafting fields, overcast grey or dusk-purple game skies, cool blue-grey or rice-white print papers, newsprint grey or pale cyan comic pages, and graphite or deep green viewports. Keep the transition bands in the colours of the incoming and outgoing scenes so that the handoff reads as continuous.

tech.implementation: Preview: a river landscape on #F0E9D7 built from about 6–10k seeded short brush dabs, with per-dab width, length and angle set by a seeded PRNG and authored flow fields per region. Colors come only from the sky #9EBCC8, foliage #829C79, sunlight #D8BF7A and rose #C59D9D families plus #364747 accents. Adjacent complementary touches give optical mixing, and distant layers have softer contrast. Static layers are rasterized once into offscreen canvases. Only the water reflection (about 1.5k dabs) and one small subject are redrawn, each dab's state a pure function of time t (shimmer = sin(t·ω+phase_i) on length and sunlight mix, with bounded jitter). 0–1.0s, regional paint-on driven by a per-dab threshold against GSAP progress. 1.0–3.0s, reflection shimmer and a slight grass sway, then hold. Disclose as a procedural approximation. Full video: approved or newly painted layered painting assets (for example Krita layers, runtime unverified) can replace procedural regions, animated per layer with only local motion. Drawing-asset paint-on sequences are stepped by time. For very large dab counts, precompute dab tables offline (NumPy) or switch the renderer to PixiJS sprites while keeping the same time-derived state.
tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.

tech.library_selection: Thousands of broken marks are a Canvas workload. SVG DOM would be too heavy, and WebGL instancing adds complexity without better fidelity at this scale. p5.js and PixiJS are viable alternatives but add a lifecycle for no default gain. Animating only the reflection avoids the forbidden whole-image boil, and no blur or swirl filters are used, keeping it distinct from Post-Impressionism.

styles.visual_cues: A mostly black-and-white backstage manga in one continuous film set. Preserve white round-headed, faceless, short-bodied characters with pointed feet, bold ink outlines and halftone scenery. A persistent director speaks beside a shadowed presentation board while stage, camera, lighting, art and sound crew perform tasks supported by timed storyboard JSON. Backgrounds and boards travel right to left; crew make brief trips to work positions and return for reading holds. Use compact black name badges, readable rounded status labels and small board captions. Oval speech and thought balloons stay above the director, with extra headroom for thought circles. Use #F47B45 sparingly for playback progress, working-crew dots, brief dialogue-change underlines, equipment indicators and an optional opening-title accent. Keep the opening title optional and opening-only; never repeat title cards per scene. Default cast identity: whenever Manga Production Theatre is selected or named, use the established storyboard crew as its character reference without requiring the brief to repeat it. Figures have a large blank white circular head, a compact white cutout body with small side arm points and two pointed feet, a continuous bold black contour and no facial features, fingers or jointed skeletal limbs. Keep head/body proportions, outline weight and prop scale consistent across scenes; use short whole-figure tilts, turns and pose changes rather than substituting generic line-stick people, rounded capsule mascots or realistic humans. The director is slightly larger and remains the persistent narrator beside the board. Roles must be recognizable from their silhouettes and equipment as well as their readable badges: DIRECTOR with a clapperboard; STAGE CREW carrying a prop box; ART DEPT with an oversized pencil; LIGHTING with an adjustable lamp on a stand; SOUND wearing headphones and operating a small mixer; CAMERA with a twin-reel camera and tripod. Keep each figure attached to the same role and prop throughout the film. Show only crew with an actual task, preserving the role-specific action and idle rules; do not invent work just to fill the cast. Explicit user changes take precedence.
styles.note: Application-authored style derived from the code-driven manga storyboard viewer and user-directed revisions. Not extracted from external reference footage.

tech.implementation: Build the manga from structured timed scene/beat JSON using HTML/CSS, with SVG only where precise contours help. Use one deterministic, seekable composition clock for board/scenery travel, crew trips, equipment actions, statuses and dialogue. Plan crew roles and tasks from actual recorded props/assets, captions, camera moves, lighting and sound cues; omit unsupported specialists, never imply real production footage, and do not make a model call to animate existing JSON. Preserve the established faceless silhouette rather than adding jointed limbs. Let stagehands deliver props, artists set lettering, lighting crew adjust lights, sound crew cue effects and camera crew aim toward the board. Crew travel out, work, return and settle; pausing, replay and backward seeking reproduce the same poses and labels. Reserve separate board, dialogue and crew zones; stagger crew lanes and stack zones on narrow screens. Keep the director balloon visible, use a concise cue summary, raise thought balloons to clear their trailing circles, and briefly gesture/react only when dialogue changes. Give every board a persistent ink shadow outside its reveal mask and keep captions smaller than dialogue. Use black pill name badges, high-contrast compact rounded task labels and an orange dot only while working. Share #F47B45 with small equipment indicators and dialogue-change underlines; do not use orange for low-contrast body text, permanent reaction rays or large color washes. In an interactive viewer, center a naturally scrolling bounded stage in the content area, hide scrollbar chrome while preserving scrolling, and use orange timeline progress/thumb. Playback controls and status chrome are viewer features, not mandatory video artwork. An opening-only Glitch Type Build is optional; omit it when not requested, and never add a title card per scene. A gentle phased character wave is a visual tempo effect unless actual audio beats were analyzed. Keep export resolution, frame rate, GIF size and excerpt duration in delivery settings rather than hardcoding them into this style. Retain readable holds, exact word spacing and reduced-motion access. Rough.js adds cached sketch contours; PixiJS is optional for a complex world; Matter.js is only for baked physical props. Anime.js may replace the motion owner after seek verification. HyperFrames owns composition/export, with Remotion only for a verified limitation. Crew performance rules: Give each crew member an independent cue-based schedule with explicit idle/frozen, travel, work, react and settle intervals; one shared seekable clock does not mean synchronized movement. Stage crew make a quick delivery and stop after placing a prop; art crew work deliberately on a lettering/drawing cue and freeze once it is readable; lighting crew make a short adjustment then hold the light steady; sound crew make a brief cue-triggered control action and then wait; camera crew use a slower smooth tracking move only during the recorded camera action, aiming at the board, then lock off. Stagger starts, travel duration, task duration and return timing by role so some crew remain still while others work; never make everyone run, bounce or react on every beat. Idle characters stay fully still, especially during reading holds; omit unsupported specialists. Reactions are short and motivated by a new instruction, reveal, impact or completion. A shout-out is a brief visual callout only for an explicit action/cut, warning or meaningful payoff, never every caption and never invented audible speech; keep callouts away from the board and director dialogue. Keep the director dialogue visible while its text updates; at a new cue, allow a subtle 1–3 degree head nod or turn toward the board, optionally a small body gesture, then settle. Preserve the faceless round-head silhouette without adding facial features or jointed limbs. Orange reaction marks appear briefly only with a reaction, not for the entire dialogue interval. Store each role's timed actions, pauses, reactions and callouts in deterministic code derived from storyboard cues; do not add unvalidated fields to STORYBOARD.json. Preview the same conditional acting language in a concise sample, rather than uniformly animating every character. Verify that unsupported and idle crew stay frozen, role timings differ, gestures end, callouts do not overlap, and direct/backward seeking recreates the same character states. Default character construction: start from the same reusable storyboard crew silhouette for every role, then attach the role-specific prop. Build a blank round head and a short pointed white body with bold black contours; hide the head/body seam so the cutout reads as one coherent figure. Do not replace it with thin line arms and legs, add a face or improvise a new mascot per scene. Keep separate head, body and prop groups only for controlled posing; no articulated human rig is required. Give the director a clapperboard, stage crew a box, art crew a pencil, lighting crew a lamp and stand, sound crew headphones and a mixer, and camera crew a twin-reel camera on a tripod. Assign stable role IDs and reuse their geometry, proportions, badge style and equipment across shots. Map each role to its existing independent cue-based schedule; the prop action must match the role. Describe the chosen crew and their tasks in the normal storyboard scene descriptions without adding new schema fields. Credits names, monogram avatars and contributions are replaceable content, separate from the crew role; a personal avatar must not silently replace the theatre figure. In every implementation, inspect an overview and a work pose to confirm the same silhouette, identifiable equipment, readable role badge, clear board/dialogue zones and idle crew remaining still. Copy the supplied CSS and role markup before animating; do not redraw the cast from the prose alone or substitute another stickman. Preserve the exact head/body contours, proportions, bold outlines and role-prop geometry. Uniform scaling, deterministic posing and scene placement are allowed; a non-DOM renderer must faithfully port this geometry rather than inventing replacement characters. Keep timeline-driven idle, work and reaction behavior consistent with the performance rules. This metadata contains all required drawing code; no application source files or imports are needed.

Use black pill name badges, high-contrast compact rounded task labels and an orange dot only while working. Share #F47B45 with small equipment indicators and dialogue-change underlines; do not use orange for low-contrast body text, permanent reaction rays or large color washes. In an interactive viewer, center a naturally scrolling bounded stage in the content area, hide scrollbar chrome while preserving scrolling, and use orange timeline progress/thumb. Playback controls and status chrome are viewer features, not mandatory video artwork. An opening-only Glitch Type Build is optional; omit it when not requested, and never add a title card per scene. A gentle phased character wave is a visual tempo effect unless actual audio beats were analyzed. Keep export resolution, frame rate, GIF size and excerpt duration in delivery settings rather than hardcoding them into this style. Retain readable holds, exact word spacing and reduced-motion access. Rough.js adds cached sketch contours; PixiJS is optional for a complex world; Matter.js is only for baked physical props. Anime.js may replace the motion owner after seek verification. HyperFrames owns composition/export, with Remotion only for a verified limitation. Crew performance rules: Give each crew member an independent cue-based schedule with explicit idle/frozen, travel, work, react and settle intervals; one shared seekable clock does not mean synchronized movement. Stage crew make a quick delivery and stop after placing a prop; art crew work deliberately on a lettering/drawing cue and freeze once it is readable; lighting crew make a short adjustment then hold the light steady; sound crew make a brief cue-triggered control action and then wait; camera crew use a slower smooth tracking move only during the recorded camera action, aiming at the board, then lock off. Stagger starts, travel duration, task duration and return timing by role so some crew remain still while others work; never make everyone run, bounce or react on every beat. Idle characters stay fully still, especially during reading holds; omit unsupported specialists. Reactions are short and motivated by a new instruction, reveal, impact or completion. A shout-out is a brief visual callout only for an explicit action/cut, warning or meaningful payoff, never every caption and never invented audible speech; keep callouts away from the board and director dialogue. Keep the director dialogue visible while its text updates; at a new cue, allow a subtle 1–3 degree head nod or turn toward the board, optionally a small body gesture, then settle. Preserve the faceless round-head silhouette without adding facial features or jointed limbs. Orange reaction marks appear briefly only with a reaction, not for the entire dialogue interval. Store each role's timed actions, pauses, reactions and callouts in deterministic code derived from storyboard cues; do not add unvalidated fields to STORYBOARD.json. Preview the same conditional acting language in a concise sample, rather than uniformly animating every character. Verify that unsupported and idle crew stay frozen, role timings differ, gestures end, callouts do not overlap, and direct/backward seeking recreates the same character states. Build a blank round head and a short pointed white body with bold black contours; hide the head/body seam so the cutout reads as one coherent figure. Give the director a clapperboard, stage crew a box, art crew a pencil, lighting crew a lamp and stand, sound crew headphones and a mixer, and camera crew a twin-reel camera on a tripod. In every implementation, inspect an overview and a work pose to confirm the same silhouette, identifiable equipment, readable role badge, clear board/dialogue zones and idle crew remaining still.

styles.visual_cues: Cassette Futurism: the 1970s–80s imagined spaceship and mission-control console, a hardware-first branch of Retrofuturism rather than cyberpunk, vaporwave or Y2K. Compose a modular dashboard of chunky charcoal and olive panels set into beige plastic cases with visible screws, seams, vents and black or white embossed labels, banded by restrained amber, orange and rust livery stripes. Recessed black CRT screens glow in ONE phosphor per screen — green #74FF9A or amber #FFB23E — with modest scanlines, soft glow, a screen-bounded vignette and seeded deterministic noise. Use monospace or pixel-like type from locally available system mono fonts: condensed uppercase panel labels such as NAV, PWR and SYS, numbers, timecodes and segmented readouts. Physical hardware carries the scene: cassette tape reels and transport, toggles, knobs, square keys and indicator lamps. Red appears only for warnings. Motion is typed text, 12fps stepped hardware actions, a brief boot flicker and short channel-static transitions that resolve into readable holds. Avoid continuous strobing, smooth generic easing, pink or purple neon, glassmorphism, gradient blobs and round flat cards.
styles.note: Authored by Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5) on 2026-10-18 from a user-specified creative brief; not extracted from external reference footage. A distinct, period-specific branch of Retrofuturism (style-065) fixed to 1970s–80s spaceship console hardware, which applies CRT / Analog Video Effects (style-066) only as a screen-bounded display treatment. Not Cyberpunk, Vaporwave or Y2K Design.

tech.implementation: Build each console as real hardware modules, not a flat UI: HTML/CSS grid or absolute layout for module placement and real text; SVG for beige cases, charcoal/olive panels, screws, seams, vents, embossed label plates, livery stripes, cassette window, reels, tape path, heads, toggles, knobs, square keys, lamps and seven-segment readouts; Canvas 2D only for seeded screen noise when SVG specks are insufficient. Use code-drawn geometry only; no external images, photographs or downloaded fonts. Set type with generic monospace or locally installed system mono fonts and verify fallback metrics; give CRT text a fixed character advance (for example textLength per typed substring) so typing never reflows. Panel labels are condensed uppercase (horizontal scale or narrow mono) with letter spacing; embossing is a 1px offset highlight or shadow copy, not a glow. CRT treatment (the style-066 CRT / Analog Video Effects vocabulary, confined to screen glass): one phosphor per screen, green #74FF9A or amber #FFB23E on a near-black screen; scanlines about 3–4px apart at 720p at modest opacity; a short blur glow merged under sharp glyphs; a radial vignette clipped to the rounded screen; static noise from a seeded generator evaluated by 12fps step index, never Math.random or wall clock. Keep scanlines, glow, noise and vignette inside the bezel and keep phosphor text at or above 4.5:1 on the composited screen. Red is warning-only: master caution lamps, fault legends and alarm readouts, paired with a text label; never stripes, titles, idle lamps or decoration. Motion: derive every visual state from absolute composition time quantized to 12 steps per second (step = floor(time × 12)); hold each pose for the whole step instead of tweening with smooth generic easing. Toggles and keys snap within one step; knobs turn in detents; tape reels rotate by fixed angles per step at different rates as the supply pack shrinks and the take-up pack grows; counters, timecodes and segmented gauges step to new values. Typewriter text reveals characters in order beside a block cursor, then holds the completed line. A boot flicker lasts at most a few steps (about 0.3s) and never repeats as a strobe. A channel-static transition between screen pages lasts about three steps (≈0.25s): a bounded band of seeded static and a small horizontal line offset inside the bezel, then a stable readable page. Allow full reading holds after typing and after each page change; vary quick snaps with deliberate holds; do not animate everything at once. Build a single time-state function that returns every module's pose and readout for an arbitrary time, apply it to the scene from one paused seekable timeline, and verify identical frames for forward, backward and direct seeks, including a fresh page. Provide reduced-motion access by replacing flicker and static with plain cuts. Keep export resolution, frame rate and file size in delivery settings; the 12fps cadence is animation quantization, not the delivery frame rate. Relationship: this is a period-specific branch of Retrofuturism (style-065) that fixes the era to 1970s–80s console hardware, and it uses CRT / Analog Video Effects (style-066) only as the screen-bounded display treatment. Do not drift into cyberpunk, vaporwave or Y2K vocabulary. HyperFrames owns composition/export, with Remotion only for a verified limitation.
alternatives: Canvas 2D for seeded per-step screen noise
Scrambled Text Reveal for a brief seeded resolve after channel static
Remotion for a verified export limitation
tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
framework_selection.scope: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

tech.library_selection: Prefer HTML/CSS and SVG for the console hardware and readouts, with Canvas 2D only for seeded screen noise. GSAP owns one paused timeline that drives a time-state function quantized to 12fps; HyperFrames owns export. Do not bundle extra tools, 3D engines or shader stacks to imitate the look.

motion_guidance.application: Preserve deliberate 12fps stepped hardware motion: toggles snap, knobs detent, reels advance by fixed angles, counters step, text types with a block cursor. Keep boot flicker and channel static brief and resolve into readable holds.
motion_guidance.cadence_guidance: This style intentionally replaces smooth generic easing with stepped holds. Quantize visual state to 12 steps per second while rendering at the delivery frame rate; vary quick snaps with sustained reading holds and never strobe continuously.
motion_guidance.implementation: Evaluate every module from absolute composition time through one pure time-state function; maintain a single owner per property and verify forward, backward and direct seeks produce identical frames.

candidates.usage_guidance: Typewriter CRT readouts: a block cursor advances character by character at the 12fps stepped cadence on a fixed monospace grid, then the completed line holds long enough to read. Fits boot logs, mission status and telemetry lines on the console screen.

Instrument readouts build from one authored data state: screen grid and labels first, then segmented gauges, seven-segment numbers and timecodes step to their values together, then hold. No decorative drift between steps.

Adapt only as a brief channel-static cut between CRT screen pages: about three 12fps steps of seeded static band and small horizontal line offset clipped inside the bezel, then a stable readable page. Never apply it to the console hardware or repeat it as a strobe; use a plain cut for reduced motion.

styles.visual_cues: Terminal Lyric Duotone Anime: a flat anime music-video grammar in which every composition sits on a CRT-style terminal screen and the subject is read as data. Despite the traditional 'Duotone' name it is a strict three-ink tritone: ultramarine, cream and near-black as hard-edged posterized flat shapes with no gradients, rendered shading or soft airbrush; supplied anime character and scene illustrations appear mostly as held poses staged like cutouts (slow push, rotation, scale, translucent hologram states). Red is a reserved accent for warnings and dark emotional peaks only, used briefly; a whole-frame negative inversion or a short red palette swap may mark one peak. Frame every shot with a mild CRT finish: an oval dark vignette, fine scanlines, seeded grain and thin corner brackets, a §NN section header at top centre and a small audio meter at bottom left. Captions are bilingual monospace lines at the bottom (English above, Chinese below) whose characters resolve from seeded scrambled glyphs into the exact copy with a fine underline that grows like a progress bar; keywords are tinted signal blue (or red at warning beats). One keyword per section may be promoted to a large hero title that enters with a brief RGB-offset split and settles inside a thin elliptical ring. HUD overlays — detection boxes, specimen cards, feature maps, scan percentages, counters — annotate the subject with authored, labelled-illustrative data. Cut to a new composition every few seconds with plain cuts or brief glitch cuts, then hold long enough to read. Avoid gradients, glossy cel shading, neon rainbow palettes, continuous glitching, strobing flashes and illegible microtext.
styles.note: Authored by Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5) on 2026-10-18 from Claude Opus 5.5's frame analysis of a user-supplied anime-style music video (1 fps overview plus six 6 fps dense windows; no audio, no transcription). The entry records reusable visual and caption rules only: the source character, creature, song, lyrics, artwork and title are content, are not reproduced and must not be imitated. Colour values are authored defaults, not measured source hex. The traditional 'Duotone' label is kept, but the ink system is a blue/cream/black tritone with a reserved red accent. Related to Anime (style-033), CRT / Analog Video Effects (style-066), Glitch Art (style-067), Kinetic Typography (style-093) and Futuristic UI (FUI) / HUD Design (style-112), none of which fixes the three inks, red reservation, terminal frame layout and bilingual decode-caption grammar together. Review record: assets/catalog/reviews/terminal-lyric-anime.json.

tech.implementation: Separate three layers. (1) Artwork: use supplied, rights-cleared anime character and scene illustrations, or purpose-drawn original art, already in the three inks; posterize existing art to ultramarine/cream/near-black only when the user is authorised to alter it. Do not generate character animation in code: stage held poses as cutouts with slow push, rotation, scale and opacity, and pre-render any drawn in-betweens. A code-drawn bust or silhouette is acceptable only as a clearly labelled illustrative placeholder. Never claim AI-generated or reference footage. (2) Frame and HUD (HTML/CSS and SVG, Canvas 2D for grain): a CRT finish of an elliptical radial vignette, scanlines about 3px apart at modest opacity and seeded grain evaluated from a frame or step index, never Math.random or wall clock; thin cream corner brackets; a §NN section header at top centre; a small audio meter at bottom left whose bars come from authored or seeded per-step levels (do not claim beat sync without measured audio). Detection boxes, specimen cards and counters use cream hairlines on near-black with monospace labels; mark invented data illustrative. (3) Typography and motion (GSAP paused timeline, Scrambled Text Reveal or a cached seeded glyph table): bilingual captions in a monospace English line over a CJK line from locally available system fonts (verify glyph coverage; use @font-face local() names, never downloaded fonts). Each character shows a seeded scrambled glyph until reveal_i = t0 + i·dt, then the exact character; the underline length equals caption progress; keyword spans take signal blue. Hold the resolved caption long enough to read. A keyword hero title reuses Glitch Type Build (motion-036): enter with a decaying RGB offset (red and blue copies offset by a few pixels, scale settling to 1), then draw a thin cream ellipse ring around the settled title. HUD readouts build with Data Build (motion-030), scene changes use plain cuts or a brief seeded Glitch Cut (motion-020), closing code can use Terminal Typing (motion-022), and searching or erasing beats may use Rotating Sonar-Sweep Reveal (motion-047) or Pixel-Tile Materialize & Targeted Delete (motion-048). Red stays reserved for warnings and peaks; limit negative inversions and flash montages to brief, photosensitivity-safe events (no more than about three flashes per second). Derive every state from absolute composition time through one pure time-state function with one owner per property, and verify identical frames for forward, backward and direct seeks, including a fresh page. Twirl distortion or radial motion blur, if requested, needs a WebGL/GLSL shader or pre-rendered frames. Relationship: narrower than Anime (style-033) by fixing three inks and the terminal caption grammar; borrows CRT / Analog Video Effects (style-066) only as a mild finishing layer and Glitch Art (style-067) only at transitions; its HUD is narrative, unlike functional Futuristic UI (style-112). Export settings stay in the project's renderer and delivery settings.
alternatives: Canvas 2D for seeded grain and dot-matrix or tile effects
Cached seeded glyph tables instead of ScrambleTextPlugin when plugin seeking is unstable
WebGL/GLSL shader or pre-rendered frames for twirl or radial-blur transitions
Remotion for a verified export limitation
tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
framework_selection.scope: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

tech.library_selection: Prefer supplied three-ink illustrations for characters and scenes, HTML/CSS and SVG for the screen frame, HUD and captions, and Canvas 2D for seeded grain and pixel effects. GSAP owns one paused timeline driving a pure time-state function; captions resolve through Scrambled Text Reveal or an equivalent cached seeded glyph table. Do not add 3D engines or shader stacks unless a twirl or blur transition is explicitly required.

motion_guidance.application: Held illustration poses staged as cutouts; captions decode character by character with a growing underline; one keyword per section becomes a ringed hero title; HUD readouts build from authored data; scene changes are plain or brief glitch cuts followed by readable holds.
motion_guidance.cadence_guidance: Change composition every few seconds as the content requires, not on every beat. Scramble glyphs can step at about 12 changes per second while transforms stay smooth; give resolved captions and titles a settled reading hold. Keep glitch, inversion and red swaps brief and never strobe.
motion_guidance.implementation: Evaluate every layer from absolute composition time through one pure time-state function; seed all scramble, grain and glitch choices; maintain a single owner per property and verify forward, backward and direct seeks.

style_renderer.selection_basis: Use visual_cues and tech.implementation for styles, or the selected style and this pattern implementation for motion recipes. Select by visual fidelity and medium, not pipeline availability.

motion_engine.selection_basis: Use the authored action, style cadence, trajectory, material behavior, and simulation requirements. Select one owner for each animated property.

values.style_application: Assemble the supplied illustrations, CRT frame, HUD and captions and export them; keep the time-state renderer and do not replace the three-ink artwork with framework defaults.
Caption and header layout with real text: monospace English over a CJK line from local system fonts, keyword spans, the progress underline, §NN header and readable reading order.

Screen frame and HUD: corner brackets, detection boxes, specimen cards, audio meter, the elliptical hero-title ring, scanline pattern and vignette; flat three-ink placeholder shapes when no artwork is supplied.
Seeded CRT grain, dot-matrix or tile effects evaluated from frame or step index inside the screen; never Math.random, requestAnimationFrame loops or wall-clock time.
One paused, seekable timeline advances a composition clock; a pure time-state function sets caption decode, underline progress, title RGB offset and ring, HUD values and cutout transforms.
Bilingual caption decode: seeded scrambled glyphs resolve left to right into the exact copy, then hold. Preserve word spacing and final text; cache the glyph sequence if plugin seeking is unstable.

Supplied or purpose-drawn three-ink character and scene illustrations with transparency, staged as held cutout poses. Inspect rights and ink count before use; never imply generated or reference footage.
Verify cream and signal-blue caption text on composited near-black, cream on ultramarine, and warning red on near-black after scanlines, grain and vignette. Keep the three inks plus reserved red.
Conditional composition/export fallback only for a verified HyperFrames limitation; keep the same artwork, captions and time-state function.

motion_references.selection_policy: Optional candidates are screened for natural style compatibility. Before selection, inspect the actual scene illustration, assets, geometry and narrative beat. Keep only references whose defining action is supported by that scene. Choosing no reference is valid. Do not infer motion from a similar label; do not replace the existing style motion direction.

candidates.usage_guidance: Keyword hero titles: the promoted lyric keyword enters with a decaying RGB-offset split and scale settle, then a thin cream ellipse ring draws around the settled title and holds. Repeated word stamps at scattered positions are a layout parameter of the same motion.
HUD readouts that read the subject as data: detection box and callout lines first, then scan percentage or counter values step to authored targets and hold; label invented data illustrative.
Adapt as a brief timeline-driven glitch cut between compositions: one or two seeded slice frames, optionally red-tinted at a warning beat, then a clean readable frame. Never continuous or strobing.
Closing or opening code lines on the terminal screen: cursor typing on a fixed monospace grid in cream, then a reading hold. Lyric captions use the scramble decode instead, not a cursor.

Searching or closing beats: one clockwise sector beam around a fixed pivot over a held three-ink illustration, clear inside and dark dot matrix outside, with the caption and header kept readable above the mask.

Loading or erasing a character: tiles of one supplied illustration converge into the full image, or a red selection box deletes fixed cells of a memory grid while a terminal progress bar in the caption advances; cells stay empty.

motion_references.agent_instruction: Read the actual illustration and complete pattern description, motion_sequence and video_adaptation. Identify which scene elements implement that action. Reject unsupported geometry, absent subjects, unintended depth, broken contact points or unrelated interactions. Select none when no candidate fits; use restrained style-native motion instead. Preserve authored transforms, fixed backgrounds and reading layers. For an opening or gallery demo, prefer motion-016 when separable illustration and text layers exist; animate both focal objects and meaningful lettering.

palette.direction: A dark CRT screen around flat three-ink art: ultramarine, cream and near-black, with signal blue for on-screen keyword text and red reserved for warnings and peaks.
constraints: Choose the screen surround from the scene; #06070B is an illustrative swatch. The artwork itself stays three inks: ultramarine #2747C8, cream #F1E8D2 and near-black #0D0F16, as flat hard-edged shapes with no gradients.
Signal blue #7A93FF is the lit on-screen form of ultramarine for keyword text, HUD lines and rings on near-black; it is not an additional fill ink for artwork.
Reserve warning red #F0473A for warnings, deletions, RGB-offset accents and dark emotional peaks, used briefly and paired with text or shape so meaning does not rely on colour.
A negative inversion or red palette swap may mark one peak; keep it brief and photosensitivity-safe.
Scanlines, grain and vignette stay mild and must keep caption text at or above 4.5:1 on the composited frame.
Approved artwork and brand colours take precedence; posterize supplied art only when authorised.

gradient.instruction: No gradients in artwork or HUD. The only permitted gradient is the elliptical CRT vignette over the whole screen.

suggested_text_pairs.use: Caption, header and HUD text on the screen.
Keyword spans and HUD accents on near-black.
Warning labels on near-black; recheck after grain.
Cream text or highlights on ultramarine fills.
Ink text on cream panels or specimen cards.
Text near the vignette edge.

contrast_checks.limitation: Two-color checks only. Not a guarantee of complete accessibility or readability over images, textures, glass, video, outlines or animated lighting. Recheck every actual foreground/background pairing in representative frames.

palette.composition_guidance: One held illustration as the primary focus, usually centred or offset with negative space for the hero title. Caption block centred in the bottom safe area, §NN header top centre, audio meter bottom left, corner brackets at the frame corners and at most one HUD panel or detection box competing with the subject.
palette.agent_instruction: Resolve colors in this order: task-provided exact palette, established brand or approved source palette, existing semantic color mappings, then this optional example. Read visual_cues and palette.constraints. Preserve approved anchor values, color families, ink counts and asset colors. Use chroma-js for validation, equivalent normalization and contrast assessment; evaluate gradients only when enabled and appropriate. Select readable token pairs from contrast_checks, otherwise move text onto an existing contrasting backing. Record the resolved tokens and inspect actual composited frames before rendering.

audio_direction.prompt: Optional electronic or synth-pop song, instrumental bed, sparse UI blips and glitch accents tied to visible cuts, or silence, according to the brief. Captions follow delivered vocals only when timing is measured; do not claim beat sync, invent lyrics or imitate a specific song or singer. The catalog preview is silent.
suggestion_dimensions: Whether background music is useful, and its suggested mood, texture, energy, tempo range, and progression.
Whether voiceover helps explain the topic, and its suggested language, tone, pace, and placement.
Whether sung vocals support the topic or distract from narration and essential text.
Whether sound effects, ambience, or silence clarify key actions, transitions, and reading holds.
How audio changes across scenes, supports motion cadence, and leaves space for speech and comprehension.
audio_direction.selection_guidance: Treat these as task-specific suggestions, not requirements to include every audio layer. Honor explicit user audio choices and supplied assets. When inputs are absent, propose a coherent direction and state assumptions; do not silently default to instrumental music or invent available audio assets.

Use render_pipeline to assemble, synchronize, mix, and export audio with picture. Keep speech intelligible, avoid clipping and competing vocals, and inspect the delivered audio and picture together.

Red only at warning beats.

styles.visual_cues: Particle Flow Network: a stable node-link diagram in which transfer is shown as streams of fine particles travelling along curved connections between circular hubs. Hubs sit in branching clusters around one or a few primary nodes; node size and a soft halo carry importance, and a small set of semantic state accents (active, idle, waiting, fault) mark status alongside text labels. A sparse dotted field and a quiet dark or paper-light surround keep the graph legible. Particle density, direction and speed communicate volume and flow; the layout itself does not drift. Typography is compact and technical: short node names with small secondary metadata in a monospace or neat sans. Applies to knowledge maps, biological pathways, logistics routes, team collaboration and cause-and-effect systems, not only software. Avoid neon rainbow networking clichés, random floating dots with no source or destination, dashboard chrome without a graph, crowded unreadable labels and constant flashing.
styles.note: Authored by Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5) on 2026-10-20 from observation of two user-supplied screenshots and four chronological frames of a 7-second, 84-frame GIF: https://github.com/tomtomsatnav/agent-orchestration-standard/blob/main/docs/screenshots/01-graph-dark.png, https://github.com/tomtomsatnav/agent-orchestration-standard/blob/main/docs/screenshots/02-graph-light.png and https://github.com/tomtomsatnav/agent-orchestration-standard/blob/main/docs/hero.gif. The entry records reusable visual and motion rules only; no source code, layout, labels, data, product name or branding is reused. Colour values are illustrative defaults, not measured source hex. Related to Particle Art (style-062), Scientific Visualization / Data Storytelling (style-097) and Futuristic UI (FUI) / HUD Design (style-112), none of which fixes a stable node-link layout with particle streams that carry meaningful source-to-destination transfer.

tech.implementation: Author the graph first: a fixed node list (id, position, radius, cluster, state) and an edge list with an explicit source, destination and curve (quadratic or cubic Bézier control points), sized for video with roughly 7-20 visible nodes and labels that never overlap streams. Render the dotted field, edges, halos, nodes and labels in SVG or HTML/CSS; draw particles in Canvas 2D (or SVG for low counts). Each particle has a seeded edge, phase, lateral offset and size; its position is p = curve(edge, frac(phase + t·speed)) plus a perpendicular offset that narrows near both endpoints so streams leave and enter nodes cleanly. Evaluate everything from absolute composition time with a seeded PRNG; never Math.random, wall clock or free-running loops. Script beats as states of one timeline: activation (source halo and state accent rise), transfer (stream density ramps along the edge), arrival (particles converge, destination pulses once, counter or label updates), settle (density returns to idle level) and overview (hold the whole graph readable). Node emphasis changes by halo, ring and fill, not by moving nodes. Mark any counts or states as authored or illustrative unless the user supplies measured data; never imply live telemetry. Use one owner per animated property and verify identical frames for forward, backward and direct seeks. Use the user's chosen renderer when specified.
alternatives: SVG dotted strokes (stroke-dasharray with round caps and animated dash offset) for low particle counts or static frames
Pre-sampled curve lookup tables cached per edge instead of evaluating Bézier math per particle
PixiJS or WebGL point rendering only when particle counts exceed what Canvas 2D can draw at the target frame rate
tech.render_pipeline: Uses the project's renderer setting. Motion Graphic recommendations select visual and motion tools, not the composition or export framework.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

framework_selection.scope: Composition and export follow the project setting.

tech.library_selection: Use SVG or HTML/CSS for the field, edges, nodes, halos and labels, Canvas 2D for seeded particle streams, and GSAP for one paused timeline that drives a pure time-state function. Use chroma-js to validate label and state colours against the actual surround. Do not add a 3D engine, physics engine or force-directed layout at render time; author or precompute positions.

motion_guidance.application: Particles travel source to destination along fixed curves; hubs signal activation with a halo and state accent, streams thicken during transfer, destinations pulse once on arrival, then the graph settles and holds for an overview.
motion_guidance.cadence_guidance: Run one primary transfer at a time, a few seconds each, with a readable hold after arrival. Keep particle motion continuous and smooth, halos easing over roughly half a second or more, and avoid simultaneous pulses or flashing; idle streams stay sparse.
motion_guidance.implementation: Evaluate particle positions, densities, halos and labels from absolute composition time through one pure time-state function; seed every random choice and keep one owner per property; verify forward, backward and direct seeks.

style_renderer.selection_basis: Use visual_cues and tech.implementation for styles, or the selected style and this pattern implementation for motion recipes. Select by visual fidelity and medium, not pipeline availability.

motion_engine.selection_basis: Use the authored action, style cadence, trajectory, material behavior, and simulation requirements. Select one owner for each animated property.

values.style_application: Node labels, secondary metadata, legends and titles as real text in compact technical type; place labels clear of streams and keep reading order.
Dotted field, curved edges, node rings, halos and state accents; dotted round-cap strokes for static frames or sparse streams.
Seeded particle streams sampled along authored curves from composition time, with endpoint-tapered spread and density ramps; no requestAnimationFrame loops or wall clock.
One paused, seekable timeline advances the clock; the time-state function sets stream density, halo intensity, node state and label updates for activation, transfer, arrival, settle and overview.
Check label, metadata and state-accent colours against the composited surround in both variants; verify state accents remain distinguishable and paired with text.

Use one owner per animated property and verify identical frames for forward, backward and direct seeks. Use the user's chosen renderer when specified.
