styles.visual_cues: Vintage Rubber Hose Animation: early sound-era hand-inked cel cartoons. Strong, irregular ink silhouettes and organic, slightly imperfect contours vary in line weight. Build focal subjects from interlocking asymmetrical drawn masses, varied contour rhythms, angular and curved features, overlapping forms, inset details and coherent perspective. Resolve secondary structure at delivery size while keeping the silhouette readable. Colour the hand-inked forms with flat cel fills and bold painterly or cel shadow masses, preserving articulated geometry and surface planes. Where scenery is present, stage foreground silhouettes, midground subjects and receding background planes with distinct light/dark values, atmospheric separation and restrained parallax. Integrate directional light, contact shadows and selective edge highlights into the drawn forms. Distribute dense detail around the focal action and quieter shapes around reading areas. Scenery and architecture must be expressive, warped and asymmetric, with leaning shapes and layered atmosphere. Environmental acting is mandatory wherever scenery is present: architecture rocks and its structural parts flex or skew, while trees sway and their branches move independently. Adapt these behaviours to the chosen setting, with deliberate readable holds; a static environment with only moving texture does not satisfy this style. When characters appear, they may be any original human, animal, robot, object or environmental subject, built from rounded elastic masses with curved, jointless rubber-hose limbs and broad theatrical expressions; keep one consistent design per project and never resemble an existing cartoon character or mascot. Shots without characters, such as landscapes or buildings, are equally valid, and architecture need not become round. Motion is hand-drawn acting: expressive elastic poses, anticipation, squash and stretch, overshoot, curved arcs and playful, rhythmic, jazz-like timing, with readable holds and no mandatory perpetual bounce. Drawings are stepped, typically 12 unique drawings per second against a 24 fps film reference, adapted to the project's delivery settings. Use charcoal ink, muted grey and brown middle values, aged ivory light accents and deliberate dark shadow masses as the default tonal structure. Recolour only when explicitly requested for this style's assigned scenes, preserving the defined tonal contrast; palettes assigned to other scenes must not bleed into this style. The only optional effects, used only where a project needs them, are film wear and a vintage film-leader countdown. Avoid clean corporate vector icons with grain pasted on top, neon, glossy gradients, modern 3D rendering, photorealism and fixed-grid pixel art unless explicitly requested.
styles.note: Authored by Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5) on 2026-10-21 from a user-supplied example brief and user-provided reference images (a cartoon drawing, a film leader and a description of rubber-hose traits); only stylistic properties were extracted, and no depicted characters, buildings, compositions, text or images are reused. Not application-authored. Self-contained visual metadata revised on 2026-10-23. The written drawing, tonal and acting requirements define the reusable style for any original subject or setting. Sample subjects and sequences are optional examples. Distinct from Rubber Hose Animation (style-034) and related to Traditional Cel Animation (style-081).

tech.implementation: Core drawing (always): Build focal subjects from interlocking asymmetrical drawn masses, varied contour rhythms, angular and curved features, overlapping forms, inset details and coherent perspective. Resolve secondary structure at delivery size while keeping the silhouette readable. Colour the hand-inked forms with flat cel fills and bold painterly or cel shadow masses, preserving articulated geometry and surface planes. Where scenery is present, stage foreground silhouettes, midground subjects and receding background planes with distinct light/dark values, atmospheric separation and restrained parallax. Integrate directional light, contact shadows and selective edge highlights into the drawn forms. Distribute dense detail around the focal action and quieter shapes around reading areas. Construct an original staged illustration from the subject, story and supplied project assets, using this written metadata as the complete visual contract. Scenery and architecture must have expressive warped, leaning or asymmetric construction suited to the subject. Build depth from layered atmospheric planes with subtle parallax. Environmental acting is mandatory wherever scenery is present: rock architecture about its base and flex or skew structural parts; sway trees and animate branches independently. Give equivalent scenery elements their own restrained elastic squash, sway or lean cues in other settings. Author explicit environmental key poses and readable holds; moving texture alone is insufficient. Author the artwork as drawn vector shapes or supplied hand-drawn cels, not generic icons with texture added afterwards. Characters (only when present): adopt or design the project's original subject (human, animal, robot, object or environmental) on one construction sheet: rounded elastic masses, a root that squashes and stretches about its contact point, curved jointless hose limbs drawn as single quadratic or cubic strokes with an ink outline and inner fill, simple hands or ends and replaceable features. Species, costume, occupation, props and shape come from the project. Keep proportions, line weight, colours and costume consistent, note the identity in the storyboard, and reject designs that resemble existing cartoon characters or mascots. Shots without characters are valid. Acting and time: author key drawings (anticipation, squash, stretch, overshoot, settle) on curved arcs rather than continuous tweens, with rhythmic timing and readable holds; idle sway is optional. Derive state from absolute composition time: drawing = floor(time × 12) by default, and a project may choose another drawing rate. Never derive state from a frame counter, so the stepped cadence survives any delivery frame rate (24 fps holds each drawing two frames, 30 fps alternates two and three, 60 fps holds five). Keep delivery resolution, frame rate and duration in the project's settings. Seed every random choice; never Math.random, wall clock or free-running loops. Use one owner per animated property and verify that forward, backward and direct seeks give identical frames. Colour and type: Use charcoal ink, muted grey and brown middle values, aged ivory light accents and deliberate dark shadow masses as the default tonal structure. Preserve the project's exact copy. Recolour only when explicitly requested for these scenes, retaining the defined tonal contrast, flat fills and opacity; keep branding and palettes assigned to other scenes confined to those scenes. A monochrome-to-colour progression is an optional storytelling choice. Cartoon titles and captions use real text in a locally available face chosen for the project; this does not apply to optional film-leader numerals. Drawing acceptance: inspect representative rendered frames at delivery size for articulated focal silhouettes, varied ink weight, overlapping structural details, distinct depth planes where scenery exists, directional shadow masses and controlled highlights. Review the drawn forms with optional surface effects disabled so their structure, lighting and depth remain legible on their own. Inspect motion over time for independent environmental acting, stepped key poses and readable holds. Refine the affected artwork before assembly when these features are missing. Optional effects (only when a project needs them): Film wear: treat it as photographic film material separate from the cartoon artwork. Apply seeded grain, flecks, dust, hairs, thin vertical scratches, subtle exposure variation, slight registration drift and whole-plate gate weave to the entire frame, stepped from a film frame index such as floor(time × 24); optional line boil cycles two or three contour variants of the cartoon artwork only. Vintage film-leader countdown: a separate photographic plate with mechanically precise, centred concentric registration circles and thin crosshair lines fixed relative to each other; large, pale, bold sans-serif numerals with clear breathing room over a darker coordinated ground; a broad, darker, translucent clock-wipe sector rotating behind the numeral and rings; grain, vertical scratches, dust and exposure variation. Gate weave moves the whole plate, never individual rings. Do not give the leader cartoon ink outlines, line boil, serif numerals, decorative paper borders or wobbly circles. Present it as a creative hybrid of historical leaders, not a strict historical reconstruction, and keep any exposure flashes partial and at most three per second. Offer a reduced-motion version with plain cuts. Composition and export use the project's renderer setting. Relationship: Rubber Hose Animation (style-034) is a broader normalized label from a modern retro reference; this entry fixes early hand-inked cel drawing, stepped cadence and the optional film wear and film-leader countdown. It borrows Traditional Cel Animation (style-081) drawing discipline.

suggestions.rationale: Traditional cel discipline keeps linework and flat fills consistent across drawn frames.
suggestions.best_for: Pieces where supplied or drawn cels replace coded drawings.
suggestions.video_application: Composite one cel drawing per step over the coded scene, matching ink weight and palette.
suggestions.html_application: Swap cel images from the same drawing index on a seekable timeline, with a static pose for reduced motion.

Keep one stepped drawing index.

Mark invented values as illustrative.

styles.visual_cues: Pixel RPG Quest Explainer: a technical or educational explainer staged as a game run in which game-progression UI is the narrative scaffold and every progress element carries meaning. Defining grammar: (1) a persistent HUD that keeps its position across scenes, a framed chip with a short heart row and a collectible counter that only ever rises across the film (in the source it never changed on a visible event; stepping it at authored concept milestones is an optional production choice, never a meaningless count), plus a thin runtime progress bar along one frame edge that grows with elapsed time; (2) chapter breaks as a quest-map card: numbered level nodes joined by a dotted path whose cleared segments take the completion colour while uncleared ones stay muted, held under a dark STAGE N title plate; (3) a cumulative skill-inventory recap: a header and a row of framed slots that fill one at a time as each concept is named, with unfinished slots left visibly empty; (4) pixel dialogue plates: captions sit at bottom centre in a solid dark plate with a stepped pixel border and small accent end caps, sized for the finished line, with keywords in the highlight colour; (5) an original pixel guide character who introduces topics, reacts to results and closes; (6) two working surfaces chosen by content, a dark charcoal-navy surface with a faint pixel grid for code, terminals and mechanisms and a warm cream paper surface with sparse specks for metaphors, maps and the guide, framed by thin corner brackets. Mechanism diagrams are built from whole-pixel blocks (cells, tokens, slots, tables, cards, icons) on a deliberate logical grid; each item keeps one identity colour through a scene, a success colour marks completion and a warning colour with an X mark marks failure. Optional motifs, only where the story needs them: an RPG status panel with a level number and segmented gauge as a premise or recap, a warm sunset bookend, map props such as pixel trees and a castle, treasure or question blocks, a short diamond-lattice pixel wipe between scenes, typed terminal or code windows. Render on a low logical resolution (for example a 4 px grid at 1280 × 720) with integer coordinates, hard edges, no gradients and a limited palette; HUD numbers, titles and labels use bitmap or pixel-style lettering and captions stay crisp and readable. Motion is stepped and purposeful: inventory slots unlock in one step on their narration cue, map cards arrive with cleared segments already drawn, and any authored counter step lands with the concept it marks, diagrams build nodes before connectors, captions type into pre-sized plates, scene changes are hard cuts or a brief pixel wipe, and held states give reading time. Topic, layout, chapter count and colours adapt to each production. Never copy an existing game's sprites, HUD, mascot or map, or any source channel branding, and never show HUD values that do not reflect the story's structure.
styles.note: Authored by Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5) on 2026-10-24 from Claude Opus 5.5's frame analysis of a user-supplied pixel-art technical explainer (contact sheets of 35 overview timestamps plus six 3 fps dense windows; no audio, no transcription). Only reusable structural, visual and motion rules are recorded: the source topic, mascot, artwork, captions, title and channel marks are content, are not reproduced and must not be imitated. Colour values are authored defaults, not measured source hex. Distinct from Pixel Art (style-057), which covers pixel rendering only, and from Cassette Futurism (style-137) and Futuristic UI (FUI) / HUD Design (style-112), whose HUDs carry no game-progression meaning; Scientific Visualization / Data Storytelling (style-097) supplies explanation discipline but no visual identity. Review record: assets/catalog/reviews/pixel-quest-explainer.json.

tech.implementation: Separate four layers. (1) Progression model: before drawing, list the concepts and chapters in story order and derive every progress value from that list: the collectible counter only rises and, as an authored choice rather than a source observation, may equal the number of concepts resolved so far, quest-map nodes are cleared for finished chapters, inventory slots unlock in concept order and stay filled, and the runtime bar is elapsed time over total duration. When an authored value changes, change it only at the moment its concept resolves on screen or in narration; a counter that simply holds through a scene is equally faithful to the source; never animate HUD numbers decoratively. (2) Pixel drawing (SVG rects/paths with shape-rendering crispEdges, or Canvas 2D with imageSmoothingEnabled false at an integer scale): choose one logical grid, snap every position and size to it, build sprites and icons from string or index maps with a limited palette, and draw original guide, map props and item icons. HUD numbers, stage titles and labels use a bitmap glyph table or a locally available monospace face declared with @font-face local() names; never download fonts. Grid lines, specks and brackets stay outside letterforms; text sits on solid plates. (3) HUD and captions (persistent top layer): heart row, collectible counter, runtime bar and corner brackets keep fixed positions; the dialogue plate is sized for the finished line before characters type in with Terminal Typing (motion-022), with keyword spans in the highlight colour and a readable settled hold. (4) Motion (GSAP paused timeline driving one pure time-state function): diagrams and counters build with Data Build (motion-030), schedulers or fixed capacity pools may use Step-Tick Slot Refill (motion-049), title letters or the guide may land with Elastic Arrival (motion-027) in whole-pixel steps, and chapter changes are hard cuts or a short seeded pixel wipe. Arrowheads stay hidden until their shafts arrive. Keep stepped motion on whole pixels, limit flashes to brief single events, mark invented numbers illustrative, and verify forward, backward and direct seeks plus rendered frames at delivery size.
alternatives: Canvas 2D at a fixed logical resolution with integer upscaling instead of SVG rectangles
Aseprite sprite sheets for a supplied or purpose-drawn guide character and item icons
Remotion for a verified export limitation
tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
framework_selection.scope: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.

tech.library_selection: Prefer SVG or Canvas 2D on one logical pixel grid for scenes, sprites, HUD and diagrams, HTML/CSS for layout and caption text, and GSAP for one paused timeline driving a pure time-state function. Aseprite is optional for authored sprite sheets. Do not add 3D engines, physics or shader stacks; pixel wipes are seeded geometry.

motion_guidance.application: Progress elements never move decoratively: inventory unlocks land on narration cues and any authored counter step lands with a resolved concept; diagrams build nodes before connectors; captions type into pre-sized dialogue plates; chapter changes are hard cuts or a short pixel wipe to a held quest-map card; the guide reacts with small stepped hops.
motion_guidance.cadence_guidance: Brisk, game-like rhythm: stepped whole-pixel moves and discrete counter changes, short slides only for travelling tokens, and a settled hold after every caption, stage card and result. Never pulse HUD elements continuously or flash more than briefly.
motion_guidance.implementation: Evaluate every layer from absolute composition time through one pure time-state function derived from the ordered concept list; snap positions to the logical grid; seed any specks, trees or wipe order; keep one owner per property and verify forward, backward and direct seeks.

style_renderer.selection_basis: Use visual_cues and tech.implementation for styles, or the selected style and this pattern implementation for motion recipes. Select by visual fidelity and medium, not pipeline availability.

motion_engine.selection_basis: Use the authored action, style cadence, trajectory, material behavior, and simulation requirements. Select one owner for each animated property.

values.style_application: Assemble the pixel scenes, persistent HUD and captions and export them; keep the time-state renderer and the logical pixel grid rather than framework defaults.

Whole-pixel scenes, sprites, map props, item icons, HUD chip, runtime bar, corner brackets and dialogue plates as rects or run-length paths with crisp edges; bitmap glyph paths for HUD numbers and titles.
Composition layout and optional real-text captions from local monospace faces, sized into the dialogue plate with keyword spans; no downloaded fonts.
Fixed logical-resolution drawing with imageSmoothingEnabled false and integer upscaling for dense sprite or cell scenes, evaluated from composition time.
One paused, seekable timeline advances a composition clock; a pure time-state function sets counters, map and inventory states, caption typing, arrows, wipes and guide poses.
Verify cream and highlight text on the dark plate, ink on cream paper and labels on lane or slot fills; keep the limited palette discrete.
Optional: author an original guide character and item icons as indexed sprite sheets, then place them on the same logical grid.
Conditional composition/export fallback only for a verified HyperFrames limitation; keep the same pixel grid, HUD and time-state function.

styles.executable_prompt_template:
Create an original Pixel RPG Quest Explainer video about {{subject}} for {{audience_and_objective}}, using {{assets_and_exact_copy}}. Duration {{duration_seconds}}, aspect ratio {{aspect_ratio}}, resolution {{resolution}}, frame rate {{frame_rate}}. Honor {{audio_or_rhythm_requirements}}. Save to {{output_directory}}. Use {{render_pipeline}} for composition/export; the project renderer setting remains binding. Take the topic, concepts, chapters and copy from the project; when a guide character is needed and none is given, design an original one and record its sprite sheet. Write structured STORYBOARD.json listing the concepts and chapters in order, the HUD values each scene shows, the scenes with their surface (dark grid or cream paper), any chosen optional motifs, exact copy and assets.

Read the selected palette and tool guidance. Validate the storyboard schema, that every authored counter, map and inventory change matches a resolved concept, whole-pixel placement, readable caption holds, arrowhead timing, flash rate, forward/backward/direct seeks and rendered frames; preserve exact copy and word spacing.

palette.direction: Two working surfaces, a dark charcoal-navy grid and a warm cream paper, with a limited set of game accents whose roles stay fixed: a highlight for keywords and cleared progress, a collectible colour, a heart colour, a success colour and item identity colours. These tokens are optional examples.
constraints: These hex values are authored suggestions, not measured source colours. Task-provided exact colours and approved palettes override them while keeping the accent roles fixed.

Keep one role per accent across the film: highlight for keywords and cleared progress, collectible colour for counters, heart colour for lives or warnings, success colour for completion and the runtime bar, and one identity colour per item within a scene.
Use discrete flat fills on the logical pixel grid; no gradients, anti-aliased glows or blurred shadows.
On cream paper, text uses the dark plate ink; the highlight orange and muted grey are for paths, borders and decoration there, not for text.
Keep grid lines, specks and corner brackets out of letterforms; captions and labels sit on solid plates.
Flashes for unlocks or completion are single brief events, never more than about three per second.

gradient.instruction: No gradients. Depth comes from stepped pixel shading with existing tokens.

suggested_text_pairs.use: Dialogue plate captions, HUD labels and stage titles.
Keyword spans and stage numbers on the dark plate.
Collectible counter digits in the HUD chip.
Diagram labels directly on the dark grid surface.
Labels and node numbers on cream paper.
Success labels and the runtime bar on the dark surface.
Dark labels on teal item fills.
Path and border colour on cream paper only; not for text.

contrast_checks.limitation: Two-color checks only. Not a guarantee of complete accessibility or readability over images, textures, glass, video, outlines or animated lighting. Recheck every actual foreground/background pairing in representative frames.

palette.composition_guidance: Reserve fixed HUD zones (top edge bar, a top-corner chip, bottom-centre dialogue plate, corner brackets) and keep diagrams inside the remaining safe area. Give each scene one focal mechanism or card; place the guide beside, never over, diagrams and text. Adapt zones to the aspect ratio.
palette.agent_instruction: Read visual_cues, tech.implementation and palette.constraints as the complete style specification. Resolve colours in this order: task-provided exact palette, approved brand or source palette, then these optional tokens, keeping accent roles fixed. Use chroma-js for validation and contrast, and inspect composited frames at delivery size.

audio_direction.prompt: Optional ideas, governed by the project's audio settings: a light chiptune or lo-fi bed under clear narration, short soft UI blips for counter or slot unlocks, and silence during dense reading. Do not invent narration or music when audio is disabled, and never sound every caption character.
suggestion_dimensions: Whether background music is useful, and its suggested mood, texture, energy, tempo range, and progression.
Whether voiceover helps explain the topic, and its suggested language, tone, pace, and placement.
Whether sung vocals support the topic or distract from narration and essential text.
Whether sound effects, ambience, or silence clarify key actions, transitions, and reading holds.
How audio changes across scenes, supports motion cadence, and leaves space for speech and comprehension.
audio_direction.selection_guidance: Treat these as task-specific suggestions, not requirements to include every audio layer. Honor explicit user audio choices and supplied assets. When inputs are absent, propose a coherent direction and state assumptions; do not silently default to instrumental music or invent available audio assets.
audio_direction.integration_guidance: Select or create authorized audio assets separately from visual construction and motion design. Use render_pipeline to assemble, synchronize, mix, and export audio with picture. Keep speech intelligible, avoid clipping and competing vocals, and inspect the delivered audio and picture together.

motion_references.selection_policy: Optional candidates are screened for natural style compatibility. Before selection, inspect the actual scene illustration, assets, geometry and narrative beat. Keep only references whose defining action is supported by that scene. Choosing no reference is valid. Do not infer motion from a similar label; do not replace the existing style motion direction.

candidates.usage_guidance: Mechanism diagrams, memory or token grids, tables, metric cards and the HUD counter, map and inventory states build from one ordered concept list: nodes and slots before connectors, and every counter or slot change at the moment its concept resolves.
Dialogue-plate captions type into a plate already sized for the finished line, and terminal or code windows type commands with a block cursor; hold the completed line before the next caption.

Scheduler or fixed-capacity explanations: fixed slot lanes on a STEP counter gain one cell per tick, a finished lane clears for one step while its request icon exits right, and a new request takes that lane on the following tick.
Opening title letters or the guide drop onto a baseline one after another in whole-pixel steps; keep any compression to a single stepped pose and settle into a readable hold.

motion_references.agent_instruction: Read each complete motion definition before use. The progression grammar stays primary; use a reference only where the scene contains that action. Selecting none is valid.

suggested_combinations.selection_guidance: Pixel RPG Quest Explainer is complete on its own. Add a supporting style only for stricter sprite rendering or a dense data scene, keeping the persistent HUD, quest-map chapters and inventory recap dominant.

supporting_styles.role: Sprite, tile and palette-cycling discipline for pixel scenes

suggestions.rationale: Pixel Art adds strict sprite construction and palette cycling while the quest grammar supplies the narrative structure.
suggestions.best_for: Explainers with many sprite scenes, animated props or palette-cycled lights.
suggestions.video_application: Draw sprites on one logical grid with integer scaling; keep HUD and dialogue plates in the quest style.
suggestions.html_application: A fixed-resolution canvas scaled by integer factors with the HUD as crisp overlay text; reduced motion holds key poses.
consistency_rules: One logical grid for sprites, HUD and diagrams.
Palette cycling stays discrete.
avoid: HUD values unrelated to the story.

supporting_styles.role: Step-by-step diagram discipline for dense technical scenes

suggestions.rationale: Data storytelling keeps each mechanism scene to one idea with honest labels while the quest grammar tracks progress.
suggestions.best_for: Technical explainers with tables, memory maps, pipelines or metrics.
suggestions.video_application: One annotated pixel diagram per beat; unlock the matching inventory slot when its idea resolves.
suggestions.html_application: Scroll steps reveal one diagram per step with the HUD counter tied to completed steps and a static fallback.
consistency_rules: Explain one idea at a time.
Mark invented values as illustrative.

library_options.name: Three.js
library_options.purpose: Build 3D scenes, cameras, geometry, materials, lighting, and shader effects.
library_options.integration_guidance: Derive scene state from composition time and render explicitly. Do not run an independent animation loop during video export.

library_options.name: PixiJS
library_options.purpose: Render layered sprites, vector graphics, masks, and particle-like 2D compositions.
library_options.integration_guidance: Initialize the renderer and preload assets. Disable autonomous ticker playback for export; derive transforms and effects from composition time before rendering.

library_options.name: GSAP
library_options.purpose: Coordinate seekable animation of DOM, SVG, and scene properties.
library_options.integration_guidance: Use the existing HyperFrames timeline contract. Animate visual layers without taking over framework-owned clip visibility or media playback.

library_options.name: Motion
library_options.runtime: browser; motion/react for mounted React components
library_options.purpose: Provide optional DOM and SVG keyframes, spring-like transitions, sequences, and staggered reveals.
library_options.integration_guidance: Use the JavaScript entry point for HTML compositions. Motion is an optional layer, not a drop-in replacement for the HyperFrames GSAP timeline contract. Explicitly synchronize and verify seeking; use GSAP when that integration is not established. Use motion/react only within a React component runtime.

library_options.name: tldraw
library_options.runtime: mounted React editor in browser; exported assets for video composition
library_options.purpose: Author diagrams, annotations, whiteboard layouts, and editable card or node artwork.
library_options.integration_guidance: Use the editor to prepare assets or scene data, then animate exported layers in the selected video framework. It is not a video renderer, 3D engine, or automatic timeline adapter. Verify export APIs against the installed SDK version.

library_options.name: chroma.js
library_options.purpose: Optionally validate colors, derive controlled palette variants, interpolate colors, and check foreground/background contrast.
library_options.integration_guidance: Start with task-provided colors and the style visual_cues. Keep a shared, deterministic palette and named color tokens. Generate gradients or interpolate colors only when the style permits them; keep limited-palette, monochrome, pixel, and print treatments discrete where required. Evaluate animated color from shared composition time. Check contrast against the actual composited background; a two-color ratio alone does not verify text over transparency, gradients, textures, or video. Pass output through the selected renderer's color API and preserve its color-space handling. Native CSS/SVG colors remain sufficient when no color processing is needed.

library_options.name: Rough.js
library_options.runtime: browser Canvas or SVG; generator geometry can also be prepared in Node.js
library_options.purpose: Optionally generate hand-drawn-like geometric contours and patterned or solid fills for styles that explicitly support sketch-like artwork.
library_options.import_guidance: Use roughjs/bundled/rough.esm.js for browser ESM, roughjs/bundled/rough.cjs.js for Node.js CommonJS, or roughjs/bundled/rough.js for a browser script. Keep DOM, SVG and Canvas operations in the browser; Node.js may prepare generator drawables or path data without DOM access.
library_options.integration_guidance: Assign each object a stable nonzero integer seed in the documented range and cache generated paths or drawables. Drive transforms, masks, reveals and pose selection from shared seekable composition time using the selected animation owner. Fixed geometry should not be randomly regenerated each frame. For deliberate line boil, prepare and inspect a small set of fixed-seed contour variants and select them deterministically by exposure time. Use approved palette tokens directly for stroke and fill. Rough.js does not provide animation, handwriting, pressure-sensitive brush simulation, paper texture or character poses. Hachure and pattern fills do not establish authentic pencil, ink-wash, halftone or print materials. Animate stroke and fill reveals separately when necessary; generated path order is not an authored drawing sequence.
library_options.selection_guidance: Use only where the style and brief call for sketch-like contours, hachure or doodles. Do not apply roughness to precise grids, clean vectors, product UI, pixel clusters, photorealistic materials or existing assets unless that specific treatment is authorized.

library_options.name: Extended Position-Based Dynamics (XPBD)
library_options.runtime: Depends on the selected solver implementation: JavaScript, WebAssembly, native offline code or a supported GPU backend
library_options.purpose: Optionally simulate compliant constrained motion for cloth, elastic deformable bodies and suitable physical interactions. XPBD is an algorithm, not a visual style, renderer, animation framework or package name.
library_options.implementation_selection: Prefer an existing maintained solver that explicitly supports XPBD and the required constraint and collision models. Verify its actual API, licensing, runtime and determinism before use. Do not assume that a generic physics package implements XPBD, or invent a universal XPBD API. The reference examples are educational starting points, not a production dependency recommendation.
constraint_options: Distance or stretch constraints for connections and cloth structure
Bending constraints for cloth or deliberately modeled paper folds
Volume or constitutive strain constraints for the chosen elastic-body model
Attachment or prescribed-position constraints for anchors and authored controls
Contact and self-collision handling appropriate to the model and solver
library_options.parameter_guidance: Specify units, masses, rest geometry, compliance, damping formulation, fixed simulation step, substep count, solver iterations and collision parameters. XPBD uses compliance scaled by the square of the solve time step and accumulated constraint multipliers within the solve. Follow the selected implementation for multiplier initialization and damping. Improved stiffness control does not remove finite-iteration error or guarantee accuracy, stability, collision robustness or cross-backend reproducibility.
library_options.integration_guidance: Keep simulation and rendering separate. Advance from a known initial state with fixed simulation steps and a defined deterministic constraint order where supported. For video, bake geometry or positions and any needed normals, or use checkpoints with deterministic replay. Resolve each composition timestamp from the cache or replay; never advance mutable physics once per render callback or use wall-clock delta. Test repeated, out-of-order and backward frame requests for identical states. Let Three.js render the evaluated state, and GSAP or the selected timeline control authored scene events without competing with solver-owned positions. Use HyperFrames as primary composition framework and Remotion only under its existing fallback condition. Preserve approved materials and palette tokens.
library_options.limitations: Basic elastic-body XPBD does not automatically provide fluid merging, splitting, viscosity, plasticity, tearing, rigid-body contact or origami crease behavior. Such effects require appropriate additional formulations, topology handling and validation. Use authored motion instead when physical simulation adds no value.

library_options.name: PhotoSwipe
library_options.runtime: browser; initialize only after the gallery DOM is mounted
library_options.purpose: Optional image-gallery dialog with swipe navigation, zoom, pan and thumbnail opening or closing transitions for interactive web delivery.
library_options.import_guidance: Use PhotoSwipeLightbox from 'photoswipe/lightbox', load 'photoswipe/style.css', and set pswpModule to () => import('photoswipe'). Check exports and API signatures against the installed version.
library_options.integration_guidance: Use for interactive image viewing only when the task includes a web gallery or lightbox. Define accurate intrinsic image dimensions and responsive sources. Retain direct image links as a fallback, meaningful image alternatives, usable keyboard navigation, focus return and reduced-motion behavior. Initialize after mounting and destroy on cleanup; access the core instance only after opening. Preserve original image colors and established palette tokens when styling controls. PhotoSwipe owns its dialog gestures and transitions; do not attach another animation owner to those properties. Captions require a deliberate custom UI or suitable plugin rather than assuming a built-in caption feature.
library_options.video_guidance: PhotoSwipe is not a video renderer or a composition-time animation engine. For rendered video, recreate the chosen thumbnail expansion, swipe, zoom, pan and reading holds as authored DOM/SVG/Canvas transforms driven by GSAP and the selected framework clock. Do not depend on live touch input, dynamic dialog state or asynchronous lightbox transitions for exported frames. Preserve HyperFrames as primary and Remotion as the existing conditional fallback.
library_options.selection_guidance: Designed primarily as an image lightbox dialog, not a general inline carousel. Use native scroll snapping or a suitable carousel library for inline cards, mixed interactive card content or persistent neighboring cards. PhotoSwipe does not generate the artwork or determine its visual style.

library_options.name: Cropper.js
library_options.runtime: browser; initialize after the image and editing container are mounted
library_options.purpose: Optionally author image crop regions and export prepared raster assets for layouts or video compositions. This is an asset-preparation or interactive editing tool, not a style generator or video animation engine.
library_options.api_version_guidance: The documented 2.x API uses Cropper custom elements and CropperSelection.$toCanvas(). Verify the installed version before implementation; do not mix it with 1.x methods such as getCroppedCanvas().
library_options.import_guidance: Import Cropper from 'cropperjs' and follow the installed 2.x documentation for its custom elements. Keep DOM, image loading, selection controls and Canvas export in the browser; initialize client-side rather than during server rendering.
library_options.integration_guidance: Await image readiness, select the intended aspect ratio and framing, and export the selection through the documented asynchronous Canvas API at appropriate output dimensions. Preserve the original asset and store the crop recipe separately: source identity, intrinsic dimensions, selection rectangle, image transform, editor coordinate system, output dimensions and any required overscan. Selection coordinates are in the editor layout, not automatically original-image pixel coordinates; account for transforms and coordinate mapping before reproducing a crop elsewhere. Confirm image permissions and cross-origin Canvas export availability before relying on export. Avoid unnecessary upscaling, repeated lossy encoding and destructive replacement of the source.
library_options.color_guidance: Crop and frame only. Preserve the approved palette and original image treatment; do not apply filters, tinting, grading or automatic palette changes. Resampling, Canvas color conversion and encoding can affect pixel values, so do not promise byte-identical colors after export. Inspect representative output colors and prefer non-destructive source-plus-crop rendering when exact source preservation is required.
library_options.video_guidance: Finish crop authoring before rendering. Load the exported asset or a reproducible source-plus-crop recipe into the composition, then animate framing, masks and pan or zoom with GSAP or the selected framework timeline. Do not drive exported frames from live crop handles or mutable editor state. Keep HyperFrames primary and Remotion under its existing fallback condition.
library_options.selection_guidance: Use when interactive crop authoring is useful. Native CSS object-fit/object-position, SVG clipping or Canvas source rectangles are sufficient for simple predetermined framing. Cropping does not remove backgrounds, create subject cutouts, separate parallax layers or fill missing artwork. Keep important faces, labels, product features and motion margins inside the intended frame.

library_options.name: mo.js
library_options.runtime: browser DOM and SVG; initialize after target elements are mounted
library_options.purpose: Optionally generate and animate geometric shapes, radial bursts, swirl accents and existing HTML elements for expressive 2D motion graphics.
library_options.import_guidance: Import mojs from '@mojs/core' using a compatible bundler or the documented browser build. Verify exports and signatures against the installed version. Keep DOM-dependent construction out of server-side rendering.
library_options.integration_guidance: Use mo.js as an optional effects layer, not a video renderer or replacement for the HyperFrames timeline registration contract. Build effects once, pause independent playback, and evaluate normalized setProgress values from shared seekable composition time. Account explicitly for local start, delay, duration, repeats, yoyo and end visibility using the installed API. Preserve the registered GSAP timeline as the HyperFrames clock and synchronize mo.js through the selected framework update mechanism; verify updates on direct seeks rather than relying only on playback callbacks. For Remotion, use its mounted browser lifecycle and frame-derived time. Assign each animated property one owner; use nested wrappers if GSAP controls scene placement while mo.js controls an inner effect.
library_options.determinism_guidance: Resolve random particle properties into explicit reproducible values before building the effect. Do not regenerate random values with generate() during export or depend on live click triggers. Keep effect state derivable from requested time. Verify initial visibility, direct, repeated, backward and out-of-order seeks against sequential playback, including delays and end holds. If the chosen mo.js effect cannot be reliably evaluated this way, recreate it with the existing GSAP/SVG route rather than introducing a separate playback clock.
library_options.color_guidance: Use the resolved palette tokens directly for stroke and fill. Keep limited and monochrome palettes discrete. Animate color interpolation only when the style and palette permit it; do not adopt example-code colors or add arbitrary particle hues. Preserve typography, approved assets and material treatment.
library_options.selection_guidance: Choose mo.js when its shape, burst or swirl modules simplify a meaningful effect. Existing GSAP or native SVG can remain sufficient. Supported shape-property animation does not establish arbitrary path morphing, fluid physics, handwriting, character rigging, frame-by-frame drawing or automatic music analysis.

library_options.name: Delaunator
library_options.runtime: JavaScript in browser or Node.js; DOM-independent geometry computation
library_options.purpose: Optionally compute Delaunay triangle connectivity, neighboring half-edges and the convex hull of 2D points for mesh-based artwork or spatial visualization. Rendering and motion are supplied separately.
library_options.import_guidance: Import Delaunator from 'delaunator' as an ES module. Supply flat coordinates [x0, y0, x1, y1, ...] to the constructor, preferably a suitable typed array, or point pairs to Delaunator.from(). Verify the installed version and data structures before implementation.
library_options.integration_guidance: Read triangle vertex indices in groups of three and use the original point coordinates to build SVG polygons, Canvas paths, PixiJS geometry or an appropriate Three.js BufferGeometry. Keep DOM and renderer operations in the browser; Node.js can prepare or cache geometry. Assign palette colors through stable point or face identities, not transient triangle-array positions when retriangulating. Preserve the selected renderer coordinate system, winding, normals and material handling.
library_options.animation_guidance: Derive point positions from shared seekable composition time, with deterministic initial coordinates and no unseeded randomness. For stable deformation, triangulate once and keep indices fixed, while checking for inverted or degenerate faces. For deliberate dynamic triangulation, update coordinates and recompute at the evaluated time, accepting that edges and face identities may switch. Design or cache those changes; do not assume update() preserves connectivity. Verify repeated, backward and out-of-order seeks, boundaries, color continuity and triangle quality. Keep HyperFrames primary and Remotion under its existing fallback condition.
library_options.input_guidance: Use finite 2D coordinates and inspect duplicate, collinear or nearly coincident inputs. Delaunator.from() skips duplicate points; retain an explicit mapping when input identity matters. Do not assume every input creates a useful triangle. Geographic inputs need a suitable projection or a spherical triangulation tool rather than treating longitude and latitude as a universally valid planar distance system.
library_options.limitations: This is unconstrained 2D point triangulation, not arbitrary 3D surface meshing, polygon-with-holes triangulation, subject segmentation, a renderer or a physics solver. The triangulation covers the convex hull and may bridge concave boundaries or holes. Use an appropriate boundary-aware triangulator, clipping strategy or separate domains when needed. For Voronoi cells, search or higher-level traversal, consider the documented d3-delaunay wrapper. Scientific interpolation and semantic network interpretation are separate tasks.
library_options.color_guidance: Use the approved palette and stable color-role mappings. Triangulation does not authorize recoloring source images, adding random face colors or interpolating discrete scientific categories. Preserve material appearance and limited-color constraints.

library_options.name: p5.js
library_options.purpose: Optionally create procedural drawings, generative patterns and animated Canvas or WebGL visual layers.
library_options.integration_guidance: Use browser-mounted instance mode to isolate sketches and avoid global callbacks. Pin a compatible p5 version and check its asset-loading and redraw completion APIs. Disable autonomous playback with noLoop(). Set an explicit requested composition time before each redraw and wait for drawing and asset readiness before capture. Derive state from that time, not millis(), deltaTime, frameCount or draw-call count. Seed noise and random generation, precompute stable per-object parameters, and reset or replay stateful simulations deterministically. Seeding once alone does not guarantee out-of-order frame equivalence. Clear and rebuild frames or use verified caches for accumulated trails. Set pixel density and backing resolution deliberately. Remove the instance and release owned resources on teardown.
library_options.constraints: p5.js supplies a visual layer, not the video framework, automatic physics, genuine hand-drawn poses or guaranteed export synchronization. Retain HyperFrames as primary and Remotion as conditional fallback. Keep existing palette tokens, approved colors, motion guidance and exposure cadence. Prefer existing suitable Canvas, SVG, PixiJS or Three.js code over an unnecessary additional renderer. Sound-reactive work needs a separate verified audio-analysis route and cached time-indexed analysis; do not assume sound APIs belong to core p5.
library_options.verification: Compare repeated, backward and out-of-order redraws with sequential frames. Inspect decoded video for aliasing, temporal flicker, output resolution, palette fidelity and media synchronization.

library_options.name: Dragula
library_options.purpose: Reorder DOM items or move/copy them between configured containers in interactive delivery or an accompanying editor.
library_options.integration_guidance: Include the required Dragula CSS. Use explicit containers, drag handles and acceptance rules. Persist stable item IDs and final ordering in application state on drop, and reconcile DOM mutations with the framework without competing ownership. Initialize after mount and destroy on teardown. Provide keyboard or button-based alternatives and meaningful status announcements; pointer/touch support alone does not establish keyboard accessibility. Use an existing suitable animation dependency for optional settling, with one owner per property.
library_options.constraints: Dragula manages DOM drag/drop interaction and drop feedback, not general animation, physics, 3D picking or freeform canvas positioning. Verify package/version compatibility and maintenance suitability before installation. For video, author cursor paths, lifted cards, placeholders, reordering and settling from seekable composition time instead of running live Dragula input. Preserve HyperFrames as primary, Remotion as conditional fallback, approved palettes and shared_motion_guidance.
library_options.verification: For interactive delivery, verify reorder, container transfer, allowed/rejected drops, cancellation, touch, state persistence, keyboard alternatives and cleanup. For video, compare repeated and out-of-order seeking and inspect decoded motion.

library_options.name: Cytoscape.js
library_options.runtime: browser for interactive rendering; Node.js or browser for headless graph analysis
library_options.purpose: Model node-edge relationships, compute graph layouts and analysis, and optionally render interactive networks or supply diagram geometry to another renderer.

suggested_layouts.name: preset
suggested_layouts.application: Reuse cached or explicitly authored node positions; preferred export route.

suggested_layouts.name: breadthfirst
suggested_layouts.application: Show appropriate hierarchical or traversal structure; configure roots and direction explicitly.

suggested_layouts.name: grid / circle / concentric
suggested_layouts.application: Use orderly schematic arrangements when they support the explanation.

suggested_layouts.name: cose
suggested_layouts.application: Optionally prepare a force-directed arrangement; await completion and cache positions, not a live export simulation.

suggested_algorithms.name: Breadth-first or depth-first traversal
suggested_algorithms.application: Explain reachability and visit order with explicit roots and directedness.

suggested_algorithms.name: Dijkstra shortest paths
suggested_algorithms.application: Explain routes or dependencies only with meaningful positive edge costs and verified connectivity; handle unreachable nodes explicitly.

suggested_algorithms.name: Degree or betweenness centrality
suggested_algorithms.application: Explain connection counts or bridging roles using documented metric options; centrality does not by itself establish importance or causation.

library_options.integration_guidance: Observe and validate graph input before processing: stable unique node/edge IDs, existing source/target IDs, directedness, weights and optional compound parents. Choose analysis and layout to fit the question. Register completion handling before running asynchronous layouts; a layoutstop event can also indicate cancellation, so confirm the intended layout completed. Cache validated node positions and use preset with explicit viewport settings for export. Precompute paths and metrics. Evaluate positions, visibility, emphasis, pan and zoom from shared composition time; do not rerun stochastic layouts or autonomous Cytoscape animations for each frame. Either use the browser renderer with verified frame readiness or pass graph data and cached geometry to SVG/Canvas/PixiJS for custom style treatment. Load fonts and assets first, initialize browser containers after mount, and dispose graph instances and listeners on teardown.
library_options.constraints: Cytoscape.js is a graph library, not a general chart library, knowledge extractor, 3D engine or video framework. Core PNG/JPG export requires a rendered instance, not a headless one; do not assume SVG export is built in. Extensions such as additional layouts require separate installation and compatibility checks. Headless layouts may need explicit bounds or styling for dimension-sensitive placement. Preserve approved palette tokens and label semantics rather than applying default graph colors. Keep HyperFrames primary and Remotion conditional fallback; shared_motion_guidance governs animated diagram changes. Provide keyboard-accessible controls and a text/table representation where interactive graph meaning would otherwise be inaccessible.
library_options.verification: Check topology, source/target direction, weights, computed paths and metric interpretation against known input examples. Inspect label overlap, arrows, reading size, graph bounds and palette fidelity. Compare repeated and out-of-order frame requests with sequential video playback; verify renderer readiness and decoded export.

library_options.name: Anime.js
library_options.runtime: browser for DOM/SVG; numeric object animation where supported by the selected runtime
library_options.purpose: Optionally animate CSS, DOM attributes, SVG geometry and numeric objects with timelines, easing, staggered sequences, line drawing and motion paths.
library_options.integration_guidance: Use documented Anime.js v4 imports and verify the installed version; do not mix legacy anime()/anime.timeline() examples with v4 APIs. Build paused animations with explicit fixed initial and target values. Map shared composition time to the configured Anime.js time unit, which is milliseconds by default. Seek the optional child animation from the framework-controlled time adapter and verify updates reach the renderer before capture. Preserve the registered HyperFrames GSAP master timeline; an Anime.js timeline is not a drop-in substitute for that contract. Prefer GSAP when a verified adapter is unavailable. Use one animation owner per property; do not have GSAP, Motion and Anime.js write the same transform. Load fonts and geometry before constructing animations, precompute random parameters, and perform lifecycle cleanup using the documented API for the installed version.
library_options.constraints: Anime.js does not generate illustration assets, solve physical simulations or render video itself. SVG morphing, motion paths and line drawing apply to their documented supported geometry; do not treat them as general 3D topology operations. Springs and overshoot are optional authored choices, not automatic smoothness improvements. Live scroll or dragging belongs to interactive delivery; author equivalent time-driven actions for video. Avoid callback-dependent state changes that fail direct or backward seeking. Preserve palette tokens, shared_motion_guidance and intentional stepped cadence. HyperFrames remains primary and Remotion conditional fallback.
library_options.verification: Verify fixed initial states, exact final copy, geometry integrity, property ownership and time-unit conversion. Compare repeated, backward and out-of-order seeking with sequential playback, then inspect the decoded video for smoothness, readability, palette fidelity and loop continuity.

library_options.name: Paper.js
library_options.runtime: browser Canvas; Node.js geometry or asset preparation only with verified compatible DOM/Canvas dependencies for the required operation
library_options.purpose: Construct and manipulate vector paths, Bezier curves, groups, clipping geometry and boolean shapes; render on Canvas or prepare SVG assets.

suggested_methods.name: Bezier path construction and sampling
suggested_methods.application: Prepare curved contours and sample positions or tangents along path length for reveals and movement.

suggested_methods.name: Path boolean operations
suggested_methods.application: Combine or cut closed shapes; inspect geometry, holes and edge cases before rendering.

suggested_methods.name: Compatible path interpolation
suggested_methods.application: Morph prepared contours with matching geometry structure; correspondence remains an authoring responsibility.

suggested_methods.name: Optional path smoothing and simplification
suggested_methods.application: Apply only when appropriate; compare against the original contour because these operations alter geometry.

library_options.integration_guidance: Prefer ordinary JavaScript with an isolated PaperScope rather than installing constructors onto window or relying on PaperScript compilation. Initialize the scope on an owned Canvas after browser mount. Keep immutable rest geometry and evaluate transforms, segments and handles at requested composition time; do not repeatedly mutate the previous frame. Disable automatic view updates and autonomous onFrame playback for export, then call view.update() after applying each time state. Preload fonts and imported assets, verify SVG import completion and supported features, cache expensive boolean results, and remove temporary items and owned projects on teardown. Use existing GSAP or another verified adapter for shared time without competing property ownership. Set logical Canvas size and output pixel density explicitly.
library_options.constraints: Paper.js is a 2D vector geometry and rendering library, not a paper material generator, physical fluid solver, 3D engine or video framework. Path interpolation requires compatible segment structures; matching counts alone does not ensure meaningful correspondence. Boolean operations may create compound paths or change topology. SVG import/export requires fidelity checks for unsupported source features, font handling and raster content. Preserve approved palette tokens, source geometry, shared_motion_guidance and intentional exposure cadence; optional smoothing must not erase sketch character. HyperFrames remains primary and Remotion conditional fallback. Prefer existing native SVG, Canvas or another suitable dependency when Paper.js adds no needed geometry capability.
library_options.verification: Check contour fidelity, winding, holes, intersections, morph intermediate states, SVG round-trip appearance and output scale. Compare repeated, backward and out-of-order frame requests with sequential playback and inspect decoded video for palette fidelity, flicker and line quality.

library_options.name: Leaflet
library_options.runtime: browser; initialize after DOM mount in a container with explicit dimensions
library_options.purpose: Build interactive 2D geographic maps with tile layers, markers, geographic vector overlays and GeoJSON, or supply a verified map layer for a video scene.
suggested_apis: Map / map construction for installed version
TileLayer / tileLayer construction for installed version
GeoJSON / geoJSON construction for installed version
library_options.integration_guidance: Pin the installed Leaflet version and consult its matching documentation; do not mix namespace-based 1.x examples with 2.x module imports. Include required Leaflet CSS and marker assets, initialize after mount, size the container explicitly and invalidateSize after layout changes. Validate real geographic coordinates and projections: Leaflet LatLng uses latitude/longitude while GeoJSON coordinate arrays use longitude/latitude. Use approved tile or geographic data providers with appropriate attribution and authorized export usage. Select basemap artwork compatible with the existing palette rather than applying color filters to approved imagery. For video, preload or locally prepare authorized map assets, disable autonomous map animations, and evaluate viewport, marker positions, path progress and highlights from composition time. Wait for required layers and tiles to finish loading and handle errors before capture; prefer fixed map images or custom SVG/Canvas geography if arbitrary-time map seeking cannot be verified. Dispose the map and owned listeners after use.
library_options.constraints: Leaflet is a 2D map library, not a tile-data provider, geocoder, routing engine, GIS analysis suite, 3D globe or video renderer. Marker clustering, vector-tile handling and other advanced features may require separate verified plugins. A drawn path is not proof of a computed real-world route. Leaflet core does not provide a universal map-to-image/video export API; renderer choice, external images, CORS and provider terms affect capture. Do not bulk prefetch public tiles without provider authorization. Preserve attribution, approved palette tokens and exact geographic meaning. A live flyTo transition is not inherently seekable for video. Retain HyperFrames primary, Remotion conditional fallback and shared_motion_guidance; provide accessible text or tabular location context for interactive delivery.
library_options.verification: Check coordinates, projection, bounds, route semantics, legends and required attribution. Verify loaded tiles and images, missing-asset handling, marker alignment, labels and output dimensions. Compare repeated and out-of-order time requests with sequential playback and inspect the decoded video for stable map rendering and readable geographic context.

library_options.name: Chartist
library_options.purpose: Optionally build SVG bar, line, and pie charts when the scene communicates real data or clearly labeled illustrative data.
library_options.integration_guidance: Bundle Chartist and its required chart CSS locally. Initialize at fixed composition dimensions after fonts and layout are ready, then wait for the created event before capture. Style the generated SVG using the selected palette, typography, stroke weights, and contrast rules. Cache chart geometry and animate SVG transforms, masks, opacity, or stroke reveals from the shared paused, seekable composition timeline. Do not use autonomous SMIL animation, timers, or live resize-driven changes during export. update reconstructs the SVG DOM, so update only at deliberate data changes and rebind animation targets afterward; do not call it every frame. Keep axes, units, and labels truthful and legible; do not invent product metrics. Use native SVG when a chart library is unnecessary.

shared_motion_guidance.priority: Smooth, intentional movement is a default quality requirement for most styles. Preserve style-specific exposure cadence, meaningful sharp cuts and deliberate stepped motion.
principles: Design a clear trajectory and readable start, key-action and end states before choosing easing.
Use coherent acceleration, deceleration, anticipation and settling appropriate to the action and material; deliberate constant speed or a sharp cut can be appropriate.
Coordinate related objects, camera moves and transitions. Avoid accidental position jumps, velocity changes, clipping, overshoot and perpetual micro-motion.
Maintain text reading holds, visual hierarchy, contact relationships and apparent weight. Move only elements that contribute to the explanation.
Preserve stepped pose exposure, whole-pixel placement and intentional contour variation when required. Smooth motion quality does not require extra in-between drawings or interpolated pixels.
Match both position and velocity at continuous transitions and loop boundaries unless an intentional cut is part of the design.
Select easing, intensity and timing from the topic, style and action; no universal spring, bounce or floating treatment is required.

methods.name: Time-based interpolation
methods.role: Evaluate position, scale or other permitted properties from defined key states and normalized local composition time.
methods.guidance: Use linear interpolation for deliberately constant speed or an appropriate eased progress curve for acceleration and settling. Evaluate the requested time directly; do not repeatedly lerp from the previous rendered frame. Respect angle wrapping, appropriate quaternion interpolation for 3D orientation, whole-pixel constraints and approved color handling.

methods.name: Authored easing
methods.role: Shape entrances, transitions, camera moves and settling with an existing timeline library.
methods.guidance: Prefer existing GSAP or selected framework facilities. Choose easing per action and inspect continuity between segments. Avoid applying identical ease-in/ease-out to every element, easing away a required impact or introducing unrequested overshoot.

methods.name: Exponential smoothing
methods.role: Optional responsive following for interactive controls or deliberately modeled lag.
methods.guidance: For live interaction, a time-step-aware factor such as 1 - exp(-response_rate * delta_time) avoids a fixed per-render-frame response factor. It still depends on evolving state. For export, use an analytic trajectory where applicable or fixed-step simulation with caching and deterministic replay. A constant-target analytic solution does not cover arbitrary moving targets.

methods.name: Camera damping
methods.role: Optional easing of user-controlled orbit movement for interactive 3D scenes.
methods.guidance: Use the installed camera-control library according to its documented update and damping behavior. For video, disable live-input control and author or bake the camera trajectory; OrbitControls damping alone does not make arbitrary frame seeking deterministic.

shared_motion_guidance.render_contract: Use HyperFrames as primary and Remotion only under the existing fallback condition. Derive visual state from shared seekable composition time. Keep one owner per animated property. Use cached or reproducible evaluation for stateful physics and smoothing. Separate pose exposure rate from delivery frame rate. Preserve palettes, source assets and existing style/motion direction.
verification: Compare direct, repeated, backward and out-of-order time requests with sequential playback at representative states.
Inspect the decoded sequence for unintended stutter, velocity discontinuities, camera wobble, collisions, distracting overshoot and unreadable moving text.
Inspect exposure holds, pixel alignment, contour cadence and other deliberate stepped behavior separately from accidental jitter.
Check opening, key actions, transitions, settling, final holds and any loop seam; fix issues and render again.

recommended_stack.integration_guidance: Align video texture UVs to the screen, preload media and synchronize it with composition time. rendering_techniques.name: Scrambled Text Reveal
rendering_techniques.description: Reveal short titles through a controlled scrambled-character transition.

recommended_stack.name: Scrambled Text Reveal
recommended_stack.purpose: Reveal short titles through a controlled scrambled-character transition.
recommended_stack.integration_guidance: Register ScrambleTextPlugin explicitly and animate short text in a paused timeline. Preserve the exact final copy, allow a readable final hold, and test the plugin at repeated, backward and out-of-order times. If results are unstable, cache a seeded character sequence evaluated from composition time.
recommended_stack.constraints: This is GSAP ScrambleTextPlugin, not Motion.dev. Use only when the topic and typography support it; keep essential information readable and preserve accessible final text. Never rely on an independent running timeline during export.

production_policy.principle: Select visual and motion technologies from the style, action, assets, and required fidelity before choosing the composition and export pipeline. Pipeline availability must not determine or simplify the visual style or motion technique.
production_policy.style_renderer: Owns visual construction: drawing, geometry, materials, lighting, typography, masks, textures, and specialist asset generation. Use the style-specific recommended technologies and implementation guidance.
production_policy.motion_engine: Owns trajectories, transforms, easing, transitions, deformation, and simulation. Select engines or algorithms appropriate to the action, with one owner for each animated property.
production_policy.render_pipeline: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.
production_policy.integration: Visual and motion layers expose deterministic state at composition time, or supply baked assets or frame sequences. The pipeline supplies seekable time and composes their output. Timeline registration and frame hooks are integration adapters, not substitutes for style-specific rendering or motion.
production_policy.selection: Choose only needed stack entries. A technology may serve multiple roles, but document its actual responsibility. Optional authoring, interaction, color, and preprocessing tools are not mandatory renderers or motion engines.

combination_analysis.guidance: Optional model-analyzed creative recommendations. One primary style controls identity and palette; supporting styles have explicit subordinate roles. Select hybrids only when they improve the brief.
